| `--model` | `-m` | string | Select the model — `provider/modelId`, bare id, provider slug, or glob/substring |
| `--list-models` | — | string | Print the model catalog (optionally filtered by a substring) and exit |
| `--account` | — | string | Authenticate the run with a named stored credential account |
| `--thinking` | — | string | Set reasoning effort (`off`/`minimal`/`low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`) |

**How a selector resolves.** A selector runs through the conductor's `ModelMatcher`, a scored-candidate resolver over `ModelCatalog`. Each card surviving the hard capability gates is scored by strategy probes, strongest-first; highest scorer wins with deterministic tie-breaks.

| Strategy | Weight | Fires when the selector is… |
|----------|--------|-----------------------------|
| Explicit pin | 1000 | a structured `provider` + `modelId` query |
| Exact canonical | 900 | exactly `provider/modelId` |
| Exact model id | 800 | exactly a provider-scoped `modelId` |
| Provider-scoped | 600 | `provider/` or a bare provider slug |
| Glob | 400 | a glob (`*`, `?`, `[set]`) matching the id |
| Alias substring | 200 | a case-folded substring of the id or name |

Strategies do not stack — a card's score is the single best strategy that fires; tier gaps are wide enough that a weaker probe never out-ranks a stronger one. Ties break by a small bonus (tighter id-length match plus a `+3` nudge toward reasoning-capable cards), then by canonical id, so equal scores never depend on iteration order. Globs are anchored and case-folded; `/` matches literally (`anthropic/*` scopes to one provider, `*sonnet*` searches all). A bare provider slug matches the provider-scoped tier and falls back to that provider's leading card.

**Scoped and capability selectors.** `ModelCatalog.get(id)` resolves a bare model id when it is unambiguous across providers; qualify it (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`) when more than one provider offers the same bare id. The structured `MatchQuery` gates on capability: `reasoning=True` keeps only models advertising a reasoning budget, `supportsImageInput=True` keeps only models accepting image input. These are **hard gates** — a failing card is removed entirely, not down-ranked.

**Listing the catalog.** `--list-models` prints an aligned text table and exits without starting a session; it takes an optional substring (becomes the case-insensitive `search` field of a `CatalogFilter`). Boot short-circuits it before any stage runs and calls `print_model_catalog(filter=CatalogFilter(search=...))`. The printer re-derives rows from the conductor `ModelCatalog`, sorts by provider then model id, and lays out six columns:

```bash
pindus --list-models                 # the whole catalog
pindus --list-models claude          # only ids matching "claude" (substring)
pindus --list-models gpt             # only ids matching "gpt"
```

| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| Provider | Owning provider slug |
| Model | Provider-scoped model id |
| Context | Context-window size (`128K`, `1.0M`, or `-` when unknown) |
| Max Output | Maximum output tokens, same compact format |
| Thinking | `yes` when the model advertises a reasoning budget |
| Images | `yes` when the model accepts image input |

`CatalogFilter` carries more than the CLI substring exposes: programmatic callers can also narrow by `provider`, `thinking_only`, and `images_only`. An absent field matches everything; `search` is a plain case-insensitive substring test over `"provider/modelId"`. When a filter matches nothing the printer emits a single `No models match the given filter.` line. The catalog deliberately excludes the framework's `mock` echo provider, so `mock-default` never surfaces as a row or auto-selected default.

```python
from induscode.launch import print_model_catalog, CatalogFilter
print_model_catalog(
    filter=CatalogFilter(provider="anthropic", thinking_only=True, search="claude"),
)
```

**Default model precedence.** When `--model` is omitted, `resolve_model_id` in the boot session runner picks one in this order:

1. **Explicit `--model`** — an explicit, non-empty selector always wins.
2. **An authenticated provider's current model** — for each provider with stored credentials, the runner picks that provider's preferred current model. The preferred-default table, by bare id:
   - `anthropic`: `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `claude-haiku-4-5`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-sonnet-4-0`, `claude-opus-4-5`
   - `openai`: `gpt-5.1`, `gpt-4.1`, `gpt-4o`
   - If none of the preferred ids are in the catalog, the provider's newest catalog entry (last by scan order) is used.
3. **Catalog default** — otherwise `ModelMatcher.resolve(MatchQuery())` returns the leading surviving card, nudged toward a reasoning model.

This keeps an unauthenticated, no-flag launch from defaulting to a model the caller has no key for.

**Reasoning effort.** `--thinking` sets the reasoning-effort rung. The accepted vocabulary is an ordered superset of the framework's `ThinkingLevel`, adding an explicit `off`:

```
off  minimal  low  medium  high  xhigh
```

`off` disables extended reasoning entirely; the remaining rungs ascend in effort. The launch contract validates against `THINKING_EFFORTS` via `is_thinking_effort` before the run starts; callers handing a level to the framework drop `off`.

```bash
pindus -m claude-sonnet-4-5 --thinking high "design the migration"
pindus -m claude-sonnet-4-5 --thinking off  "just answer briefly"
```

**The catalog programmatically.** `ModelCatalog` builds a normalized, validated, de-duplicated view of the framework model list in its constructor (a view over the framework's `get_providers()` / `get_models()`); each card retains the full framework `Model` record so the conductor can bind without a second registry round-trip. The `--list-models` printer reads through the same catalog via a `CatalogModelSource` seam, so there is exactly one catalog path (picker, printer, resolver, session bind all see the same cards).

```python
from induscode.conductor import ModelCatalog
from induscode.conductor.matcher import ModelMatcher
from induscode.conductor.contract import MatchQuery

catalog = ModelCatalog()                 # eager build over the live framework registry
print(catalog.size, catalog.providers())
matcher = ModelMatcher(catalog)
ref = matcher.resolve("claude-sonnet-4-5")          # -> ModelCardRef | None
best = matcher.resolve(MatchQuery(provider="anthropic", reasoning=True))
field = matcher.resolve_all("gpt")                  # ranked "did you mean" list
```

Public API (exported from `induscode.launch` and `induscode.conductor`):

| Name | Kind | Source | Purpose |
|------|------|--------|---------|
| `print_model_catalog` | function | `launch/catalog.py` | Render the aligned model table over the conductor catalog |
| `CatalogFilter` | dataclass | `launch/contract.py` | `--list-models` filter: `provider`, `thinking_only`, `images_only`, `search` |
| `CatalogIo` / `default_catalog_io` | Protocol / function | `launch/catalog.py` | The line sink the table prints onto (stdout default; injectable) |
| `CatalogModelSource` / `catalog_source` | Protocol / function | `launch/catalog.py` | The seam the printer sources raw models from |
| `ModelCatalog` | class | `conductor/catalog.py` | Normalized view of the framework model list; `.all()`, `.by_provider()`, `.get()`, `.size` |
| `CatalogCard` | dataclass | `conductor/catalog.py` | One normalized catalog entry (id, provider, modelId, capabilities, retained framework `model`) |
| `ModelMatcher` | class | `conductor/matcher.py` | Scored-candidate resolver: `.resolve()`, `.resolve_card()`, `.resolve_all()` |
| `MatchQuery` | dataclass | `conductor/contract.py` | Structured selector: `pattern`, `provider`, `modelId`, `reasoning`, `supportsImageInput` |
| `THINKING_EFFORTS` / `is_thinking_effort` | const / function | `launch/contract.py` | The `--thinking` vocabulary and its validator |

#### MCP

External Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool servers mount into a `pindus` session via the repeatable `--mcp` flag. Each endpoint's tools connect through the framework MCP pool and are concatenated onto the built-in capability deck as ordinary `AgentTool`s, so the agent calls them exactly like `read` or `bash`. Requires the `indusagi[mcp]` extra (pulled in by `indusagi[mcp,tui]`). Connections go through the framework MCP facade (`indusagi.mcp`), a thin shim over the core protocol bridge (`indusagi.interop`); the shim speaks both subprocess **stdio** servers (the `command`/`args` form) and **HTTP/SSE** servers (the `url` form).

**The `--mcp` flag** names where to find MCP server config. It is a **list** flag — repeat it or comma-join values:

```bash
pindus --mcp .                              # auto-detected project/user config
pindus --mcp ./mcp.json                     # an explicit config file
pindus --mcp ./fs.json --mcp ./github.json  # several endpoints (repeated)
pindus --mcp ./fs.json,./github.json        # comma-joined (equivalent)
```

Each value is interpreted by the framework loader: **if it points at a file**, that file is loaded directly; **otherwise it is treated as a working directory** and the standard config locations under it are merged. When `--mcp` is omitted, no external servers attach and the session runs on the built-in deck alone.

**Config file format.** JSON with a top-level `servers` field, which may be either an **array** of server objects or an **object** keyed by server name (the key becomes the server's `name`). A server is reached over **HTTP** when it carries a `url`, or over **stdio** when it carries a `command`; one of the two is required. A server with `"enabled": false` is skipped.

```json
{
  "servers": [
    {
      "name": "filesystem",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/path/to/allowed/dir"],
      "enabled": true
    },
    {
      "name": "github",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"],
      "env": { "GITHUB_TOKEN": "your-github-token" },
      "enabled": true
    },
    {
      "name": "remote-server",
      "url": "http://localhost:8080/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer your-token" },
      "enabled": false
    }
  ]
}
```

The object form is equivalent (the map key becomes `name`):

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "filesystem": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "."]
    },
    "remote-server": {
      "url": "http://localhost:8080/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer your-token" }
    }
  }
}
```

| Field | Applies to | Purpose |
|-------|-----------|---------|
| `name` | both | Server id; namespaces its tools. In the object form this is the map key. |
| `command` | stdio | Executable to spawn (e.g. `npx`, `python`, `node`). |
| `args` | stdio | Argument list passed to `command`. |
| `env` | stdio | Extra environment variables for the spawned process. |
| `url` | HTTP | Endpoint URL; the core transport speaks SSE. |
| `headers` | HTTP | Headers sent on the connection (e.g. an auth bearer token). |
| `timeout` | both | Per-request timeout in milliseconds. |
| `enabled` | both | `false` skips the entry without removing it from the file. |

A file missing the `servers` field, or whose `servers` is neither array nor object, is reported and yields no servers — it does not crash the run.

**Auto-detected config search.** When a `--mcp` value is a **directory** (or `.`), the framework loader merges config from these conventional locations, in order:

1. **Project:** `./.indusvx/mcp.json`
2. **User (XDG):** `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/indusvx/mcp.json` (default `~/.config/indusvx/mcp.json`)
3. **Legacy:** `~/.indusvx/agent/mcp.json`
4. **Legacy alt:** `~/.indusvx/agent/mcp-servers.json`

All present sources are concatenated. Passing an explicit file path bypasses the search and loads only that file.

**How tools are attached.** Attachment happens at conductor-assembly time in `induscode.boot.runners.session`:

```python
servers = loadMCPConfig(path)                       # parse file or merge a cwd
pool = MCPClientPool(MCPClientPoolOptions(servers=servers))
await pool.connectAll()
for client in pool.getAllClients():
    for definition in await client.listTools():
        tools.append(createMCPAgentToolFactory(definition, client)())
```

`createMCPAgentToolFactory` mints a tool that is structurally a conductor `AgentTool`, so MCP tools require no adapter — they are simply appended to the deck:

```python
# induscode/boot/runners/session.py
tools = [*select_tools(cwd, inv), *(await load_mcp_tools(inv))]
```

The combined list becomes `SessionConductorOptions.tools`, and the system prompt is composed *after* attachment, so the briefing already describes the MCP tools. The deck comes from `provision_deck("all", ...)`.

**Failure handling and noise suppression.** `--mcp` is best-effort and never sinks a session: an endpoint that fails to load/connect is **skipped** (remaining endpoints and the built-in deck still come up); a config with zero usable servers contributes nothing and is silently passed over. The framework pool reports per-server progress on stdout/stderr and via `logging`; during attachment those streams are scope-redirected to `/dev/null` and logging below `ERROR` is disabled, so MCP chatter can never corrupt the Textual console render or the `-p --json` NDJSON stream. Setting `INDUSAGI_DEBUG` keeps all connection output visible:

```bash
INDUSAGI_DEBUG=1 pindus --mcp ./mcp.json -p "list the repo tools you have"
```

**Tool naming and filtering.** MCP tools land on the same deck as the built-ins, so `--tools` / `--no-tools` apply to them. Names are matched case-insensitively with `_` and `-` stripped. `--no-tools` disables the **built-in** deck for the run, but MCP tools are attached after that selection, so they are still available.

```bash
pindus --no-tools --mcp ./mcp.json          # built-ins off, but MCP tools still attach
pindus --tools read,bash --mcp ./mcp.json   # restrict to a named subset (built-in or MCP)
```

MCP reference symbols:

| Symbol | Kind | Source | Purpose |
|--------|------|--------|---------|
| `--mcp` | flag (list) | `launch/invocation/flags.py` | Attach external MCP endpoints; comma-separated or repeated. |
| `Invocation.mcp` | field | `boot/contract.py` | The parsed tuple of `--mcp` paths (`None` when unset). |
| `load_mcp_tools` | async function | `boot/runners/session.py` | Connect every `--mcp` endpoint and return their tools; skips failures. |
| `select_tools` | function | `boot/runners/session.py` | Build the built-in deck and apply `--tools` / `--no-tools`. |
| `build_session_conductor` | async function | `boot/runners/session.py` | Assemble the conductor; concatenates deck + MCP tools into `options.tools`. |
| `loadMCPConfig` | function | `indusagi.mcp` | Parse a config file or merge the auto-detected locations. |
| `MCPClientPool` / `MCPClientPoolOptions` | class | `indusagi.mcp` | Connect a set of MCP servers and surface their clients. |
| `createMCPAgentToolFactory` | function | `indusagi.mcp` | Mint a conductor-compatible `AgentTool` from an MCP tool definition. |
| `StdioServerConfig` / `HttpServerConfig` | dataclass | `indusagi.mcp` | The stdio (`command`) and HTTP (`url`) server config shapes. |

#### CLI reference (`pindus`)

**Synopsis:** `pindus [options] [prompt] [@file ...]`. Both console scripts (`pindus` and `induscode`) map to `induscode.entry:run`, which calls `induscode.entry:main(argv)` and `asyncio.run(boot(args))`. `main` installs a one-shot logging filter dropping `[MCP]` transport chatter from the root logger (a no-op when `INDUSAGI_DEBUG` is set), and `run` treats a `BrokenPipeError` from a vanished stdout reader (e.g. `pindus … | head`) as a clean exit 0. A bare command line opens the interactive console; a leading `prompt` positional is the first user message.

```bash
pindus                                  # interactive console (default)
pindus "refactor the auth module"       # interactive, prompt pre-filled
pindus -p "summarize this repo"         # one-shot, print the result, exit
pindus -i "start here"                  # force interactive even with a prompt
pindus -m anthropic/claude --thinking high "review this diff"
```

**Flags.** Every option is declared exactly once in a single declarative flag table (`launch.invocation.flags.FLAG_SPECS`, **17 rows**). The parser (`read_invocation`) indexes that table and the `--help` renderer (`render_usage`) walks the same rows, so help text can never drift from what the parser accepts. Inline `--name=value` and separated `--name value` are equivalent; `list` flags accept a comma-separated token or repetition; clustered short booleans (`-pi`) expand to their component switches.

*Output:*

| Flag | Alias | Kind | Purpose |
|------|-------|------|---------|
| `--print` | `-p` | boolean | Run a single request, print only the result, and exit. |
| `--json` | `--rpc` | boolean | Speak the headless line protocol for a driving parent process. |
| `--interactive` | `-i` | boolean | Force the interactive session even when a prompt is supplied. |

*Model:*

| Flag | Alias | Kind | Purpose |
|------|-------|------|---------|
| `--model` | `-m` | string | Select the model, provider-qualified or bare (e.g. `provider/name`). |
| `--account` | — | string | Authenticate the run with a named stored credential account. |
| `--thinking` | — | string | Set the reasoning effort: `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`. |
| `--list-models` | — | string | List the available models (optionally filtered by a substring) and exit. |

The `--thinking` vocabulary (`ThinkingEffort`) is a superset of the framework `ThinkingLevel` (adds `off`). An unrecognised value is silently ignored (treated as absent), not rejected.

*Context:*

| Flag | Alias | Kind | Purpose |
|------|-------|------|---------|
| `--cwd` | — | string | Scope the run to a working directory (default: the current directory). |
| `--system` | — | string | Replace the built-in system prompt with the given text. |
| `--append-system` | — | string | Append extra text after the system prompt. |
| `--resume` | `-r` | boolean | Pick a previous session to resume. |
| `--continue` | `-c` | boolean | Continue the most recent session in this directory. |

`--resume` mounts the Textual session picker; `--continue` reloads the newest session for the current directory (both honoured by the interactive runner, resolving through the Sessions store).

*Tools:*

| Flag | Alias | Kind | Purpose |
|------|-------|------|---------|
| `--tools` | — | list | Allow only the named built-in tools (comma-separated or repeated). |
| `--no-tools` | — | boolean | Disable every built-in tool for this run. |
| `--mcp` | — | list | Attach an external MCP server endpoint (comma-separated or repeated). |

`--tools` validates each name against the closed roster of built-in tool ids (`ToolName` / `TOOL_NAMES`); unrecognised names are dropped.

```bash
pindus --tools read,bash "list and read the config files"
pindus --no-tools "just explain how this code works"
pindus --mcp http://localhost:8931/sse "use the browser tools"
```

*Meta:*

| Flag | Alias | Kind | Purpose |
|------|-------|------|---------|
| `--help` | `-h` | boolean | Show the usage and exit. |
| `--version` | `-v` | boolean | Show the version and exit. |

*Unknown flags:* The parse is total — an unrecognised `--flag` is **not rejected**. It is recorded as a boolean switch in the loose `flags` bag (an inline `--flag=value` keeps its value), surviving parsing for a later phase (e.g. an extension) to reinterpret. Nothing is silently dropped.

**Run modes.** The output flags resolve to one of three modes, derived by `_derive_mode`. The launch-level mode name (`OutputMode`) projects one-to-one onto the boot runner:

| Output mode | Runner | Triggered by | Behavior |
|-------------|--------|--------------|----------|
| `text` | `repl` (interactive) | default (no `-p`/`--json`, or `-i`) | The Textual console: live REPL, slash commands, dialogs. |
| `json` | `oneshot` (print) | `-p` / `--print` (without `-i`) | One non-interactive request to settlement, then exit. Clean final text by default; an NDJSON event log when `--json` is also set. |
| `rpc` | `link` (wire) | `--json` / `--rpc` | The long-lived bidirectional JSON-RPC 2.0 / NDJSON channel over stdin/stdout for a driving parent process. |

Derivation precedence: `--json` / `--rpc` wins (→ `rpc`); otherwise `--print` without `--interactive` → `json`; otherwise `text`. So `-p` alone is one-shot print, `-p --json` is one-shot **NDJSON** print, and `--json` alone is the headless wire link. The wire link serves the `submit`, `abort`, `snapshot`, `resume`, `listModels`, and `cycleModel` operations.

```bash
pindus "help me debug this"                  # interactive (text -> repl)
pindus -p "summarize this repo"              # print: clean final text (json -> oneshot)
pindus -p --json "summarize this repo"       # print: streamed NDJSON event log
pindus --json                                # wire: headless JSON-RPC link (rpc -> link)
```

**@file attachments.** Any token of the form `@<path>` (before the `--` terminator) is collected as a file attachment for the first message rather than as a positional. The gatherer (`gather_attachments`) resolves each path against the run's working directory (with `~` expansion) and classifies by extension:

- **Text files** are inlined as a `<file path="…">…</file>` prose block, capped at **10 MB**.
- **Image files** are read and surfaced as a base64 `indusagi.ai.ImageContent` media value, capped at **20 MB**.

Anything else raises a typed `AttachmentError` whose kind is `unsupported`, `too-large`, `not-found`, or `read-failed`.

```bash
pindus "review this change" @src/main.py @docs/diagram.png
pindus -p "explain this config" @~/.config/app/settings.toml
```

**The `--` terminator.** A bare `--` stops option parsing; every subsequent token is a positional, even if it starts with `-` or `@`.

```bash
pindus -- "--this is a prompt, not a flag--"
```

**Meta short-circuits.** Three requests are handled before any session starts or directory is touched: `--help` (usage banner generated from the flag table), `--version` (e.g. `induscode 0.1.2`), and `--list-models [filter]`. `--version` is single-sourced from installed package metadata (`importlib.metadata.version("induscode")`), reflecting the installed wheel, not a hardcoded literal.

**Credential subcommands.** When the first token is a credential verb the launcher runs the sign-in/sign-out command and exits, before any normal launch. `login`/`logout` are aliases of `signin`/`signout`.

| Verb | Aliases | Purpose |
|------|---------|---------|
| `signin` | `login` | Store a credential for a provider — browser sign-in (OAuth) when supported, otherwise an api key. |
| `signout` | `logout` | Remove the named account, or all accounts for the provider when `--account` is omitted. |

Verb flags (parsed by the credential command, not the main flag table):

| Flag | Applies to | Purpose |
|------|------------|---------|
| `--provider <id>` | both | The provider id to act on. The first bare positional is also taken as the provider. |
| `--account <name>` | both | Name the credential account (default: `default`). Letters, digits, `-`, `_`; max 50 chars. |
| `--method <oauth\|api-key>` | `signin` | Force the sign-in method. `--oauth` and `--api-key` are shorthands. |
| `--list` (`--ls`) | `signin` | Read-only listing of saved accounts (kind + default marker); stores nothing. |

OAuth-capable providers (browser sign-in): `anthropic`, `openai`, and `github-copilot` (the last via an RFC 8628 device grant). Api-key providers (the `PROVIDER_DIRECTORY`, 14 entries): `anthropic`, `openai`, `google`, `xai`, `groq`, `cerebras`, `mistral`, `openrouter`, `minimax`, `kimi`, `sarvam`, `krutrim`, `nvidia`, `zai`. Every failure is a typed `CredentialFault` printed via `format_credential_fault` before a non-zero exit.

**Package subcommands.** When the first token is a package subcommand the launcher manages the extension-package sources and exits. Sources are plain strings the addon loader understands — an `npm:` spec, a `git:` / `https:` repo, or a bare local path — persisted under the `extensionPackages` key in the two-tier settings store.

```bash
pindus install npm:@scope/my-ext     # add a source (idempotent)
pindus list                          # show configured sources
pindus remove npm:@scope/my-ext      # drop a source
pindus update                        # re-read and confirm the configured set
pindus config                        # print resolved settings paths + merged JSON
```

| Subcommand | Argument | Purpose |
|------------|----------|---------|
| `install` | source | Add a package source to the configured set (idempotent under source matching). |
| `remove` | source | Remove a package source from the configured set. |
| `update` | — | Re-read and report the configured sources (resolution is lazy at startup; no separate fetch step). |
| `list` | — | Print the configured package sources. |
| `config` | — | Print the global/project settings file locations and the merged resolved settings as JSON. |

`install`/`remove` compare sources structurally (an `npm:` spec ignores a trailing `@version`, a git url drops its scheme and `.git` suffix, a local path matches verbatim). A missing/invalid argument is a printed error line and a non-zero exit; the command never raises for an expected failure.

**Dispatch order.** `boot.boot` consumes the command line in a fixed order, so a leading subcommand verb always wins over a prompt of the same spelling:

1. **Credential command** — `argv[0]` ∈ `{signin, signout, login, logout}` → run and exit.
2. **Package command** — `argv[0]` ∈ `{install, remove, update, list, config}` → run and exit.
3. **Meta short-circuits** — `--help`, `--version`, `--list-models [filter]` → print and exit, before any stage runs or directory is touched.
4. **Stage pipeline** — build the run context (workspace, settings, auth, model, tools, MCP, addons).
5. **Runner dispatch** — `select_runner` picks the runner whose `accepts` predicate matches the resolved mode (`repl` / `oneshot` / `link`), defaulting to the interactive REPL.

**Exit codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `0` | Clean run (or a `BrokenPipeError` from a closed stdout reader). |
| `1` | An unexpected boot failure, a handled credential command that did not complete (printed fault), or a package command that reported a bad/missing argument. |

The one-shot (`oneshot`) channel additionally returns `1` when the settled run is faulted (`state.phase == "faulted"`).

**Parsing in Python.** `read_invocation` folds a sliced `argv` into a fully-typed `Invocation`; `read_file_references` re-walks just the `@file` refs.

```python
from induscode.launch import read_invocation, read_file_references

inv = read_invocation(["-p", "--model", "openai/gpt", "hello", "@notes.md"])
assert inv.mode == "json" and inv.print is True
assert inv.model == "openai/gpt" and inv.prompt == "hello"

refs = read_file_references(["-p", "hi", "@notes.md"])  # -> ["notes.md"]
```

#### Package exports

The importable public surface is defined by exactly two files:

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `src/induscode/__init__.py` | Lazy meta-barrel: `VERSION`/`__version__` plus **17 subsystem packages** exposed as lazily-imported attributes. |
| `src/induscode/entry.py` | Process entry: `main()` / `run()` console-script shim that boots the agent. |

`pyproject.toml` maps both console scripts to the entry shim. The package requires **Python 3.11+** and is built on `indusagi[mcp,tui]`. The live binary path is `entry.run` → `boot.boot` → `run_stages` / `select_runner`.

```toml
[project.scripts]
pindus = "induscode.entry:run"
induscode = "induscode.entry:run"
```

**The entry module** exports two names:

| Name | Kind | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `main(argv=None)` | function | Process-level entry. Installs the one-shot `[MCP]` log-noise filter, lazily imports `boot`, returns `asyncio.run(boot(args))`. Returns the exit code (does **not** raise `SystemExit`) so tests can call it directly. Resolves `argv` to `sys.argv[1:]` when omitted. |
| `run()` | function | The `[project.scripts]` shim. Calls `main()`, flushes stdout, and on `BrokenPipeError` parks stdout on `/dev/null` and treats the run as a clean exit 0; then `sys.exit(code)`. |

The MCP-noise filter is a single idempotent `logging.Filter` on the root logger that drops any record carrying the `[MCP]` marker — a **no-op when `INDUSAGI_DEBUG` is set** (the brand's `env_debug`). The `boot` import is deferred to function scope so `import induscode.entry` stays side-effect-light.

**The induscode barrel.** `import induscode` is cheap and side-effect-free; the only eager import is `from induscode.workspace import VERSION`, and every subsystem loads lazily on first attribute access via PEP-562 `__getattr__`. `__all__` is computed as `["VERSION", "__version__", *sorted(_SUBSYSTEMS)]`:

```python
>>> import induscode
>>> sorted(induscode.__all__)
['VERSION', '__version__', 'addons', 'boot', 'briefing', 'capability_deck',
 'channels', 'conductor', 'console', 'console_slash', 'insight', 'kit',
 'launch', 'runtime_bridge', 'sessions', 'settings', 'transcript_export',
 'window_budget', 'workspace']
```

`_SUBSYSTEMS` is the single source of truth: a dict mapping the 17 public snake_case attribute names to their subpackage names. Touching `induscode.console` is the only thing that pulls in the Textual / react_ink stack.

**Subsystem barrels** (each attribute resolves to a subpackage with its own explicit `__all__`):

| Attribute | Representative exports |
|-----------|------------------------|
| `workspace` | `VERSION`, `BRAND`, `Brand`, `create_workspace`, `Workspace`, `LAYOUT`, `ensure_dirs` |
| `boot` | `boot`, `run_stages`, `STAGES`, `select_runner`, `RUNNERS`, `BootContext`, `create_auth_vault`, `apply_upgrades` |
| `launch` | `read_invocation`, `Invocation`, `run_credential_command`, `start_oauth_login`, `print_model_catalog`, `FLAG_SPECS` |
| `conductor` | `create_session_conductor`, `SessionConductor`, `ConductorState`, `reduce_state`, `TranscriptEntry`, `SessionHead` |
| `console` | `mount_console`, `console_reducer`, `init_console_state`, `ConsoleApp`, `ConsoleState`, `ConsoleEvent` |
| `console_slash` | `build_registry`, `resolve_slash`, `SlashRegistry`, `SlashCommand`, `Handled`, `Prompt`, `Unknown` |
| `channels` | `create_link_server`, `run_oneshot`, `NdjsonFramer`, `define_ops` |
| `capability_deck` | `provision_deck`, `ToolDeck`, `CAPABILITY_CARDS`, `reduce_ledger`, `Capability` |
| `addons` | `create_addon_host`, `AddonManifest`, `EventDispatcher`, `InterceptorChain` |
| `briefing` | `compose_briefing`, `BriefingSection`, `apply_macros`, `gather_skill_cards`, `SkillCard` |
| `insight` | `create_recorder`, `InsightRecorder`, `Probe`, `create_collector_sink`, `replay_probes` |
| `window_budget` | `create_condenser`, `condense`, `estimate_tokens`, `plan_slice`, `summarize` |
| `transcript_export` | `publish_transcript`, `paint_sgr`, `ThemeBridge`, `PAGE_SHELL`, `fold_sgr` |
| `runtime_bridge` | `create_runtime_broker`, `RuntimeBridge`, `claude_cli_bridge`, `codex_cli_bridge`, `NormalizedEvent` |
| `settings` | `PreferenceStore`, `Preferences`, `DEFAULT_PREFERENCES`, `canonical_key`, `SETTING_KEYS` |
| `sessions` | `SessionLibrary`, `SavedSession`, `BranchNode`, `PriorTurn` |
| `kit` | `plan_provision`, `build_download_request`, `quote_arg`, `sniff_image_format`, `open_in_external_editor` |

Subsystem relationships worth knowing: `boot` re-exports the `workspace` surface (`BRAND`, `Brand`, `Workspace`, `create_workspace`, `ensure_dirs`, `WorkspaceOverrides`); `console` re-exports `console_slash` types; `conductor` is the largest barrel (~100 names) and wraps exactly one framework `Agent`, exposing the `SessionConductor` that the console, oneshot, and JSON-RPC link all drive; `window_budget` feeds the conductor's `CondenseFn` seam; `capability_deck` builds the `ToolDeck` the conductor consumes (its `Capability` aliases the framework `AgentTool`); `insight` is a thin wrapper over framework tracing (aliasing `Probe`/`Signal` onto the framework `Segment`/`TraceSignal`); `runtime_bridge` is a complete, fully-tested library layer **not yet wired into the boot path**.

**Barrel discipline.** Every subsystem `__init__.py` follows the same shape: top-of-file `from .module import ...` lines, then an explicit alphabetized `__all__` re-exporting that subsystem's frozen contract types plus the behavior functions. The smallest barrel is `sessions` (4 names: `SessionLibrary`, `SavedSession`, `BranchNode`, `PriorTurn`); the largest is `conductor`. Console sub-packages (`components`, `input`, `overlays`, `theme`, `slash_commands`) each carry their own `__all__`, reached as `induscode.console.<sub>`.

```python
from induscode.entry import main
exit_code = main(["--version"])   # returns an int, does not raise SystemExit

import induscode
print(induscode.VERSION)                            # eager: from workspace import VERSION
ws = induscode.workspace.create_workspace()         # first touch imports the subsystem
```

#### Parity & gaps

`induscode` is a **clean-room Python rebuild** of the TypeScript `indusagi-coding-agent` (lineage `v0.1.62`), running entirely on the indusagi framework. The audit compares `induscode-python-rebuild/src/induscode` row by row against the TS source tree `indus-code-rebuild/src`. Verdict: **full feature parity** on the user-facing surface (every CLI flag, all 26 slash commands, every console overlay, settings, sessions, channels, addons, capability deck) with **13 deliberate, plan-cited divergences** and a short list of known gaps clustered in two subsystems (`launch` and `insight`).

**Provenance.** An independent implementation written against a behavioral spec plus the public `indusagi` API; no third-party application source was copied. Two release gates enforce this:

| Gate | What it checks |
|------|----------------|
| `scripts/lineage_scan.py` | Word-boundary greps `src/induscode` (excluding tests and the framework) for upstream `pi` / `mariozechner` markers; exits `1` on any hit. |
| public-API guard test | Pins the package's exported surface so it cannot silently drift. |

`pyproject.toml` embeds both `NOTICE` and `CREDITS.md` into the wheel via PEP 639 `license-files`. The package is MIT-licensed, built with `hatchling`. The underlying `indusagi` framework is a separate PyPI package, reused wholesale and **not** scanned by the lineage gate.

**Parity by area.** Delivered milestone by milestone (M0–M6); the M6 audit marked **106/106 checklist rows done** (0 partial, 0 missing), suite green.

| Area | Parity | Notes |
|------|--------|-------|
| CLI flags + conventions | full (23/23) | All 17 flags plus `@file` attachments, `--` terminator, `-pi` clustering, unknown-flag tolerance. |
| Subcommands | full | `signin`/`login`, `signout`/`logout`, and `install`/`remove`/`update`/`list`/`config`. |
| Slash commands | full (26 static + dynamic + 10 aliases) | Transcript, workbench, integrations groups, plus dynamic `/skill:<name>` and `/<template>` macros. |
| Overlays, theme, input, startup | full (16/16) | 12 modal kinds via `OVERLAY_HANDLERS`, 4 theme schemes with live preview, 21-chord `/keys`, double-Ctrl+C exit, startup map + changelog splash. |
| Channels | full (5/5) | `SESSION_OPS` ×6 with flat `LinkSnapshot`, dialog bridge `ask`/`tell` (90 s timeout→fallback), oneshot text + NDJSON framing, U+2028/29 escaping, JSON-RPC error codes. |
| Addons + capability deck | full (8/8) | 13 hook events, interceptor onion, `.indus/addons` discovery via `importlib`, 12 framework built-ins, 5 app cards, content/ULID bridge ledger. |
| Sessions, transcripts, export | full | Branchable NDJSON tree (`indus/transcript@1`), resume by id with deepest-leaf recovery, per-cwd `--<slug>--` scoping, legacy import, self-contained HTML `/export`. |
| Runtime-bridge | full (2/2) | 3 dialects (`claude-cli`, `codex-cli`, `indusagi-cli`) → `NormalizedEvent`. Library-only in both builds (not wired into boot). |
| Window-budget + insight | full (wired) | `window_budget` condenser (`0.75` trigger / `6000` keep-recent / `2048` reserve), manual `/summarize-context`, insight collector/replay wrapper over framework tracing. |
| Auth vault | full | Multi-account with OAuth refresh, default promotion, `0600` file mode. |

**Deliberate divergences (13)** — by-design ports of TS behavior onto Python / Textual / framework idioms; documented, plan-cited, fully tested:

| # | Divergence |
|---|-----------|
| W1 | Composer deleted — TS software-caret composer replaced by framework `PromptEditor`. |
| W2 | Paste vault / burst-debounce deleted — replaced by framework `EditorCore` paste markers + native paste events. |
| W3 | jiti → importlib — `.py` addons load via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`; `BUNDLED_NAMESPACES` vestigial. |
| W4 | insight wraps `indusagi.tracing` — only the collector sink, replay reader, and redaction wrapper are app code. |
| W5 | repl placeholder → real Textual mount in `boot/runners/repl_runner.py`. |
| W6 | runtime-bridge barrel-only — tested library, deliberately not wired into boot. |
| W7 | `/memory` on/off cosmetic — flips a reporting flag only; never removes the memory card. |
| W8 | Two distinct compaction engines — `window_budget` (tokens, `0.75`, 3.6 chars/token) wired; framework `runtime.memory` (turns, `0.8`) intentionally unwired. |
| W9 | Chord-latch break semantics — timer-bounded (600 ms) under Textual. |
| W10 | OAuth overlay on `asyncio.Future` — parked-resolver replaces TS callback threading. |
| W11 | TypeBox → literal JSON-schema dicts (framework `parameters: Mapping` convention). |
| W12 | Modal routing inversion — TS always-mounted overlays become awaited `push_screen` flows with typed outcomes via `OVERLAY_HANDLERS`. |
| W13 | todo wire names — `todo_read` / `todo_set` (vs TS internal names), honoring the Python framework's wire contract. |

**Known gaps.** The gap audit (2026-06-12 snapshot) records **7 gaps: 0 high, 1 medium, 6 low**, clustered in `launch` and `insight`. Nothing in the core agent loop, tool execution, or console UI is affected. Estimate: ~98% behavioral parity.

| # | Gap | Subsystem | Status | Severity |
|---|-----|-----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | CLI `--resume` interactive picker never mounts on a TTY; runner silently falls back to a fresh session | launch | broken | **medium** |
| 2 | GitHub Copilot browser sign-in provider absent (framework `OAUTH_PROVIDERS` carries only `anthropic`, `openai`) | launch | missing | low |
| 3 | Insight secret redaction over-redacts — whole value instead of the matched run | insight | divergent | low |
| 4 | Insight `fail()` emits no in-flight `update` signal before close | insight | divergent | low |
| 5 | Insight persisted/streamed fault loses the error name + stack | insight | partial | low |
| 6 | Insight redactor `omit_keys` option (drop keys wholesale) missing | insight | missing | low |
| 7 | Top-level package namespace re-export of all subsystems | root barrel | divergent | low |

Notes: **Gap 1** (`_DefaultResumeDeps.mount_picker` unconditionally raises; `repl_runner.py` calls `pick_resume_target` with no injected deps) is *medium* not *high* because the in-console `/resume` slash command is fully wired and opens the same picker — a user can run `pindus --resume`, land in a fresh session, type `/resume`, and reach the picker. **Gaps 3–6 (insight)** are wrapper-side costs of delegating to framework `SecretScrubber` / `SegmentError` / transport (waiver W4); none affects the final close record's status or end-user behavior; impact is limited to live trace dashboards and offline analysis. **Gap 7 is now closed in source**: the current `induscode/__init__.py` lazily re-exports all 17 subsystems via PEP 562 `__getattr__` (treat the gap report as a point-in-time snapshot). Recommended fix order, highest user-impact first: wire the CLI `--resume` Textual picker (gap 1), add GitHub Copilot OAuth config (gap 2), then the four insight refinements (gaps 3–6).

**Upstream framework defect (DO-NOT-FIX in the app).** Symptom: the first streamed text chunk is dropped from `-p` / `--json` / NDJSON output (`"pong"` → `"ong"`); the whole first chunk is dropped, not a fixed character count. Root cause: the framework `agent/agent.py` `_FacadeTranslator._on_delta` emits the first text delta only inside the `MessageStartEvent` partial; only second-and-later deltas surface as `MessageUpdateEvent` text deltas. The app side is parity-correct (`conductor/signal_hub.py` maps `message_start → []`, matching the TS translator table), so no `TextSignal` is produced for the first chunk and `-p` loses it. Blast radius: `-p` text output and the `-p`/`--json` text-signal stream; the interactive TUI **masks** it (the final `message_end` carries the complete assistant message). The fix is filed upstream; the app intentionally does not work around it to avoid diverging from the TS translator table.

**Library swaps** (TS deps replaced with Python equivalents during the port):

| TS dependency | Python replacement |
|---------------|--------------------|
| `marked` | `markdown-it-py>=3.0` (transcript-export markdown) |
| `highlight.js` | `pygments>=2.18` (transcript-export highlighting) |
| `ulid` | `python-ulid>=2.7` (bridge-ledger ULID keys) |
| Ink / React | Textual (interactive console) |
| jiti virtual modules | plain `importlib` addon loading |

The sole framework dependency is `indusagi[mcp,tui]>=0.1.2` (the `mcp` and `tui`/Textual extras are required because the framework's `shell_app` barrel imports `mcp` and `textual` eagerly). The process title is not set (Python has no portable titling without a third-party dep — deliberately skipped, same as the framework port).

**Version & doc-string drift.** The version is single-sourced: it lives only in `pyproject.toml` (currently `0.1.2`); `workspace/brand.py` reads it back at runtime via `importlib.metadata.version("induscode")`, with a `"0.1.0.dev0"` fallback that fires only on an uninstalled source checkout. So `pindus --version` reports whatever `pyproject.toml` declares, not the doc strings. The `README`, `CHANGELOG` (header `0.1.0 — 2026-06-11`), and `PARITY_REPORT` still reference `0.1.0`/`v0.1.0` from the first release. Test-count figures drift across documents: the changelog and parity report cite **649 tests**, the README cites **703** — take the per-document figure as the snapshot at that document's date.

**Source files of record:** `PARITY_REPORT.md` (M6 audit, 106/106 rows, 13 waivers), `GAP_REPORT.md` (the 7-gap audit), `CREDITS.md` / `NOTICE` (provenance, PEP 639 `license-files`), `CHANGELOG.md`, `pyproject.toml`, `scripts/lineage_scan.py`, `src/induscode/__init__.py`, `src/induscode/workspace/brand.py`, `src/induscode/entry.py`.

#### Testing

The rebuild ships a **703-test, network-free `pytest` suite** under `tests/`. Run it with `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`. Every test runs against a mock connector and the Textual `Pilot` driver — no LLM calls, no real home directory, no sleeps.

**Running the suite.** There is no `conftest.py` and no shared-fixtures module — every test file defines its own fakes inline. All configuration lives in `pyproject.toml`:

```toml
[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
testpaths = ["tests"]
```

`asyncio_mode = "auto"` means the ~240 `async def test_*` functions run under `pytest-asyncio` with no per-test marker; `testpaths = ["tests"]` pins collection.

```bash
cd induscode-python-rebuild
.venv/bin/python -m pytest                          # whole suite — 703 tests
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/conductor/         # 110 catalog/matcher/serialize/submit/queue/fork cases
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/console/test_e2e_pilot.py   # scripted Pilot e2e over the real ConsoleApp
```

**Hermetic discipline** (sealed off along three axes):

| Axis | Rule | How it is enforced |
|------|------|--------------------|
| No network | Nothing talks to a real model | A mock connector / `ScriptedConductor` stands in for the LLM and streams deterministic deltas |
| No real home | No test touches `~/.pindusagi/` | Every disk test runs under `tmp_path`, with `BRAND.env_profile_dir` (`INDUSAGI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) pinned beneath it and `INDUSAGI_HOME` deleted |
| No sleeps | No wall-clock timing | Textual `Pilot.pause()`, the bounded `wait_until()` poller, and `app.workers.wait_for_complete()` synchronize against the message pump |

Full collection runs in ~1s.

**Layout.** `tests/` mirrors `src/induscode/` one-to-one (`tests/<subsystem>/test_*.py`). Two flat root files guard the package as a whole. **Coverage map** (703 collected tests by top-level directory):

| Directory | Tests | What it covers |
|-----------|------:|----------------|
| `console/` | 324 | Reducer, input/intents/chords/completion, theme, banner + chrome, overlays (`ModalKind` router), startup survey, the slash handler + command groups, and the two Pilot files (`test_console_app.py`, `test_e2e_pilot.py`). |
| `conductor/` | 110 | `catalog_store` (tolerant catalog gate, `ModelMatcher` scoring constants, transcript-tree append/branch/fork, NDJSON serialize round-trip), submit/resume, queue + fork, contract + signal-hub + skill-parse. |
| `console_slash/` | 36 | The framework-backed slash registry (`build_registry`, `Handled`) end-to-end with no TUI/conductor. |
| `launch/` | 34 | The flag table and `read_invocation` parser, usage renderer, package command. |
| `capability_deck/` | 34 | The contract + bridge-ledger (pure, `python-ulid` keys) and card provisioning / novel cards. |
| `boot/` | 33 | `tokenize_invocation` flag→mode mapping, `--help`/`--version` short-circuit, workspace resolution, idempotent `apply_upgrades`, `run_stages` `BootContext`, `select_runner`; invocation projection, `--resume` picker seam, session-persist integration. |
| `runtime_bridge/` | 18 | External-runtime provider routing. |
| `addons/` | 14 | The addons host pipeline (no real import, no disk for host-pipeline cases). |
| `settings/` | 11 | The `PreferenceStore`. |
| `window_budget/` | 10 | Context-window budgeting incl. the condense-scope branch digest. |
| `kit/` | 10 | The leaf helper kit. |
| `briefing/` | 10 | System-prompt composition. |
| `sessions/` | 9 | The `SessionLibrary`. |
| `insight/` | 9 | The tracing wrapper over the framework. |
| `transcript_export/` | 8 | The markdown/highlight transcript export (`markdown-it-py` + `pygments`). |
| `channels/` | 8 | The non-interactive channels. |
| `test_public_api.py` | 7 | The frozen-contract / lazy-barrel guard. |
| `test_scaffold.py` | 17 | The M0 version / brand / workspace gate. |

**The two root guards.** `tests/test_public_api.py` proves the public surface stays frozen and the lazy barrel stays lazy: `EXPECTED_SUBSYSTEMS` (the 17-name tuple, hardcoded on purpose so a silently-dropped subpackage is caught), `test_all_modules_import` (walks every module via `pkgutil.walk_packages`), `test_declared_exports_resolve` (every `__all__` sorted + resolving), `test_barrel_reexports_every_subsystem`, `test_barrel_subsystems_match_packages` (cross-checks against on-disk packages and `induscode._SUBSYSTEMS`), and `test_bare_import_is_side_effect_free` (runs `import induscode` in a clean subprocess; asserts no `textual.*` and no subsystem beyond `workspace`/`brand`/`locator` got eagerly loaded). `tests/test_scaffold.py` pins identity and path resolution: version single-sourcing (`induscode.__version__ == induscode.VERSION == metadata.version("induscode")`, no hardcoded literal), frozen `BRAND` identity (`BRAND.name == "induscode"`, `BRAND.profile_dir_name == ".pindusagi"`, `BRAND.bin_names == ("pindus", "induscode")`, `BRAND.env_profile_dir == "INDUSAGI_CODING_AGENT_DIR"`), and sandboxed `Workspace` path resolution with the 15-key `LAYOUT`.

**Three layers of fidelity:** (1) pure-data unit tests over dependency-free reducers, folds, and matchers; (2) protocol/seam tests over injected stubs (`CatalogSource` stubs, `memory_backend`/`fs_backend` stores, the `SessionConductor` protocol faked by `ScriptedConductor`); (3) full Textual end-to-end drives in `tests/console/test_e2e_pilot.py` and `test_console_app.py` that mount the real `ConsoleApp` via `app.run_test(size=...)` and drive it through `Pilot`.

**The console e2e harness** mounts the actual `ConsoleApp` and drives it like a user, then synchronizes against the message pump; it reads `app.screen._compositor.render_strips()` to assert against actually-painted terminal cells (and caret visibility) — a deliberate fix after a blank-content-row regression slipped past buffer-only checks. Explicit regression pins: `TestEditorRendersTypedText` (prompt box drew its border but content row was blank) and `TestEditorKeyboardFocus` (text could not be typed into the composer — non-focusable-scroll-containers fix).

**Key fixtures/helpers** (in `tests/console/test_e2e_pilot.py`): `ScriptedConductor` (a deterministic fake satisfying the `SessionConductor` protocol, ~25 methods inline; `submit()` streams scripted `TextSignal` deltas and can park mid-stream via `hold_turn_end`/hang), `build_app` (assembles a real `ConsoleApp` over a fresh `ScriptedConductor`; returns `(app, scripted)`), `wait_until` (a bounded message-pump poll helper, default 100 tries — the no-sleep synchronization primitive), and `make_services` (builds an `OverlayServices` wiring a `PreferenceStore.at_paths`, a `SessionLibrary`, a `FakeVault`, and stubbed login callbacks over `tmp_path`). The boot sandbox fixture `sandbox_home` (in `tests/boot/test_boot.py`) gives a fresh `tmp_path` home with `BRAND.env_profile_dir` pinned and `INDUSAGI_HOME` deleted. The reducer exhaustiveness pin `_REPRESENTATIVES` (in `tests/console/test_reducer.py`) feeds one `ConsoleEvent` per discriminant through `console_reducer`, asserted to cover all `CONSOLE_EVENT_TYPES`.

**The 703 vs 683 gap.** The headline count is **703 collected tests** (confirmed by `pytest --collect-only`), while there are 683 raw `def test_` declarations. The 20-test gap is `@pytest.mark.parametrize` expansion — exactly three parametrize sites in the suite (two in `tests/conductor/test_catalog_store.py`, one in `tests/console/test_console_app.py`).

**Framework as a test dependency.** The suite imports from both the package under test and the upstream `indusagi` framework — **21 test files import `from indusagi...`** — making it an integration boundary, not a closed unit. Framework imports cluster on:

| Framework area | Files | Used for |
|----------------|------:|----------|
| `indusagi.ai` | 11 | `AssistantMessage`, `UserMessage`, `TextContent`, `ToolCall`, `create_zero_usage`, … |
| `indusagi.react_ink` | 9 | `ModelDialog`, `StatusMessage`, `UiDisplayBlock`, and `components.editor.PromptEditor` / `components.messages.list.MessageList` / `components.display_block.DisplayBlockView` used in the Pilot e2e |
| `indusagi.agent` | 3 | Custom message kinds `BashExecutionMessage` / `BranchSummaryMessage` / `CompactionSummaryMessage` / `CustomMessage` |
| `indusagi.tui.*` | — | Editor / keybindings / keys / autocomplete primitives |
| `indusagi.llmgateway.credentials.oauth` | — | OAuth credential seam |

Consequences: the input tests in `tests/console/test_input.py` verify that editor verbs were *absorbed* by the framework's editor defaults rather than reimplemented, and the reducer's dropped buffer/caret/history event families are asserted *absent*. The suite tests against the live framework source (an editable-installed `indusagi[mcp,tui]>=0.1.2`), so a framework change can break these tests even with no `induscode` change.

## Edition 3 — induscode for Rust (`/rust-cli`)

> The Rust coding agent. Installed with `cargo install induscode`, which builds
> two equivalent commands — `indusr` (primary) and `indusagir` — running a ratatui
> REPL console and built on the single-binary Rust indusagi framework. Documented
> at `/rust-cli` on the site.


### Start & the ratatui console

This section covers the Rust edition of the coding agent — `induscode` (docs area `/rust-cli`) — from install and first run through the interactive ratatui console: its overview, getting-started/install path, layered architecture, console internals, the slash-command catalog, the thirteen modal overlays, and the theming engine.

#### Overview & README

`induscode` is the **100%-Rust edition** of the terminal-first AI coding agent, built entirely on the published [`indusagi`](/rust) framework crate. It is built from scratch in Rust, **never transliterated** from the TypeScript (`/cli`) or Python (`/python-cli`) editions — it is the third edition of the same agent, reverse-engineered to a behavioral spec.

It ships as **one merged product crate** (`crates/induscode`): every former `induscode-*` library crate is now a `pub mod` under `src/`, and the framework arrives as the single published `indusagi` umbrella crate (`version = "0.1.0"`, declared with `features = ["swarm"]`), replacing 13 former `indusagi-*` path deps. Two `[[bin]]` targets — **`indusr`** and **`indusagir`** — share one `async fn main() -> ExitCode` in `src/bin/main.rs`; the live brand is whichever name the OS launched under. The library surface is `induscode::<module>` (e.g. `induscode::boot`, `induscode::conductor`); the framework is reached as `indusagi::<module>`.

Installation registers two equivalent bin targets, both pointing at `src/bin/main.rs`:

```bash
cargo install induscode          # the CLI — installs indusr + indusagir
cargo binstall induscode         # prebuilt binary (no compile)
cargo add induscode              # the library — depend on the agent (induscode::<module>)
```

```toml
# crates/induscode/Cargo.toml
[[bin]]
name = "indusr"
path = "src/bin/main.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "indusagir"
path = "src/bin/main.rs"
```

Toolchain floor: **edition 2024, MSRV 1.96** (matching the framework's `rust-toolchain.toml` pin). Authenticate by exporting a provider key (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, etc.) or storing one in the local vault (`indusr signin anthropic`, `indusr auth status`). The version is single-sourced from `Cargo.toml` and read at compile time (`VERSION == env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`) — never a string literal, enforced by `cargo run -p xtask -- version`.

**Brand vs. bin names.** The crate is `induscode` on crates.io; the two installed bins are `indusr` (primary) and `indusagir`. The internal **brand** (`BIN_NAMES`, process title, `--version` app name) is `indus` / `indusagi`. A launch of `indusr`/`indusagir` resolves through `resolve_brand`'s `BIN_NAMES[0]` fallback to the `indus` brand; `--version` prints `indusagi <version>` because `BRAND.app_name == "indusagi"`.

**The `indusr` command / runner selection.** A bare invocation opens the interactive ratatui console; `-p`/`--print` runs one-shot print-and-exit; `--json` speaks the headless NDJSON / JSON-RPC line protocol. The runner is selected inside `boot::boot_run`:

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
indusr                                  # interactive ratatui console (current repo)
indusr "fix the failing test in src/auth"
indusr -p "summarise what changed on this branch"   # one-shot print, then exit
indusr --json                           # NDJSON line protocol for a parent process
indusr -m anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 -p "hi"       # pick a model
indusr --list-models                    # browse the model / provider catalog
indusr --version                        # print "<app name> <version>" and exit
```

| Invocation | Mode | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `indusr` | interactive | ratatui REPL — streaming replies, a live tool deck, slash commands |
| `indusr -p "…"` / `--print` | print | one request, prints the final result, exits |
| `indusr --json` | line protocol | newline-delimited JSON for a parent process to drive |
| `indusr auth login` / `status` | credentials | store / inspect credentials in the local auth vault |

**No-session verbs** are intercepted by `route()` in `main.rs` *before* the boot handoff (they never need a session, and boot would otherwise drop them into the REPL):

| Verb | Owner | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `signin <provider>` | agent vault | Interactive API-key login (defaults to `--method api-key`) |
| `signout <provider>` | agent vault | Remove a stored credential for a provider |
| `auth login \| refresh \| help` | framework `indusagi::shell_app::auth_cli` | Browser (OAuth/PKCE) flows |
| `auth status [provider]` | agent vault reader | Reconciles framework + multi-account vault shapes |
| `auth logout` | agent `signout` path | The framework `auth` command has no logout verb |
| `install \| remove \| update \| list \| config` | `induscode::launch::pickers` | The extension-package surface over `PreferenceStore` |
| `--list-models [filter]` | `induscode::launch::catalog` | Prints the model catalog over the live gateway cards |

Because the shipped OAuth client ids are unconfigured sentinels in a default build, `signin <provider>` auto-appends `--method api-key`; pass `--method oauth` (or `--oauth`) for the browser flow.

**Feature Overview** — every subsystem is a `pub mod` of the merged crate: `launch` (launch front door), `boot` (boot pipeline), `conductor` (session core), `window_budget`, `deck` (capability deck), `runtime_bridge`, `addons`, `console` (the ratatui UI with **13 overlays**), `channels` (print + JSON-RPC 2.0), `briefing`, `transcript_export`, `insight`, and `core`.

**Cargo features** (defaults `["rustls", "mcp", "tui", "oauth"]`): `tui` pulls the framework render layer for the console; `mcp` forwards to `indusagi/mcp`; `swarm` gates subagent delegation; `composio` adds the SaaS adapter; `cli-bridges` gates the external-runtime child transport; `mimalloc` is an opt-in global allocator. A headless build drops the console entirely.

**Build & clean-room gates:**

```bash
cargo build --workspace
cargo build --release -p induscode          # the release/dist profile (lto)
cargo build -p induscode --no-default-features --features "rustls,anthropic"   # headless
cargo run -p xtask -- lineage               # source-hygiene gate
cargo run -p xtask -- version               # literal-VERSION single-source gate
```

`xtask lineage` exits non-zero if any provenance marker appears in non-test source; `xtask framework-via-deps` asserts the framework is reached only through declared crate deps; `xtask version` forbids any string-literal version outside `Cargo.toml`.

**Parity** across the three editions (same `FLAG_SPECS` grammar, slash catalog, runner trio, boot short-circuit verbs):

| Edition | Package | Bins | Framework |
|---|---|---|---|
| TypeScript | `indusagi-coding-agent` | `indus` / `indusagi` | `indusagi` (npm) |
| Python | `induscode` (PyPI) | `pindus` / `induscode` | `indusagi` (PyPI) |
| Rust | `induscode` (crates.io) | `indusr` / `indusagir` | `indusagi` (crates.io) |

#### Getting started & install

State lives under `~/.indusagi/agent/`. The toolchain is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml`:

```toml
[toolchain]
channel    = "1.96.0"
components = ["rustfmt", "clippy"]
```

The pin matches the framework's MSRV floor (`rust-version = "1.96"`, edition 2024). The product crate depends on `indusagi = { version = "0.1.0", features = ["swarm"] }`, exactly as the TS agent declared `"indusagi": "^0.13.1"`.

**Build from source / dev launch:**

```bash
cargo build --workspace
cargo build -p induscode --no-default-features --features "rustls,anthropic"  # headless
cargo build --release -p induscode                                            # dist profile, lto = "fat"
cargo run -p induscode --bin indusr -- --help
cargo run -p induscode --bin indusr -- "fix the failing test in src/auth"
```

**Install matrix:**

| Audience | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Rust user (crates.io) | `cargo install induscode` | installs `indusr` + `indusagir` |
| Rust user, prebuilt | `cargo binstall induscode` | downloads a release binary |
| Embedding as a library | `cargo add induscode` | adds the dependency (surface `induscode::<module>`) |
| npm user (preserves the habit) | `npm i -g indusagi-coding-agent` | the published package wrapper |
| macOS / Linux, scripted | `curl --proto '=https' -sSf https://…/install.sh \| sh` | scripted install |
| Windows | `irm https://…/install.ps1 \| iex` | scripted install |

**The binary's `main`** is `async fn main() -> ExitCode` — the single OS exit point (returning `ExitCode` lets tokio drain and destructors run, so raw/alt-screen mode is always restored). It runs four steps mirroring the TS `entry.ts` + `boot.ts`: (1) brand off `argv[0]`'s basename via `resolve_brand` (falls back to `BIN_NAMES[0]` = `"indus"`); (2) install the single `[MCP]` console-noise filter (`install_mcp_noise_filter`, a no-op when `INDUSAGI_DEBUG` is set); (3) route the argv (`route`) — no-session verbs run to an exit code without touching boot, `--help`/`--version` short-circuit; (4) hand a real run to `boot_run`, whose `ExitCode` is adopted unchanged.

```bash
indusr --help        # the option reference, generated from the flag table
indusr --version     # prints: indusagi <version>
indusagir --version  # the second bin name prints the same
```

`--help`/`-h` renders usage from the single declarative flag table via `render_usage()` then appends a `Commands:` footer for the credential verbs. An unknown **leading** flag is a usage error — **exit code 2** (the malformed-invocation convention). The parser (`read_invocation`) is otherwise tolerant: unknown `--flag`s land in a loose flag bag as booleans (the extension-flag escape hatch).

**Set a provider key.** The credential directory (`induscode::launch::credentials::PROVIDER_DIRECTORY`) has **14 entries**, each mapping a provider id to its `env_key` + `docs_url`:

| Provider id | Label | Env var |
|---|---|---|
| `anthropic` | Anthropic (Claude) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| `openai` | OpenAI | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `google` | Google Gemini | `GEMINI_API_KEY` |
| `xai` | xAI (Grok) | `XAI_API_KEY` |
| `groq` | Groq | `GROQ_API_KEY` |
| `cerebras` | Cerebras | `CEREBRAS_API_KEY` |
| `mistral` | Mistral | `MISTRAL_API_KEY` |
| `openrouter` | OpenRouter | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| `minimax` | MiniMax | `MINIMAX_API_KEY` |
| `kimi` | Kimi (Moonshot) | `MOONSHOT_API_KEY` |
| `sarvam` | Sarvam | `SARVAM_API_KEY` |
| `krutrim` | Krutrim | `KRUTRIM_API_KEY` |
| `nvidia` | NVIDIA | `NVIDIA_API_KEY` |
| `zai` | Z.ai | `ZAI_API_KEY` |

**Sign in interactively.** `signin`/`signout` are no-session credential commands recognized by `induscode::launch::credentials` (`run_credential_command`), accepting `--provider` / `--account` / `--method <oauth|api-key>` (alias `--api-key` / `--oauth`) / `--list`, treating the first bare positional as the provider. The api key is read with echo muted on a TTY (crossterm raw mode) and wrapped in a `SecretString` immediately. A bare `signin <provider>` appends `--method api-key` (`default_signin_to_api_key`) past the inert OAuth sentinel. Credentials persist to the multi-account `auth.json` vault under `~/.indusagi/agent/`, byte-compatible with the framework's single-record auth store.

```bash
indusr signin anthropic                    # store an Anthropic API key (the default path)
indusr signin openai --account work        # name a stored credential account
indusr signin anthropic --method oauth     # force the browser (OAuth) path
indusr signin anthropic --oauth            # shorthand for --method oauth
indusr signin --list                       # read-only: list saved accounts
indusr signout anthropic                   # remove a stored credential
indusr auth login anthropic                # framework PKCE browser flow (where configured)
indusr auth status [provider]              # show which providers are signed in
indusr auth logout                         # routed to the agent's signout path
```

**Run modes.** A bare `indusr` (or any invocation whose resolved mode is `text`) opens the interactive console (`OutputMode::Text` → `RunnerId::Repl`). `--interactive`/`-i` forces interactive even with a prompt (overrides `--print`). `--resume`/`-r` picks a previous session; `--continue`/`-c` continues the most recent session in this directory. Attach files with `@path` references (`read_file_references`): text files inline into the prompt, images decode to the framework image block; the `--` terminator stops option parsing.

- **One-shot print mode** — `-p`/`--print` runs a single request to settlement, prints only the final result, exits (`OutputMode::Json` → `RunnerId::Oneshot`). The `StdioSink` writes text to stdout, diagnostics to stderr, flushing each write; a closed pipe is swallowed.
- **Headless line-protocol mode** — `--json` (alias `--rpc`) selects a newline-delimited JSON wire (`OutputMode::Rpc` → `RunnerId::Link`). The `StdinSource` does one blocking stdin read per line on a blocking thread, dropping the trailing newline.

**How the mode is derived** (`derive_mode` precedence in `read_invocation`):

| Flags | `OutputMode` | Runner (`RunnerId`) |
|-------|--------------|---------------------|
| `--json` / `--rpc` | `Rpc` | `Link` (line protocol over stdio) |
| `--print` (`-p`) without `--interactive` | `Json` | `Oneshot` |
| anything else (default) | `Text` | `Repl` (interactive ratatui console) |

`--json` wins over `--print`; `--interactive` overrides `--print` to keep `Text`.

**Pick a model.** `-m`/`--model` matches the framework catalog, provider-qualified (`provider/name`) or bare. Pair with `--thinking`; accepted rungs (`THINKING_EFFORTS` / `ThinkingEffort`): `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` (unrecognized values ignored). `--fallback-model` names a model to switch to mid-turn on overload (HTTP 529). With no `-m`, the model falls back to `default_model`/`default_provider` from settings (default provider `anthropic`), then the framework default.

**Browse the model catalog.** `--list-models [filter]` prints an aligned table and exits (handled before boot via `induscode::launch::catalog::print_model_catalog`, sourcing rows from the live facade catalog `RegistrySource`, walking `get_providers()` × `get_models()`). The filter is a plain case-insensitive substring over the `provider/modelId`. Six columns: `Provider`, `Model`, `Context`, `Max Output`, `Thinking`, `Images`. The `mock` echo provider is excluded (`EXCLUDED_PROVIDERS`).

**Where state lives.** Per-user state is under `~/.indusagi/agent/` by default — the agent nests one level deeper than the framework `Locator`: `profile_dir_name` is `.indusagi`, `state_dir_name` is `agent`, so the resolved root is `<home>/.indusagi/agent`. Override with `INDUSAGI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` (`~`-expanded, cwd-relative-aware). The resolved `Workspace` (`induscode::core::create_workspace`):

| Member | Path under profile root | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `settings_path` | `settings.json` | merged user preferences |
| `auth_path` | `auth.json` | the multi-account credential vault |
| `sessions_dir` | `sessions/` | per-cwd transcript directories |
| `models_path` | `models.json` | custom model-catalog overrides |
| `tools_dir` / `bin_dir` | `bin/` | provisioned native helpers (fd / rg) |
| `prompts_dir` | `prompts/` | user-authored prompt / command templates |
| `themes_dir` | `themes/` | user-installed colour themes |
| `export_template_dir` | `export-template/` | HTML transcript-export template |
| `debug_log_path` | `debug.log` | verbose diagnostic log |
| `mcp_config_path` | `mcp-servers.json` | external MCP server config |
| `memory_config_path` | `memory.json` | memory-feature config |
| `composio_config_path` | `composio.json` | Composio-integration config |
| `memory_db_path` | `memory.db` | on-disk memory database |

Settings read through a two-tier `PreferenceStore` (project-over-global-over-default on read; writes land in the project tier `<cwd>/.indusagi/settings.json`). A missing/unreadable/bad-JSON/non-object settings file degrades to the empty record. The `Preferences` record has **24 keys**.

#### Architecture (the layer stack)

The Rust edition is **one merged product crate**: the thirteen former `induscode-*` library crates are plain modules under `src/`, the framework is the single published `indusagi` umbrella crate (the deleted `indusagi-*` path deps). `lib.rs` is the library surface; `bin/main.rs` is the terminal binary; everything else is `pub mod`.

A turn flows down through induscode's modules onto the framework runtime:

| Layer | Module | Built on |
|-------|--------|----------|
| Process entry | `src/bin/main.rs` (the `indusr`/`indusagir` shim) | tokio, stdlib |
| Launch | `induscode::launch` | framework AI + PKCE/transport |
| Boot | `induscode::boot` | `induscode::core`, all subsystems |
| Conductor | `induscode::conductor` | framework runtime |
| Capabilities | `induscode::deck` | framework capabilities |
| Console (UI) | `induscode::console` | framework tui |
| Channels (output) | `induscode::channels` | conductor signals |
| Runtime | `indusagi::runtime` / `indusagi::llmgateway` | framework runtime |

The conductor is the pivot: console and channels are *consumers* of its signal stream and `submit`/`snapshot`/`resume` surface; the deck and framework agent are *assembled into* it at startup by the boot layer's `build_conductor`.

**The two faces.** `lib.rs` declares `pub mod`s for the thirteen subsystems (`addons`, `boot`, `briefing`, `channels`, `conductor`, `console`, `core`, `deck`, `insight`, `launch`, `runtime_bridge`, `transcript_export`, `window_budget`); `bin/main.rs` is two `[[bin]]` targets (`indusr`, `indusagir`) sharing one `async fn main() -> ExitCode`.

`route` runs these checks in verbatim order before the boot handoff:

| Order | Check | Handler |
|-------|-------|---------|
| 1 | `auth` leading verb | `run_auth_subcommand` (`login`/`refresh`/`status`/`help` → framework `run_auth_command`; `logout` → agent `signout`; `status` → agent vault reader) |
| 2 | `--help` / `-h` | `render_usage` + `render_commands_section` |
| 3 | `--version` / `-v` | print `BRAND.app_name VERSION` |
| 4 | unknown leading flag | `eprintln!` + exit `EXIT_USAGE` (`2`) via `unknown_leading_flag` |
| 5 | `signin` / `signout` | `run_agent_credential` over `DiskAuthVault` |
| 6 | `install`/`remove`/`update`/`list`/`config` | `run_package` over the `PreferenceStore` |
| 7 | `--list-models [filter]` | `print_model_catalog` |
| 8 | everything else | `boot_run(rest, production_io())` |

`production_io()` pairs a `StdioSink` with a `StdinSource`.

**Launch layer — the FLAG_SPECS grammar.** The single source of truth is `launch::flags::flag_specs()` — `&[FlagSpec]` walked by both `parser::read_invocation` and `usage::render_usage`, so `--help` never drifts. Each `FlagSpec` carries a canonical `name`, `aliases` (all normalise to `name`, e.g. `--rpc` → `--json`), a `FlagKind` (`Boolean` | `String` | `Number` | `List`), a `FlagGroup` (`Output` | `Model` | `Context` | `Tools` | `Meta`), and a `describe`. The full **18-flag grammar in 5 groups** (declaration order):

| Flag | Aliases | Kind | Group | Purpose |
|------|---------|------|-------|---------|
| `--print` | `-p` | Boolean | Output | Run a single request, print only the result, and exit. |
| `--json` | `--rpc` | Boolean | Output | Speak the headless line protocol for a driving parent process. |
| `--interactive` | `-i` | Boolean | Output | Force the interactive session even when a prompt is supplied. |
| `--model` | `-m` | String | Model | Select the model, provider-qualified or bare (e.g. `provider/name`). |
| `--fallback-model` | — | String | Model | Model to switch to mid-turn when the selected model is overloaded (HTTP 529). |
| `--account` | — | String | Model | Authenticate the run with a named stored credential account. |
| `--thinking` | — | String | Model | Set the reasoning effort (`off`/`minimal`/`low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`; rungs interpolated from `THINKING_EFFORTS`). |
| `--list-models` | — | String | Model | List the available models (optionally substring-filtered) and exit. |
| `--cwd` | — | String | Context | Scope the run to a working directory (default: current). |
| `--system` | — | String | Context | Replace the built-in system prompt with the given text. |
| `--append-system` | — | String | Context | Append extra text after the system prompt. |
| `--resume` | `-r` | Boolean | Context | Pick a previous session to resume. |
| `--continue` | `-c` | Boolean | Context | Continue the most recent session in this directory. |
| `--tools` | — | List | Tools | Allow only the named built-in tools (comma-separated or repeated). |
| `--no-tools` | — | Boolean | Tools | Disable every built-in tool for this run. |
| `--mcp` | — | List | Tools | Attach an external MCP server endpoint (comma-separated or repeated). |
| `--help` | `-h` | Boolean | Meta | Show this usage and exit. |
| `--version` | `-v` | Boolean | Meta | Show the version and exit. |

**The boot pipeline.** `boot_run(argv, io)` (in `boot/mod.rs`) seeds an immutable `BootContext`, folds it through a **five-stage** `BootPipeline` (each `Stage::apply` returns a fresh successor, never mutating in place), dispatches a runner, and **always** drains closables in reverse on the way out:

| Stage | Name | What it does |
|-------|------|--------------|
| 1 | `locate-workspace` | `ensure_dirs(&ctx.workspace)` materialises the profile layout (failed `mkdir` non-fatal). |
| 2 | `apply-upgrades` | Folds the idempotent `apply_upgrades` registry — `fold-credentials-into-secure-auth-file`, `reshelve-loose-transcripts-into-sessions-dir`, `relocate-managed-helper-binaries-to-bin`, `rename-legacy-commands-dir-to-prompts` (each marker-gated, retried next launch). |
| 3 | `build-invocation` | `read_invocation` then `map_invocation` projects the launch `Invocation` onto the boot-routing `Invocation`. |
| 4 | `resolve-resources` | `resolve_startup_resources` best-effort assembles settings/auth/model graph (degrades to `None`). |
| 5 | `select-runner` | A marker/tracing no-op — real dispatch happens after the pipeline. |

`map_invocation` maps `Rpc → Link`, `Json → Oneshot`, `Text → Repl`. `drain_closables` runs every teardown latest-first, swallowing failures; `BootContext::closables` is a `Mutex<Vec<Closable>>`.

**Runner dispatch** is a total table lookup — `registry()` returns `RunnerRegistry::new([ReplRunner, OneShotRunner, LinkRunner])`; `select` returns the first whose `accepts` matches `inv.mode`, falling back to the **first** (`ReplRunner`) so a bare command line always lands interactive:

| Runner | `id()` | Behaviour |
|--------|--------|-----------|
| `ReplRunner` | `RunnerId::Repl` | Builds the conductor, honours `--resume`/`--continue` via `apply_resume`, then `mount_console(conductor, opts)` behind the `tui` feature. Headless (`--no-default-features`) build reports the surface needs `tui` and exits non-zero (`EXIT_REPL_UNAVAILABLE` = `1`). |
| `OneShotRunner` | `RunnerId::Oneshot` | One non-interactive run to stdout via `run_oneshot` over a `ChannelContext` — clean text or NDJSON; no input exits `EXIT_NO_INPUT` (`2`). |
| `LinkRunner` | `RunnerId::Link` | Reads framed JSON-RPC lines, dispatches through `session_ops` via `dispatch`, frames a correlated `Reply` back via NDJSON `encode_line`. EOF exits `0`; blank/malformed lines tolerated. |

**How a session is assembled** — all three runners call `build_conductor(ctx)` (the Rust analogue of TS `buildSessionConductor`): (1) **Model** — `resolve_model_id` resolves `--model` ▸ saved `settings.default_model` ▸ an authenticated provider's model ▸ catalog fallback, seeds `AgentConfig::new`; thinking threads `resolve_thinking` (`minimal`/`xhigh` fold onto framework `Low`/`Max`). (2) **Tools** — `build_session_tools` calls `provision_deck(Profile::All, ctx)`, honours `--tools` (case-insensitive, `_`/`-`-stripped via `canon_tool_name`) and `--no-tools`, then `graft`s `--mcp` (or auto-discovered) servers and `<cwd>/.indus/addons` tools + interceptors; per-session read-state + checkpoint stores enforce read-before-edit and snapshot/rewind. (3) **System prompt** — `compose_session_briefing` (`--system` replaces, `--append-system` appends). (4) **Permissions** — `resolve_permission_policy` reads project-then-global tiers into deny/ask/allow `PermissionRule`s + a `PermissionMode`; when anything is enforceable, the deck is wrapped in a `GatedToolBox`. (5) **Credentials** — `build_key_resolver` builds an `--account`-scoped `KeyResolver` (requested ▸ default ▸ first), stamping the key onto each request's `StreamOptions::api_key` — no `unsafe` env mutation (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`). (6) **The conductor** — `Conductor::new(config, LoopDeps { … store: SessionStore::new(sessions_dir), key_resolver, fallback_model_id, plans_dir, workspace, diagnostics, .. })` wraps exactly one framework agent loop; the cwd-scoped `sessions_dir` (`session_scope_dir_for`) is the same directory resume reads and overlays list.

**Module map** (grouped by concern, reached as `induscode::<module>`):

*Launch & lifecycle:* `launch` (FLAG_SPECS + parser + render_usage, `@file` `gather_attachments` inliner, multi-account `DiskAuthVault` + `run_credential_command`, the **three OAuth flows** — Anthropic / OpenAI Codex / GitHub Copilot, the `ModelRegistry` catalog over `ModelCard`, picker data); `boot` (`boot_run`, the five-stage pipeline, `apply_upgrades`, the total `RunnerRegistry`, `build_conductor`, `resolve_startup_resources`, addon wiring, `drain_closables`); `core` (the `BRAND` record — `app_name` `indusagi`, bins `["indus", "indusagi"]`, env prefix `INDUSAGI`, profile dir `.indusagi`, `env_profile_dir` `INDUSAGI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`; `VERSION`; `create_workspace`/`ensure_dirs`; the two-tier `PreferenceStore`; `SessionLibrary`; kit helpers).

*Session core:* `conductor` (the `Conductor` over one agent loop, the product `SessionSignal` stream, branchable transcript store, model catalog/matcher, `create_permission_gate`/`GatedToolBox`, `PermissionMode` cycling, post-edit `DiagnosticsEngine`, plan-mode, `submit`/`snapshot`/`resume`); `deck` (the `Capability` catalog, `provision_deck`, `app_novel_cards()` appended after framework built-ins — todo / bg-process / task / saas / memory / the two plan-mode markers `enter_plan_mode`+`exit_plan_mode`, `CheckpointingCard`, `DeckFramework`, the event-sourced MCP bridge ledger `load_mcp_config`/`attach_bridge_capabilities`); `window_budget` (token measurement, slice planning, the transcript condense engine feeding `/compact` and auto-compaction); `briefing` (`compose_briefing_with_options`, the macro model, the Agent-Skills card loader).

*Surfaces & I/O:* `console` (the ratatui shell — pure reducer, theme engine, slash catalog, input/intent/completion, overlay dialogs, `mount_console`); `channels` (`ChannelContext`/`LineSink`/`OneshotRequest`/`OneshotShape`, `run_oneshot`, the `session_ops` JSON-RPC registry + `dispatch`, the NDJSON `encode_line` framer); `transcript_export` (the SGR-to-HTML painter, the WCAG-luminance theme bridge with pulldown-cmark + syntect, the page-shell template, `publish_transcript`).

*Integrations & extension:* `runtime_bridge` (the `bridge:<adapter>` endpoint convention, the normalized event union, child-transport boundary, broker/route surface); `addons` (the addon manifest/surface, the colon-named hook taxonomy + dispatcher, the `ToolInterceptor` chain, `AddonCommand` tools/commands, the module loader wired by `boot::addon_wiring`); `insight` (a thin wrapper over framework tracing + an in-memory collector sink + NDJSON replay readers).
