The `console` and `addons` modules always compile (no `#[cfg]` gate); the `tui` feature only forwards to the framework render layer and gates the `mount_repl` body. Three off-by-default features tune the build: `mimalloc`, `swarm` (boot delegate-runner stage), `composio` (the `saas` card backend). The framework boundary is sharp — the conductor drives one `indusagi::runtime` loop and re-emits a stable `SessionSignal` stream; the deck projects `Capability` into the framework `indusagi::runtime::ToolBox`; the console renders over framework `tui`; launch builds on `indusagi::llmgateway` PKCE/transport primitives and `indusagi::shell_app::auth_cli`; boot ports the framework `indusagi::shell_app::boot`/`runners` templates.

#### Console overview

The interactive console is the Rust edition's product shell — the ratatui REPL a TTY launch hands a session to. It is a deliberate re-architecture of the TS Ink/React surface (ports `indus-code-rebuild/src/console/**`, ≈5,826 LOC) onto the frozen `indusagi-tui` / `indusagi-tui-render` immediate-mode framework — **not** a line-by-line translation. The Ink `useReducer` + `conductor.subscribe` design becomes four cooperating pieces:

- **One immutable `ConsoleState`** — every observable property of the surface; live session data (messages, usage, bound model) is deliberately *absent*, projected from the conductor snapshot on every draw.
- **One pure `console_reducer`** — `(ConsoleState, ConsoleEvent) -> ConsoleState`, an exhaustive `match` (no `_` arm), no I/O.
- **Immediate-mode `view`** — `draw(frame, &state)` over ratatui, flicker-free streaming markdown via a stable-prefix cache, inline viewport (not alt-screen).
- **A typed `ConsoleEvent` enum** — the closed `domain:verb` action union the reducer folds.

`mount_console` is the boot entry: the `ReplRunner` TTY branch calls *into* this crate. The subsystem performs exactly one terminal takeover (`ratatui::init`).

**Module map:**

| Module | File | Role |
|--------|------|------|
| `state` | `console/state.rs` | `ConsoleState` + `ViewRow` / `ModalKind` / `ThemeScheme` value types |
| `events` | `console/events.rs` | `ConsoleEvent` action union + `type_tag` discriminants |
| `reducer` | `console/reducer.rs` | the pure total fold `console_reducer` + `init_console_state` |
| `input` | `console/input.rs` | keymap, chord latch, paste coalescing, completion, `InputController` |
| `mount` | `console/mount.rs` | `mount_console`, the `SignalCursor` turn projection, the live ratatui loop |
| `tool_row` | `console/tool_row.rs` | projects a settled `ToolEnd` into a `ToolCard` |
| `slash` | `console/slash.rs` | the slash-command registry, dispatch, effects |
| `theme` | `console/theme.rs` | maps a `ThemeScheme` to a resolved framework adapter |
| `overlays` | `console/overlays/` | the **13** modal overlays keyed by `ModalKind` |
| `view` | `console/view/` | the immediate-mode painter (banner, chrome, composer, transcript, diff, markdown) |

**Reaching the console.** `mount_console(conductor, MountConsoleOptions { … }).await` — everything but the conductor is optional. `MountConsoleOptions` fields: `scheme` (`midnight`/`daylight`/`midnight-cb`/`daylight-cb`; `None` → default), `initial_input`, `initial_images`, `verbose`, `cwd` (footer + roots `@path` completion), `auth_path` (the `auth.json` sign-in/out overlays read/write via `DiskAuthVault`; filters `/model` to authenticated providers), `sessions_dir` (read by `/resume`, `/tree`, `/branch`, `/timeline`), `prefs` (the two-tier `PreferenceStore`). Returns `MountResult { clean: bool }`. Off a TTY it refuses cleanly (it would panic in raw mode), mapped to the headless fallback exit.

**The state backbone** — `ConsoleState` fields: `rows: Vec<ViewRow>`, `blocks: Vec<UiDisplayBlock>`, `buffer: String`, `caret: usize` (**chars, not bytes**), `history: Vec<String>`, `history_at: Option<usize>`, `stash: String`, `modal: ModalState`, `modal_selected: usize`, `status: Option<StatusMessage>`, `scheme: ThemeScheme`, `show_reasoning: bool`, `show_images: bool`, `expand_tools: bool` (Ctrl+O), `busy: bool`, `tick: u64`. `default()` seeds empty collections, `caret 0`, `history_at None`, `modal NO_MODAL`, `scheme Midnight`, `show_reasoning false`, `show_images true`, `busy false`, `tick 0`.

A `ViewRow { id, kind, text, run_id, output, diff }` is identity-stable (a streaming row keeps its `id` while `text` grows). `ViewRowKind` is `Prompt` / `Answer` / `Reason` / `ToolRun` / `Notice`; `RowDiff { path, old, new }` mirrors the conductor's `ToolDiff`.

**The reducer** is pure and total — input taken by value (move-enforced "never mutate the input"); the exhaustive `match` is the Rust analogue of the TS `const _never: never` guard. Transition families: composer edits (`buffer:*`/`caret:*`, caret clamped to `[0, len_chars]`), history recall (`history:*`, `push_history` ignores blanks + immediate dupes), transcript view (`rows:*`/`block:append`/`blocks:clear`, `patch_row` grows by id, `patch_tool_row` reconciles a settled `ToolRun`), and overlays/status/theme/toggles/busy. `BusySet(true)` also clears a sticky status toast. **The char-offset hazard:** `caret` is a char offset; every splice/erase walks `char_indices` (`byte_at`, `splice_at`, `with_buffer`, `erase_prev`/`erase_next`); tests pin this with multi-byte buffers (`héllo`, inserting `ü`).

**The event union** — `ConsoleEvent` carries the `domain:verb` discriminant (via `type_tag()`). 26 variants including the two `modal:select*` cursor verbs added over the 22 ported variants: `BufferSet`, `BufferInsert`, `BufferErasePrev`, `BufferEraseNext`, `CaretMove`, `CaretJump`, `HistoryPush`, `HistoryBack`, `HistoryForward`, `RowsSet`, `RowsAppend`, `RowsPatch`, `RowsPatchTool`, `BlockAppend`, `BlocksClear`, `ModalOpen`, `ModalClose`, `ModalSelectMove`, `ModalSelectSet`, `StatusSet`, `StatusClear`, `SchemeSet`, `ToggleReasoning`, `ToggleImages`, `ToggleExpandTools`, `BusySet`, `Tick`. `ConsoleEvent` is `Debug`-only (embeds non-`Serialize` framework types); snapshot tests assert on `Debug`.

**Input handling.** `read_key(input, &KeyChord) -> ConsoleIntent` is a pure memoryless classifier (control combos/named keys win over raw text, so `Ctrl+U` never types "u"). `KeyChord::from_crossterm` folds `BackTab` → `tab + shift` and `Delete`/DEL/BS → erase-backward. The chord bindings:

| Chord | Verb / effect |
|-------|---------------|
| `Ctrl+C` | `FlowInterrupt` — abort a busy turn; idle, leaves |
| `Ctrl+Z` | `FlowSuspend` — background (SIGTSTP) |
| `Ctrl+U` | `EditClearLine`; twice on empty buffer → `Clear2` (request exit) |
| `Ctrl+A` / `Ctrl+E` | `NavHome` / `NavEnd` |
| `Ctrl+J` | `TextNewline` — soft newline |
| `Ctrl+N` / `Ctrl+P` | `FlowCycleModel` — rotate the bound model |
| `Ctrl+T` | `ModelCycleThinking` — step the reasoning ladder |
| `Ctrl+V` | `InputPasteImage` — stage a clipboard image |
| `Ctrl+G` | `InputExternalEditor` — hand the buffer to `$EDITOR` |
| `Ctrl+R` | `OverlayOpen(Sessions)` — session picker |
| `Ctrl+L` | `OverlayOpen(Models)` — model picker |
| `Ctrl+O` | `ViewExpandTools` — toggle full tool-output |
| `Alt+Up` | `QueueDequeue` — pull newest queued input back |
| `Enter` / `Shift+Enter` | `FlowSubmit` / `TextNewline` |
| `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | `FlowAccept` / `ModeCyclePermission` |
| `Esc` | `FlowDismiss`; twice within window → `Dismiss2` (open tree) |

`advance_chord` layers a double-tap latch (`CHORD_WINDOW_MS` = 600 ms); `InputController::expire_chord` resets a stale latch synchronously. **Paste coalescing:** `classify_paste` (defaults: 8 newlines or 800 chars) returns `Inline`/`Coalesce`; a large chunk hides behind `[Pasted text #N +K lines]`, minted into an immutable `PasteVault`, rewritten by `expand_markers` at submit; bracketed paste arrives as one `Event::Paste`, non-bracketing terminals fall back to a per-char burst (`PASTE_BURST_GAP_MS` = 24 ms). **Completion:** `complete_at` routes on the active token — a `/` only at buffer-start yields slash completion, an `@`/path stem yields directory completion (dirs-first, alphabetical, trailing-slash, via an injected `DirReader` whose errors collapse to empty). **`InputController`** returns `InputEffect`s (`Edit`, `Submit`, `OpenOverlay`, `AcceptCompletion`, `MoveHighlight`, `HistoryBack/Forward`, `Interrupt`, `Dismiss`, `Suspend`, `CycleModel`, `CyclePermission`, `TogglePlan`, `CycleThinking`, `ExpandTools`, `ToggleReasoning`, `PasteImage`, `ExternalEditor`, `Dequeue`, `DoubleDismiss`, `RequestExit`, `None`); `refresh_completion` resets the highlight only when `(buffer, caret)` actually changed (the "BUG A" fix). With a completion menu open, `Enter` on a slash row accepts *and* submits in one press (`/logout` runs on one Enter); an `@file` row only accepts.

**Signal cursor & live turn projection.** `SignalCursor` (`console/mount.rs`) projects the conductor `SessionSignal` stream into rows, tracking which streaming `Answer`/`Reason` rows are "live" so deltas grow the *same* row in place. `project(&SessionSignal) -> Vec<ConsoleEvent>` is pure; `apply_signal` is the shared application path:

| `SessionSignal` | Projection |
|-----------------|------------|
| `Prompt { text }` | Close open streams, append a `Prompt` row, `BusySet(true)`. |
| `Text { delta }` | Grow the open `Answer` row (`rows:patch`), or open one. |
| `Thinking { delta }` | Grow/open the `Reason` row (gated by `show_reasoning`). |
| `ToolStart { id, name }` | Append a `ToolRun` row `"> <FriendlyTitle> (running)"`, tracked by `run_id`. |
| `ToolEnd { id, name, ok, output, diff }` | Build the settled card and patch the same row (or append if pruned). |
| `TurnEnd { .. }` / `Idle` | Close streams, `BusySet(false)`. |
| `Fault { fault }` | Close streams, `BusySet(false)`, set status (calm "Stopped" for `Aborted`, else "Turn faulted"). |
| `Compacted` | Append a muted `Notice` "Context condensed to fit the window." |
| `Persisted { .. }` / `Queue { .. }` | No transcript surface. |

`build_tool_card(name, ok, output, has_diff, show_images) -> ToolCard` reuses the framework `describe_tool_source` (`indusagi::tui_render::utils::tool_display`) — the same per-tool switch (read/write/edit/ls/find/grep/bash/task/todo/default). The status marker is `=` on success, `!` on error, `>` while running.

**The view tree.** `console/view/`: the transcript scrolls inline (not alt-screen), streaming markdown flicker-free via a stable-prefix cache.
- *Banner* (`view/banner.rs`) — the six-row "INDUS CODE" ANSI-Shadow block-figlet (`WORDMARK_ROWS`), accent-tinted via a static `row_gradient`, the `indus console  vVERSION` brand line, a `welcome_line` greeting; prepended to the transcript and scrolls with content.
- *Transcript* (`view/transcript.rs`) — `build_transcript_lines` (pure), `render_transcript` paints the last `area.height` lines. `Prompt` (bold accent `You`), `Answer` (bold accent `Assistant` + `render_streaming` with syntect), `Reason` (dim `…`, skipped when off), `ToolRun` (dim `⏵` + card header + body clamped to `TOOL_BODY_COLLAPSED_LINES` = 10 with a `... N more line(s)` footer, full when Ctrl+O; colored unified diff for edit/write when expanded), `Notice` (dim `›`).
- *Streaming markdown* (`view/markdown.rs`) — `StreamingMarkdownCache` over `render_streaming` / `last_stable_boundary` (monotonic); `render_stream` is the un-cached one-shot.
- *Diff* (`view/diff.rs`) — `render_file_diff(old, new, path, theme)`; the framework does the line diff (`CONTEXT_LINES=3`, word-level spans, gutter, `diffAddedBg`/`diffRemovedBg` truecolor tints), this adds the header (`path  +N -M`) and `DIFF_INDENT`.
- *Composer* (`view/composer.rs`) — a rounded box (`borderMuted → accent → gray` fallthrough), `› ` glyph, caret drawn by inverting the cell (`Modifier::REVERSED`), up to `SUGGESTION_WINDOW` (8) completion rows (highlighted `▸ label` in accent); when busy the text dims but the caret stays legible.
- *Chrome* (`view/chrome.rs`) — `WorkingIndicator` (braille `SPINNER_FRAMES`, a rotating word from `WORKING_WORDS` (**30** of them) via `pick_word` or a `phase_label` `tooling → "Running tools"` / `condensing → "Compacting context"`, an elapsed clock, an "esc to interrupt" hint; height 0 when idle); `StatusBar` (the framework `StatusLine` toast, an optional `● permission: <label>` badge via `permission_badge` — `bypass-permissions` red, `plan` cyan, `accept-edits` yellow, `default` grey — and the framework `Footer` cwd/branch/model/token-cost-context strip, run with `show_busy_text=false`).

**The mount loop** (the `live` module, gated behind `tui`). After taking over the terminal (bracketed paste on, `ratatui::init` installing a panic hook), each iteration: (1) drain + project signals via `apply_signal`; (2) drain approvals into a serialising `ApprovalQueue`, mirroring the head into the `Approval` modal (one at a time); (3) refresh completion; (4) draw the frame (bottom-anchored `Layout::vertical`, `project_snapshot` resolving the bound model id to a `provider/name` + `ContextUsage`); (5) poll input with a 40 ms `POLL_TIMEOUT`; (6) route the key (modal-open keys route to the overlay; otherwise through `InputController`). A submit is routed by `submit_line`: clear + push to history, then `slash::dispatch_slash` — a `NotSlash` line goes to the conductor via `spawn_submit`; `Handled`/`Submit` drains its `SlashEffect`s; `Unknown(name)` raises a warning toast. Slash effects are **not** sent to the model.

#### Slash commands

A typed line like `/model`, `/resume`, or `/export out.html` is parsed, resolved against an ordered registry, and run as a thin **synchronous** handler that touches the world only by pushing typed `SlashEffect` values. The whole machine lives in one file, `crates/induscode/src/console/slash.rs` (the TS `console/slash/{contract,resolve,registry,shared,builtins,transcript,workbench,integrations,dynamic}.ts` split + the `TerminalConsole.tsx` dispatch, folded into numbered sections). No `if`-ladder: every command is one row in `build_catalog`.

The `SlashCommand` trait: `name`, `summary`, `aliases` (default `&[]`), `family` (default `None`), `takes_args` (default `false`), `run(&self, ctx: &mut SlashContext) -> SlashOutcome`. `run` is **synchronous** — the TS async-only-because-of-React closures become `SlashEffect::Conductor` requests the host loop performs.

`SlashOutcome` is `Handled` / `Prompt(String)` / `Unknown` (plus the const `HANDLED`). `SlashEffect` (`Debug + Clone`, not `PartialEq`): `Event(ConsoleEvent)`, `OpenModal { kind, payload }`, `CloseModal`, `Status(StatusMessage)`, `SetBuffer(String)`, `AppendBlock(UiDisplayBlock)`, `RequestExit`, `Conductor(ConductorAction)`. `SlashModalPayload`: `SignInProvider(String)`, `ScopedModels(ScopedModelsIntent)`, `Plugin { surface, title, text }`.

**Resolution pipeline** (three pure functions): `looks_like_slash` (after trimming, must start with `/` (`SLASH_PREFIX`) and match the hand-rolled `COMMAND_TOKEN` shape `^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9:-]*(?:\s|$)`; a second slash disqualifies, so `/`, `//comment`, `/usr/local/bin` fall through); `parse_slash` (token to first whitespace, lower-cased; arg tail outer-trimmed); `resolve_slash` → `SlashResolution`:

| Outcome | Meaning | Dispatcher action |
|---------|---------|-------------------|
| `NotSlash` | not command-shaped | normal prompt or `!`/`!!` escape |
| `Match { command, args }` | a row owns the token | `command.run(ctx)` |
| `Miss { name }` | command-shaped, unowned | surface "Unknown command: /name" |

Resolution is case-insensitive. An alias resolves to its canonical row (`/fork` → `branch`). No `regex` dependency — `COMMAND_TOKEN` is hand-rolled in `matches_command_token`.

**The catalog** — `build_catalog(&DynamicCommandSources)` concatenates three static groups then splices dynamic rows (dropping any token that shadows a built-in, the `reserved_tokens` guard):

```
transcript_commands (12)  ->  workbench_commands (9)  ->  integration_commands (8)
                          ->  dynamic /skill:<name> rows  ->  dynamic /<template> rows
```

That is **29 static commands** (12 + 9 + 8) plus *N* dynamic rows; counting aliases there are about **41 resolvable static tokens**. `DEFAULT_SLASH_REGISTRY` is a `LazyLock<SlashRegistry>` over `static_commands()` (no dynamic rows) for pure derivations and `/help`.

*Transcript & session control (12 rows):*

| Command | Aliases | Args | What it does |
|---------|---------|------|--------------|
| `/clear` | `reset` | — | Wipe view (`rows:set` empty, `blocks:clear`, `status:clear`), toast, request `ConductorAction::NewSession`. |
| `/new` | — | — | Identical to `/clear` (same `run_clear`). |
| `/summarize-context` | `condense`, `compact` | yes | Busy toast + `ConductorAction::Condense { guidance }` (trailing text = optional guidance). |
| `/resume` | `sessions` | — | Open the persisted-session list (`ModalKind::Sessions`). |
| `/session` | — | — | `ConductorAction::StatsBlock { cost_only: false }` — full stats block. |
| `/cost` | `usage` | — | `ConductorAction::StatsBlock { cost_only: true }` — compact cost table. |
| `/branch` | `fork` | — | Branch from a prior turn (`ModalKind::UserTurns`). |
| `/timeline` | `tree` | — | Navigate the transcript tree (`ModalKind::Tree`). |
| `/name` | — | yes | `ConductorAction::SetSessionName`, or bare → `ReportSessionName`. |
| `/reload` | — | — | Busy toast + `ConductorAction::Reload`. |
| `/quit` | — | — | `ctx.request_exit()`. |
| `/exit` | — | — | Same as `/quit`. |

*Workbench: pickers, help, diagnostics (9 rows):*

| Command | Aliases | Args | What it does |
|---------|---------|------|--------------|
| `/model` | `models` | — | Single-model picker (`ModalKind::Models`). |
| `/models-for` | `scoped-models` | yes | Edit/show/reset per-scope routing (a family; `ModalKind::ScopedModels`). |
| `/settings` | — | — | Settings overlay (`ModalKind::Settings`). |
| `/help` | `?` | — | Append a `Commands` block (from `DEFAULT_SLASH_REGISTRY`). |
| `/keys` | `hotkeys` | — | Append a `Keyboard shortcuts` table from the **22-row** `HOTKEYS` map. |
| `/whats-new` | `changelog` | — | Append a `What's new` block (`CHANGELOG_FALLBACK`). |
| `/plan` | — | — | `ConductorAction::TogglePlanMode` (read-only research; mutating tools blocked). |
| `/thinking` | — | — | `ConductorAction::CycleThinkingLevel` (off → low → medium → off). |
| `/debug` | — | — | `ConsoleEvent::ToggleReasoning` + `ConductorAction::WriteDebugLog`. |

*Integrations: auth, MCP, memory, composio, IO (8 rows):*

| Command | Aliases | Args | Family | What it does |
|---------|---------|------|--------|--------------|
| `/login` | — | yes | — | Sign-in launcher (`ModalKind::SignIn`); `/login <provider>` threads `SignInProvider`. |
| `/logout` | — | — | — | Sign-out confirmation (`ModalKind::SignOut`). |
| `/mcp` | — | yes | — | `status` (default) / `connect` / `reconnect` / `disconnect` / `tools` → `ConductorAction::Mcp { verb }`. |
| `/memory` | — | yes | `memory` | verbs `status`, `on`, `off`, `tools` (`ModalKind::Plugin`). |
| `/composio` | — | yes | `composio` | verbs `status`, `accounts`, `tools`, `connect`, `enable` (`ModalKind::Plugin`). |
| `/copy` | — | — | — | `ConductorAction::CopyLastReply`. |
| `/export` | — | yes | — | `ConductorAction::ExportTranscript { path }` — HTML only. |
| `/share` | — | — | — | `ConductorAction::ShareTranscript` — export then publish a secret GitHub gist. |

`/composio` needs `COMPOSIO_API_KEY` (else a warn toast + plugin overlay carrying `COMPOSIO_NO_KEY`). `/memory on|off` flips only the reported active flag — it does not detach the `memory` tool.

**Dynamic rows** are *discovered* from the briefing layer's `DynamicCommandSources { skills: Vec<SkillCard>, templates: Vec<Macro> }` via `build_dynamic_commands` (skills first, namespaced under `skill:`, then templates; self-collisions suppressed first-wins). `/skill:<name>` (`SkillCommand`, family `skill`, `takes_args`) mints `<skill name="..." location="...">body</skill>` via `skill_invocation_block` (the trailing arg is the body, XML chars escaped by `escape_attr`; summary clamped at `SUMMARY_BUDGET = 88` chars). `/<template>` (`TemplateCommand`, family `template`, `takes_args`) expands the macro via `apply_macros` (`$1`/`$2` positional, `$ARGUMENTS` whole-tail). Both return `SlashOutcome::Prompt`.

The authoritative order-preserving catalog listing (pinned by `catalog_listing_snapshot`, format `/<name> (<aliases>)  [<family>]  <summary>`):

```text
/clear (reset)  [-]  Clear the conversation and start a new session
/new  [-]  Start a fresh session
/summarize-context (condense,compact)  [-]  Condense the conversation context
/resume (sessions)  [-]  Resume a persisted session
/session  [-]  Show live session statistics (ids, counts, tokens, cost)
/cost (usage)  [-]  Show session cost and token usage
/branch (fork)  [-]  Branch the transcript from a prior turn
/timeline (tree)  [-]  Navigate the transcript tree
/name  [-]  Name the session, or show the current name
/reload  [-]  Reload session resources
/quit  [-]  Leave the interactive console
/exit  [-]  Leave the interactive console
/model (models)  [-]  Switch the model bound to this session
/models-for (scoped-models)  [models-for]  Edit, show, or reset per-scope model routing
/settings  [-]  Open the settings overlay
/help (?)  [-]  List the available commands
/keys (hotkeys)  [-]  Show the keyboard shortcut map
/whats-new (changelog)  [-]  Show what changed in this build
/plan  [-]  Toggle plan mode (read-only research; mutating tools are blocked)
/thinking  [-]  Cycle thinking effort level (off → low → medium → off)
/debug  [-]  Write a session diagnostics log and toggle verbose view
/login  [-]  Sign in to a model provider.
/logout  [-]  Sign out of a model provider.
/mcp  [-]  Manage MCP servers and their tools.
/memory  [memory]  Inspect and toggle the working-memory capability.
/composio  [composio]  Connect and inspect Composio app bridges.
/copy  [-]  Copy the last reply to the clipboard.
/export  [-]  Export the transcript to an HTML file.
/share  [-]  Share the session as a secret GitHub gist.
/skill:commit-helper  [skill]  a test skill
/review-pr  [template]  the review-pr template (project)
```

**Family commands.** A command with sub-verbs (`/models-for`, `/memory`, `/composio`) is a `FamilyCommand` over a `&'static [SubCommand]` table; `FamilyCommand::run` calls `split_verb` then `subs.iter().find(...)`. A bare verb emits a usage warn; an unknown verb emits `/<family>: unrecognised action "<verb>".` The `family` module declares `COMPOSIO`, `MEMORY`, `SCOPED_MODELS` (`models-for`), `THEME`, `SKILL`, `TEMPLATE` labels — `theme` is declared for parity but **no `/theme` command ships** (the scheme picker is reached via `/settings`).

**The registry** — `SlashRegistry` is an ordered `Vec<Box<dyn SlashCommand>>` + a derived `HashMap<String, usize>` token→slot. `build` **panics** on any duplicate token; `find` is canonical-or-alias case-insensitive; `match_prefix` returns deduped completion candidates in registry order (empty partial → whole list).

**Dispatch** — `dispatch_slash(line, &registry) -> DispatchResult` (`NotSlash` / `Unknown(String)` / `Handled { effects }` / `Submit { text, effects }`). `apply_slash_effects` folds each into the reducer (`Event` verbatim, `OpenModal` → `ModalOpen`, `CloseModal`, `Status` → `StatusSet`, `SetBuffer` → `BufferSet`, `AppendBlock` → `BlockAppend`), with `RequestExit` returning `Flow::Exit` and `Conductor` deferred to `apply_conductor_action`.

`ConductorAction`: `NewSession`, `Condense { guidance }`, `SetSessionName`, `Reload`, `TogglePlanMode`, `CycleThinkingLevel`, `WriteDebugLog`, `StatsBlock { cost_only }`, `ReportSessionName`, `CopyLastReply`, `ExportTranscript { path }`, `ShareTranscript`, `Mcp { verb }`.

Parity notes: **29 static commands** (the 9-row workbench group adds `/cost`, `/plan`, `/thinking` over the 7-row Python edition); every handler is synchronous (the inverse of the Python edition where each is `async`); `/export` is HTML only.

#### Dialogs & overlays

The console raises **thirteen** modal overlays over the transcript. An overlay is a kind recorded in `ConsoleState.modal` (`ModalState { kind, payload }`) that the per-frame draw mirrors onto the framework `DialogStack`; the reducer is the single source of truth. Each overlay is the **render half** of a host-driven flow — a leaf module owns pure projections + a `draw_*` painter, while binding/`await`/side effects are the host's job. `mod.rs` declares one leaf per kind:

| Kind | Overlay | Module | Painter / widget |
|------|---------|--------|------------------|
| `None` | inert — composer has focus | — | — |
| `Settings` | the settings list | `overlays::settings` | `draw_settings` |
| `Models` | single-model picker | `overlays::models` | `draw_models` |
| `ScopedModels` | per-scope model picker | `overlays::scoped_models` | `draw_scoped_models` |
| `Theme` | colour-scheme picker | `overlays::theme` | `draw_theme` |
| `Sessions` | session resume / list browser | `overlays::sessions` | `draw_sessions` |
| `Tree` | transcript-tree navigator | `overlays::tree` | `draw_tree` |
| `UserTurns` | prior-user-turn fork picker | `overlays::user_turns` | `draw_user_turns` |
| `SignIn` | provider sign-in launcher | `overlays::signin` | `build_login_dialog` |
| `SignOut` | sign-out confirmation | `overlays::signout` | `build_logout_dialog` |
| `Oauth` | in-flight OAuth / api-key entry | `overlays::oauth` | framework `OAuthDialog` |
| `Plugin` | host/plugin-supplied surface | `overlays::plugin` | `PluginDialog` (bespoke) |
| `Approval` | tool-permission prompt | `overlays::approval` (+ `approval_queue`, `approval_resolver`) | `ApprovalDialog` (bespoke) |

Only **five** kinds carry data (`Approval`, `Oauth`, `Plugin`, `ScopedModels`, `SignIn`) via the typed `ModalPayload` (Rust has no `unknown`); the rest never construct a payload. `transition_modal(ModalKind::None, _)` returns the inert `NO_MODAL`.

The painters render frozen framework dialogs from `indusagi::tui_render::components::dialogs` (`ModelDialog`, `ScopedModelsDialog`, `SettingsDialog`, `ThemeDialog`, `SessionDialog`, `TreeDialog`, `UserMessageDialog`, `LoginDialog`, `OAuthDialog`); the two the framework has no widget for (`PluginDialog`, `ApprovalDialog`) are bespoke over `DialogFrame` + `WindowedList`. The render-half contract is three-part: an `is_active(state) -> bool` guard; **pure projections pre-fetched before the push** (a synchronous `Dialog::handle_key` cannot `await`, so I/O-backed lists are pre-fetched); a `draw_*` painter that builds a fresh dialog each draw, seeded with the host's shared `modal_selected` cursor (re-clamped), staying pure/I/O-free.

**Picker overlays.**
- *Model picker (`Models`)* — paints over the live `indusagi/ai` facade catalog — **708 models across 24 providers** (`mock` excluded). Projections: `catalog()`, `authenticated_providers(auth_path)`, `catalog_for`, `auth_filter`, `bound_index`, `provider_for`, `draw_models`. `authenticated_providers` reads the nested `auth.json` vault unioned with every provider whose api-key env var holds a non-empty value (so env-only users aren't filtered out). Empty→all fallback: when no provider is authenticated, the whole catalog shows. On selection the host binds via the conductor's `select_model`, persists it (`persist_default_model`), toasts, and closes; Esc leaves untouched. Shared by `/model` and the first-run startup picker.
- *Scoped models (`ScopedModels`)* — edits the per-scope `enabledModels` preference (empty = every model enabled). `seed_selection` / `collapse_selection` round-trip ("all selected" collapses back to `[]`). The `{intent:"reset"}` path is a planned `ConsoleEffect::ResetScopedModels` (not yet materialized). The per-scope **save is deferred** — Enter currently just closes (needs an as-yet-unthreaded `PreferenceStore`). Carried by `ModalPayload::ScopedModels(ScopedModelsRef)` (opaque marker).
- *Theme picker (`Theme`)* — four schemes from a static catalog in listing order; **preview-before-commit** (`scheme_index` seeds the highlight, `scheme_at` maps a row back; Enter commits + persists `colourScheme`, Esc reverts). See Theming below.
- *Settings (`Settings`)* — a value-based `SettingsItem` catalog of **15 rows** in fixed listing order. `settings_items(value_of)` binds each row's live value via the host's lookup; `next_value` computes the wrapping advance the framework `SettingsDialog` applies on Enter; the host commits via `apply_settings_row` → `stage_setting` (dialog stays open after a cycle; Esc closes). Vocab consts: `TOGGLE_VALUES`, `SCHEME_VALUES`, `DELIVERY_VALUES`, `PADDING_VALUES`. The 15 rows:

| Row key | Label | Values |
|---------|-------|--------|
| `colourScheme` | Colour scheme | `midnight`, `daylight`, `midnight-cb`, `daylight-cb` |
| `showImages` | Show images | on/off |
| `imageAutoResize` | Auto-resize images | on/off |
| `blockImages` | Block images | on/off |
| `showReasoning` | Show reasoning | on/off |
| `enableSkillCommands` | Skill commands | on/off |
| `steeringMode` | Steering mode | `all`, `one-at-a-time` |
| `followUpMode` | Follow-up mode | `all`, `one-at-a-time` |
| `autoCompact` | Auto-compact | on/off |
| `collapseChangelog` | Collapse changelog | on/off |
| `quietStartup` | Quiet startup | on/off |
| `logoSweep` | Logo sweep | on/off |
| `reducedMotion` | Reduced motion | on/off |
| `showHardwareCursor` | Hardware cursor | on/off |
| `editorPaddingX` | Editor padding | `0`–`3` |

**Session overlays** each project the app session vocabulary onto a framework shape and pre-fetch before the push.
- *Session browser (`Sessions`)* — `to_session_info` maps a `SavedSession` onto a framework `SessionInfo` (missing `last_modified` → `0`, preview → `first_message`, path stringified; `cwd`/`all_messages_text` `None`). The host pre-fetches via the session library's `list(false)`, highlights the conductor's `session_id()`, and on selection rides `Flow::Resume(id)` back to the async loop calling `conductor.resume(id)`. Delete/rename deferred.
- *Tree navigator (`Tree`)* — `to_tree_option` carries `id`/`label`/`depth`/`is_leaf`/`is_current`. The conductor exposes **no tree-navigate seam yet** — Enter reports a status toast (`"Tree navigation not yet wired — would jump to …"`) and closes.
- *Prior-turn fork (`UserTurns`)* — `to_turn_option` carries `entry_id`, `text`, `preview`. The conductor exposes **no fork seam yet** — Enter reports (`"Branch not yet wired — would fork at …"`) and closes.

**Auth overlays** sit over the launch crate's OAuth machinery + credential vault.
- *Sign-in (`SignIn`)* — a `LoginDialog` in `LoginMode::Login`. `entry_mode_for` maps `AuthKind::Oauth` → `OAuthMode::Oauth`, `AuthKind::ApiKey` → `OAuthMode::ApiKey` (both open the same `Oauth` entry overlay; the mode picks the body). `resolve_direct_route` lets `/login <provider>` skip the picker. Carried by `ModalPayload::SignIn(SignInRef { requested_provider })`.
- *OAuth / api-key entry (`Oauth`)* — seeds and drives the framework `OAuthDialog`. `seed_oauth_state` builds fresh state (`input_label` `"{providerName} API key"` in api-key mode, `"Authorization code"` in OAuth mode). The **callbacks-as-channel** rewrite: `OverlayCallbacks` implements `OAuthLoginCallbacks` by sending `OAuthProgress` over an mpsc channel the host folds via `apply_progress` — `Auth(AuthRedirectInfo)` (sets `auth_info` + `OPENING_BROWSER`, host opens URL then `set_browser_opened` → `OPENED_BROWSER`/`OPEN_FAILED`), `Prompt { prompt, reply }` (returns the parked `oneshot::Sender<String>` Enter fulfils), `Progress(String)`. The api-key path is local (`build_api_key_save` trims, defaults account to `"default"`, `None` for blank). After sign-in the host binds the provider's *newest* catalog model via `provider_model_rule` (`cards.last()`, since early entries 404). Carried by `ModalPayload::Oauth(OAuthFlowRef { provider_id, oauth_mode })`.
- *Sign-out (`SignOut`)* — a `LoginDialog` in `LoginMode::Logout`; accounts **pre-fetched before the push**. `to_saved_account` builds the display label `"{providerLabel} · {accountId}"` while carrying the provider *id* for `vault.remove(provider, account_id)`. Empty → "No saved credentials were found."

**The plugin overlay (`Plugin`)** — the only overlay needing no runtime services; the mcp/memory/composio commands pass their real state down as the request `text`. `PluginRequest { surface, title, text }` / `from_payload` narrows opaque JSON (non-object → surface `"plugin"`). `PluginDialog` is bespoke over `DialogFrame` + `Paragraph` (empty line → single space; no text → `"No data available for the {surface} surface."`; title default `"Plugin surface"`, footer `"esc to close"`). Only Esc is live (`DialogOutcome::Close`); other keys inert, `Release` ignored. Carried by `ModalPayload::Plugin(PluginOverlayRef { surface, title, text })`.

**The approval overlay (`Approval`)** — the thirteenth kind, absent from the Python/TS modal-kind enum but first-class here; raised when the conductor's permission gate reaches an `ask` decision. Backed by three modules.
- *The prompt widget (`overlays::approval`)* — `ApprovalRequest { tool_name, input, suggestions }`; shows `Allow <tool> to run?`, a one-line argument preview, any suggested allow-rule, and a three-choice list. `read_request` narrows the payload; `choice_from_id` is pure/total (unrecognized → `DISMISS_CHOICE` = `Deny`); `summarize_input` renders args as one short line (shell `command` verbatim else compact JSON, elided at `ARG_PREVIEW_LIMIT` = 200 chars counting characters). The widget is bespoke (`DialogFrame` titled `Permission` + a three-row `WindowedList`). Enter → `Select(choice)`, Esc → `Close` (folded to `Deny`), Up/Down clamped (no wrap). The choices:

| id | choice | label | description |
|----|--------|-------|-------------|
| `allow-once` | `ApprovalChoice::AllowOnce` | Allow once | run this one call |
| `allow-always` | `ApprovalChoice::AllowAlways` | Allow always | run it and remember the tool for this session |
| `deny` | `ApprovalChoice::Deny` | Deny | block this call |

- *The queue (`overlays::approval_queue`)* — `ApprovalQueue` holds concurrent requests (`ApprovalEntry { id, request, resolve: oneshot::Sender<ApprovalChoice> }`); `reduce(ApprovalEvent)` handles `Enqueue` (tail), `Settle { id, choice }` (resolve + advance), `Clear` (drain, settling each `Deny` so a cancelled turn never hangs). The send IS the resolve (a `oneshot::Sender` is consumed by `send`, making double-settle a compile-time impossibility); every send is `let _ =`.
- *The resolver (`overlays::approval_resolver`)* — `ChannelApprovalResolver` implements the conductor's `ApprovalResolver`, bridging the gate (turn task) to the modal (UI loop) over two channels. `request` mints a monotonic id (`ap_0`, `ap_1`, …), parks an entry on an `mpsc::UnboundedSender`, and `await`s its `oneshot`. `AllowOnce`/`AllowAlways` → `ApprovalDecision::Allow`, `Deny` → `Deny`. A closed channel/dropped receiver denies.

**Reaching each overlay:**

| Overlay | Slash command(s) | Keybinding |
|---------|------------------|------------|
| `Models` | `/model` (alias `/models`) | `Ctrl+L` |
| `ScopedModels` | `/models-for` (alias `/scoped-models`; `edit`/`show`/`reset`) | — |
| `Settings` | `/settings` | — |
| `Theme` | via the settings `colourScheme` row | — |
| `Sessions` | `/resume` (alias `/sessions`) | `Ctrl+R` |
| `Tree` | `/timeline` (alias `/tree`) | — |
| `UserTurns` | `/branch` (alias `/fork`) | — |
| `SignIn` | `/login [provider]` | — |
| `SignOut` | `/logout` | — |
| `Oauth` | (sub-flow of `SignIn`) | — |
| `Plugin` | `/mcp`, `/memory`, `/composio` surfaces | — |
| `Approval` | (raised by the permission gate on an `ask` decision) | — |

#### Theming

The colour engine ships **four schemes** (`midnight` / `daylight` + their daltonized `-cb` variants) and runs a deterministic pipeline from a raw 9-stop ramp (`ThemePalette`) to **25 semantic roles** (`ThemeTokens`) to the framework's flat colour-key vocabulary, with a fully-built `ConsoleTheme` per scheme assembled once behind a `OnceLock`. Defined in `induscode::console::theme`. The console body never names a hex or framework key — it names a semantic *role* (`signal`, `frame`, `body_text`, `alarm`, …).

```text
ThemePalette ──derive_tokens──▶ ThemeTokens ──framework_colors──▶ framework keys
  (9-stop ramp)                  (25 roles)         │
                                                    └─theme_adapter─▶ InkTheme
  └──────────────────────────────── ConsoleTheme ────────────────────────────┘
```

Key symbols: `ThemePalette` (struct, the only place hex literals live), `ThemeTokens` (the 25 roles), `ConsoleTheme` (`scheme` + `palette` + `tokens` + `adapter`), `ThemeScheme` (enum, in `console::state`), `palette_for`, `derive_tokens`, `framework_colors`, `theme_adapter`, `resolve_theme`, `theme_for`, `THEME_SCHEMES`. `ThemePalette` fields are `&'static str` (declarable `const`); `ThemeTokens` fields are `String` (two are computed at derive time).

**Palettes & schemes.** A `ThemePalette` has nine stops: three accent hues (cool `primary`, warm `secondary`, muted `tertiary`), a three-stop neutral text gradient (`ink`/`body`/`muted`), and three status hues (`affirm`/`caution`/`alarm`):

| Scheme (`ThemeScheme`) | Literal | Palette `const` | Target | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Midnight` | `"midnight"` | `MIDNIGHT_PALETTE` | dark terminal | Cool spring-teal `primary` (`#3ad6b4`), warm amber `secondary`, periwinkle support; the **default** |
| `Daylight` | `"daylight"` | `DAYLIGHT_PALETTE` | light terminal | Same roles re-derived deeper/saturated; neutral gradient inverts to dark-on-light |
| `MidnightCb` | `"midnight-cb"` | `MIDNIGHT_CB_PALETTE` | dark, color-blind-safe | Clones midnight, re-derives only the three status hues (`affirm → #4aa3ff`), deuteran/protan-safe |
| `DaylightCb` | `"daylight-cb"` | `DAYLIGHT_CB_PALETTE` | light, color-blind-safe | Daylight counterpart; status hues tuned for lightness separation |

`ThemeScheme` lives in `console::state` (`#[default]` Midnight) with `parse(value)` and `as_str(self)`. The CB variants only move the three status stops (accent hues + neutral gradient carry over via functional-record-update). `palette_for` is a `match` over the four consts (const-evaluable). A clean-room guard test asserts the ramps never reuse the forbidden upstream hexes `#00d7ff` / `#5f87ff` / `#8abeb7`.

**Token derivation.** `derive_tokens(palette) -> ThemeTokens` binds the 25 roles to ramp stops exactly once (pure/total/deterministic). The 13 base roles map straight onto stops (`signal ← primary`, `frame ← tertiary`, `quiet_frame ← muted`, `body_text ← body`, `ink_text ← ink`, `alarm ← alarm`, `pending ← primary`, …). The 12 markdown/diff/syntax roles are *derived* from the same nine stops: `code_inline ← primary`, `heading ← primary`, `blockquote_bar ← muted`; `syn_keyword ← primary`, `syn_string ← affirm`, `syn_number ← caution`, `syn_comment ← muted`, `syn_type ← tertiary`; `diff_added_text ← affirm`, `diff_removed_text ← alarm`; `diff_added_bg` / `diff_removed_bg` are **computed**.

**Diff-background colour math** — the only net-new colour math over the framework (the framework ships `parse_hex_color` but no `to_hex`/`mix`/`luminance`). Four private helpers: `parse_rgb`, `to_hex`, `mix_hex(a, b, t)` (linear blend, rounds in `f64` then clamps `0..=255` — NOT `as u8`; a golden test pins the bytes), `luminance(hex) -> f64` (`0.2126·r + 0.7152·g + 0.0722·b`). `background_anchor` picks the neutral (light `ink`/dark terminal → black; dark `ink`/light terminal → white; threshold inclusive `>= 0.5`). `diff_background(hue, anchor) = mix_hex(hue, anchor, 0.78)` blends a status hue **78% toward the anchor**. For midnight: `diff_added_bg == "#0f2c1e"`, `diff_removed_bg == "#351717"`. Painted as backgrounds via `InkTheme::role_background`.

**The framework boundary.** `framework_colors(tokens) -> HashMap<String, String>` projects console roles onto the framework's wire keys: `accent ← signal`, `text ← body_text`, `dim`/`muted ← muted_text`, `borderMuted ← quiet_frame`, `bashBorder ← frame`, `customMessage ← card_accent`, `success ← affirm`, `warning ← caution`, `error ← alarm`, `info ← notice`, `highlight ← ink_text`, `diffAddedBg ← diff_added_bg`, etc. One deliberate divergence: `userMessage` is projected as `""` (matching TS, not the Python `prompt_surface`) — `parse_hex_color("") == None` drops it so the built `InkTheme.colors` has no `userMessage` key. `theme_adapter(scheme_name, tokens)` is the sole `create_theme_adapter` call site (`role_overrides = None`, since the console keys already match `ThemeRole::default_key()`). The framework `InkTheme` (`indusagi::tui_render::theme_adapter`, aliased `Theme`) exposes `color(key)`, `role(role)`, `role_background(bg, fg)`, `muted()`, `dim()`.

**Resolving & switching.** The four `ConsoleTheme`s assemble once behind a `OnceLock`. `SCHEME_ORDER = [Midnight, Daylight, MidnightCb, DaylightCb]`; `assemble_theme` runs `palette_for` → `derive_tokens` → `theme_adapter`. Two resolvers, neither panics: `resolve_theme(scheme: Option<&str>)` (unknown/absent → `ThemeScheme::default()` = midnight, so a corrupt preference never blanks the console) and `theme_for(scheme: ThemeScheme)`; both return `&'static ConsoleTheme` (boot clones only the `InkTheme`). `THEME_SCHEMES` is the picker-order array from the fixed `SCHEME_ORDER` (not `HashMap` iteration, whose order is unstable) — a guard pins `[midnight, daylight, midnight-cb, daylight-cb]`. A live switch is the pure reducer event `ConsoleEvent::SchemeSet(scheme)` (sets `state.scheme`; the next draw re-resolves the adapter).

**The theme picker overlay** (`overlays::theme`, `ModalKind::Theme`) paints the framework `ThemeDialog` and owns the static catalog (id / label / description) in listing order:

| Row | id | label | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `midnight` | Midnight | dark terminals |
| 1 | `daylight` | Daylight | light terminals |
| 2 | `midnight-cb` | Midnight (color-blind) | deuteran-safe, dark |
| 3 | `daylight-cb` | Daylight (color-blind) | deuteran-safe, light |

Seams: `theme_choices()`, `theme_names()`, `scheme_index(scheme)`, `scheme_at(index)` (mutual inverses), `is_active(state)`, `draw_theme(f, area, theme, selected)` (builds a fresh `ThemeDialog`, seeds the `▸` highlight on `selected` re-clamped). **Preview-before-commit** (wired in the mount loop): *Open* captures `theme_revert = Some(state.scheme)` and seeds the highlight via `scheme_index`; *Move* live-previews via `preview_highlighted_scheme` → `scheme_at(modal_selected)` dispatching `SchemeSet` only (nothing written); *Enter* via `commit_theme_selection` re-themes, persists `colour_scheme` through the `PreferenceStore` (faults swallowed), clears `theme_revert`, closes; *Esc/cancel* reverts to `theme_revert` (no write). The same `colour_scheme` value is reachable from the `/settings` colour-scheme row.

**Chrome & live re-theming.** Every component is handed the resolved `&Theme` and reads colours by key. `WorkingIndicator`'s lead span is `theme.color("accent")`, its tail `theme.muted()`. The mount loop resolves `theme_for(state.scheme).adapter.clone()` each frame and threads `&scheme_adapter` into every draw; a `SchemeSet` (preview, commit, `/settings`, or boot from persisted `colour_scheme`) restyles the whole surface deterministically — proven by golden snapshots rendering the same `StatusBar` under midnight and daylight.

**Source files** (`crates/induscode/src/console`): `theme.rs` (the engine — the four `const` ramps, `palette_for`, the hex math, `derive_tokens`, `framework_colors`, `theme_adapter`, the `OnceLock` `themes()` table, `resolve_theme`/`theme_for`, `THEME_SCHEMES`); `overlays/theme.rs` (the picker render half — `CHOICES`, `theme_choices`/`theme_names`, `scheme_index`/`scheme_at`, `is_active`, `draw_theme`); `view/chrome.rs` (`WorkingIndicator`, `StatusBar`, `permission_badge`); `state.rs` (`ThemeScheme`); `reducer.rs` (`ConsoleEvent::SchemeSet`); `mount.rs` (`preview_highlighted_scheme`, `commit_theme_selection`, `theme_revert`, the per-frame adapter resolve). The other editions share the same four schemes, role names, and 78%-toward-anchor diff tints; differences are idiomatic (`const` ramps + `OnceLock` here vs. module-load eval in TS and frozen dataclasses + a Pygments style in Python).


### Subsystems — launch, boot, conductor, runtime bridge

These four subsystems form the front-to-back startup-and-turn spine of the Rust `induscode` coding agent (docs area `/rust-cli`, bins `indusr` / `indusagir`). The crate is `induscode` (one merged product crate, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`), built on the published `indusagi` framework crate. The flow at a glance: **launch** owns the application command line and credential surface; **boot** orchestrates startup (seed → pipeline → runner dispatch → drain), builds the shared session conductor, and resolves resources; the **conductor** is the per-session runtime brain that drives a prompt to settlement; and the **runtime bridge** is the per-turn routing seam that decides whether a turn is produced by the framework gateway or by an external child coding-agent (`claude` / `codex` / peer `indusagi`).

#### Launch

`induscode::launch` (the `pub mod launch` under `src/`) turns a raw argument vector into a fully-configured run. It owns the *application* command line — distinct from the framework's *boot-routing* parser in `indusagi::shell_app::invocation`. The hard architectural decision is a **single declarative flag table**: `flags::flag_specs()` returns one `&'static [FlagSpec]`; `parser::read_invocation` indexes it to parse, and `usage::render_usage` walks it to print help, so help text and parsing can never drift. Adding a row adds both behavior and help text at once. A test pins the agent table at **18 rows** so a contributor cannot accidentally edit the framework's separate **10-row** routing table. The brand bin name surfaced in usage comes from `indusagi::core::BRAND.bin_name` (`"indusagi"`), so a rebrand is a one-file edit.

**Module layout** (`launch/mod.rs` declares the fixed module set and re-exports the frozen contract as a barrel via `pub use contract::*`):

```rust
// induscode::launch
pub mod attachments;  // @file inliner -> Attachments / AttachmentError
pub mod catalog;      // ModelRegistry over ModelCard (filter / sort / resolution)
pub mod contract;     // shared frozen types (Invocation, OutputMode, FlagValue, …)
pub mod credentials;  // multi-account vault + auth.json schema + command surface
pub mod flags;        // FLAG table + FlagSpec/FlagKind/FlagGroup/Mode types
pub mod oauth;        // 3 OAuth providers + poll/refresh FSM
pub mod parser;       // tokenize + parse -> Invocation, derive_mode precedence
pub mod pickers;      // resume / settings / package DATA (ratatui UI deferred)
pub mod usage;        // render_usage from flag_specs() + flag groups
```

The `oauth` module is gated behind the `oauth` feature (it pulls in `indusagi-connectors-saas` and `reqwest`); the rest compiles unconditionally and is unit-testable with no real disk, TTY, or network.

**The frozen contract** (`contract.rs` declares only shapes plus inert pure helpers — no parsing, no terminal I/O). The media element of an attachment is the framework image block `indusagi::llmgateway::Block::Image` directly — there is no second image type.

| Type | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Invocation` | The fully-parsed command line: `mode`, `prompt`, loose `flags` bag, `positionals`, plus resolved typed fields (`model`, `fallback_model`, `account`, `cwd`, `system`, `append_system`, `thinking`, `tools`, `no_tools`, `mcp`, `print`, `interactive`, `help`, `version`, `attachments`) |
| `OutputMode` | `Text` / `Json` / `Rpc` — the agent's vocabulary, mapped to the boot runner; `as_str()` and `is_output_mode()` narrow. **Not** the framework `Mode` (Print/Wire/Repl/Help/Version) |
| `ThinkingEffort` | `Off`/`Minimal`/`Low`/`Medium`/`High`/`XHigh` accepted by `--thinking`; the ordered `THINKING_EFFORTS` tuple is the single source of truth, a superset of the framework `ThinkingLevel` (which omits `Off`); `parse()` + `is_thinking_effort()` |
| `ToolName` | Closed **13-id** roster the `--tools` / `--no-tools` flags validate against before any tool is built (`Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Bash`, `Grep`, `Find`, `Ls`, `Task`, `TodoRead`, `TodoWrite`, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, `Composio`); `TOOL_NAMES`, `parse()`, `is_tool_name()` |
| `FlagValue` | `Bool` / `Str` / `Num(f64)` / `List(Vec<String>)` — the runtime value a parsed flag carries in `Invocation::flags` |
| `Attachments` / `AttachmentOptions` | Result of `@file` expansion (`prose: String` + `media: Vec<Block>`) and the gatherer's `cwd` option |
| `CredentialFault` / `CredentialFaultKind` | Typed credential failure (7 kinds) + the `credential_fault()` builder; impls `Display` + `Error` |
| `CredentialVerb` / `ProviderEntry` | The `Signin`/`Signout` verb enum and a directory row (`id`/`label`/`env_key`/`docs_url`) |
| `CatalogFilter` | `--list-models` filter: optional `provider`, `thinking_only`, `images_only`, case-insensitive `search` substring |
| `ResumeFault` / `SettingsBrowseOptions` | Resume-picker fault + settings-browser options (resolved `Preferences`, grouped resource paths, cwd, profile dir) |

**The flag table** — `flags::flag_specs()` is the one declarative option table: 18 `FlagSpec` rows across five render groups (`Output`, `Model`, `Context`, `Tools`, `Meta`), built once in an `OnceLock` because the `--thinking` description is computed from `THINKING_EFFORTS`.

```rust
pub struct FlagSpec {
    pub name: &'static str,          // canonical long spelling, leading dashes
    pub aliases: &'static [&'static str],
    pub kind: FlagKind,              // Boolean | String | Number | List
    pub group: FlagGroup,            // Output | Model | Context | Tools | Meta
    pub describe: &'static str,
}
```

`FlagKind::List` is the agent's superset over the framework's `{Boolean,String,Number}` (it models the comma-split / repeat-accumulate `--tools` and `--mcp`); `group` drives sectioned help and is inert at parse time. The complete table:

| Flag | Aliases | Kind | Group | Purpose |
|------|---------|------|-------|---------|
| `--print` | `-p` | Boolean | Output | Run a single request, print only the result, and exit. |
| `--json` | `--rpc` | Boolean | Output | Speak the headless line protocol for a driving parent process. |
| `--interactive` | `-i` | Boolean | Output | Force the interactive session even when a prompt is supplied. |
| `--model` | `-m` | String | Model | Select the model, provider-qualified or bare (e.g. `provider/name`). |
| `--fallback-model` | — | String | Model | Model to switch to mid-turn when the selected model is overloaded (HTTP 529). |
| `--account` | — | String | Model | Authenticate the run with a named stored credential account. |
| `--thinking` | — | String | Model | Set the reasoning effort (off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh). |
| `--list-models` | — | String | Model | List available models (optionally filtered by a substring) and exit. |
| `--cwd` | — | String | Context | Scope the run to a working directory (default: current directory). |
| `--system` | — | String | Context | Replace the built-in system prompt with the given text. |
| `--append-system` | — | String | Context | Append extra text after the system prompt. |
| `--resume` | `-r` | Boolean | Context | Pick a previous session to resume. |
| `--continue` | `-c` | Boolean | Context | Continue the most recent session in this directory. |
| `--tools` | — | List | Tools | Allow only the named built-in tools (comma-separated or repeated). |
| `--no-tools` | — | Boolean | Tools | Disable every built-in tool for this run. |
| `--mcp` | — | List | Tools | Attach an external MCP server endpoint (comma-separated or repeated). |
| `--help` | `-h` | Boolean | Meta | Show this usage and exit. |
| `--version` | `-v` | Boolean | Meta | Show the version and exit. |

Three derived indexes are computed once and cached: `flag_key(name)` strips leading dashes (`"--no-tools"` → `"no-tools"`); `token_index()` maps every canonical name **and** alias to its owning row index (so `"-p"`, `"--print"`, `"--rpc"` all resolve); `short_booleans()` is the `HashSet<char>` of single-letter boolean aliases (`p`, `i`, `r`, `c`, `h`, `v`) used for cluster expansion — `-m` is excluded because it is a string flag.

**The argv parser** — `parser::read_invocation(argv: &[String]) -> Invocation` is the hand-rolled, table-driven, **total** reader. It walks the argv once via `token_index()`, accumulates into a private `ParseState`, then folds into the typed `Invocation`. Grammar rules (no per-flag branch):

- `--name=value` and `--name value` both bind a value flag; an inline `=value` wins, else the next token is consumed unless it is itself a flag (`raw = value ?? ""`).
- `--` terminates option parsing; every later token is positional.
- clustered short booleans (`-pi`) expand to each switch via `apply_short_cluster`; a cluster with any unknown letter is kept whole as one extension flag.
- `list` flags accumulate across repetition and `split_list` comma-splits a token, trimming and dropping blanks.
- `@file` tokens (`@x` with len > 1) are recorded as attachment references, never as flags or positionals.
- the parse is **total**: an unrecognised `--flag` is tolerated as a loose boolean (or a string with `=value`) in the `flags` bag — the extension-flag escape hatch. This contrasts with the framework `tokenize_invocation`, which returns an `InvocationError` on an unknown flag.

The first positional becomes `prompt`; the rest accumulate in `positionals`. A final fold derives the named fields — `resolve_thinking` drops an unrecognised `--thinking` value, `resolve_tools` filters `--tools` to known `ToolName`s, and `js_number` mirrors JS `Number(raw)` (`NaN`-as-absent) for the `Number` kind. The `attachments` field is left `None`; `read_file_references(argv)` re-walks argv for just the `@file` refs so the gatherer expands them separately.

```rust
use induscode::launch::parser::{read_invocation, read_file_references};

let inv = read_invocation(&[
    "-p".into(), "prompt".into(), "-m".into(), "model".into(),
    "--mcp".into(), "a".into(), "--mcp".into(), "b".into(),
    "--thinking".into(), "high".into(), "--no-tools".into(),
]);
assert_eq!(inv.mode, OutputMode::Json);
assert_eq!(inv.model.as_deref(), Some("model"));
assert_eq!(inv.mcp, vec!["a".to_string(), "b".to_string()]);
assert_eq!(inv.thinking, Some(ThinkingEffort::High));
assert!(inv.no_tools);

let refs = read_file_references(&["-p".into(), "hi".into(), "@notes.md".into()]); // ["notes.md"]
```

**Mode derivation** — `derive_mode(&flags)` resolves the `OutputMode` via fixed precedence: `--json`/`--rpc` → `Rpc`; `--print` && !`--interactive` → `Json` (one-shot); else `Text` (interactive default). The headless line protocol wins over a one-shot `--print`.

```rust
fn derive_mode(flags: &HashMap<String, FlagValue>) -> OutputMode {
    if read_bool(flags, "json") {
        return OutputMode::Rpc;                                   // --json / --rpc
    }
    if read_bool(flags, "print") && !read_bool(flags, "interactive") {
        return OutputMode::Json;                                  // -p one-shot
    }
    OutputMode::Text                                              // interactive default
}
```

```bash
indusr "refactor the auth module"          # interactive text mode (default)
indusr -p "summarize this repo"            # one-shot json mode, then exits
indusr --json                              # headless rpc line protocol
indusr -i "start here"                     # force interactive even with a prompt
indusr -m anthropic/claude --thinking high "..."
indusr "review" @src/main.rs @diagram.png  # @file attachments
```

**Usage rendering** — `usage::render_usage() -> String` generates the `--help` banner entirely from `FLAG_GROUPS` then the matching `flag_specs()` rows in declaration order (no second hand-maintained help string). The synopsis carries `BRAND.bin_name`; each option line is a signature column padded to `SIGNATURE_COLUMN` (28) followed by `describe`. Per-kind placeholders: `Boolean` → none, `Number` → ` <n>`, `List` → ` <a,b>`, `String` → ` <value>`. A trailing `Arguments:` block documents `@file` and `--`. The returned string has no trailing newline; the CLI print wrapper appends it. A byte-for-byte oracle test pins the generated banner against drift in the table, padding, group order, or brand name. The rendered output begins:

```
Usage: indusagi [options] [prompt] [@file ...]

A terminal-first AI coding agent.

Output:
  --print (-p)                Run a single request, print only the result, and exit.
  --json (--rpc)              Speak the headless line protocol for a driving parent process.
  ...
Arguments:
  @file                       Attach a text or image file to the first message.
  --                          Stop parsing options; treat every later token as a positional.
```

**Attachments (@file)** — `attachments::gather_attachments(references, options) -> Result<Attachments, AttachmentError>` expands each `@file` ref. Each reference is resolved against `options.cwd` (private `resolve_read_path` expands a leading `~` to `$HOME` / `%USERPROFILE%`, takes an absolute path verbatim, else joins onto cwd), classified by lower-cased extension, bounded by a per-kind size cap, and folded:

- **text files** — a closed `TEXT_EXTENSIONS` set (`.txt`, `.md`, `.rs`, `.ts`, `.py`, `.json`, `.toml`, `.yaml`, … ~40 extensions) — are read as UTF-8 and inlined into `Attachments.prose`, each wrapped in a `<file path="...">…</file>` block. Cap: `MAX_TEXT_BYTES` = **10 MiB**. Blocks joined with a blank line.
- **image files** — `IMAGE_MIME_BY_EXT` maps `.png`/`.jpg`/`.jpeg`/`.gif`/`.webp`/`.bmp`/`.svg` to a media type — base64-encoded into `indusagi::llmgateway::Block::Image { media_type, data_base64 }`, collected in `Attachments.media`. Cap: `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` = **20 MiB**.
- a zero-byte file is skipped silently; an unknown extension, oversized file, missing file, or read error returns a typed `AttachmentError` with discriminant `kind` — `Unsupported` / `TooLarge` / `NotFound` / `ReadFailed` — plus the offending `reference` and resolved path (never a string sentinel or a process exit).

**Model catalog and resolution** — `catalog::print_model_catalog(io, filter, source)` renders the `--list-models` table. Rows come from a `CatalogModelSource` seam: `RegistrySource` reads the live `indusagi::facade::ai` catalog (`get_providers()` × `get_models(..)` — **~708 models / 24 providers**) and filters out `EXCLUDED_PROVIDERS` (`"mock"`); `SliceSource` projects an injected `Vec<ModelCard>` for tests. Each row → a `CatalogRow` (Provider, Model, Context, Max Output, Thinking, Images). `filter_rows` applies provider equality (lower-cased), `thinking_only`, `images_only`, and case-insensitive `search` over `"provider/modelId"`; `sort_rows` orders by provider then model id. `format_token_count` renders compact widths (`128K` / `1.5M` / `-`); `layout` computes per-column widths, emits a Title-Case header, a dash rule, then body rows. An empty match prints one notice line. The `CatalogIo` sink (`StdoutCatalogIo` / `VecCatalogIo`) is injectable so the layout is unit-tested in memory.

`resolve_model_id(invocation_model, saved_model, authed) -> String` mirrors the merged framework + product precedence:

1. an **explicit `--model`** naming a real catalog model wins outright;
2. a **saved `settings.default_model`** — but only when `saved_model_usable` (names a real model **and** its owning provider is in the authenticated set), so a stale id from an unauthenticated provider is skipped;
3. an **authenticated provider's current model** via `provider_default_model` (which uses the `PREFERRED_DEFAULT` table to avoid leading-but-deprecated catalog entries);
4. the catalog-guaranteed `FALLBACK_MODEL_ID`, hardened to `CAPABLE_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID` (`claude-sonnet-4`) when the framework fallback names no card — so a bare launch never lands on a zero-window model that would trip a spurious auto-condense.

`model_known` screens a candidate against both the facade catalog (canonical or bare id) and the gateway routing cards; `model_provider(id)` reports the owning provider slug.

**Credentials (signin / signout)** — `credentials::run_credential_command(argv, vault, io, oauth) -> CredentialResult` owns the first positional token only, returning `handled == false` when `argv[0]` is not a verb, so the orchestrator calls it first and falls through to a normal launch on a miss. Verbs: `signin`/`login` and `signout`/`logout` (natural-language aliases keep `indusr login` from being a chat prompt). `read_verb_flags` peels `--provider` / `--account` / `--method` / `--oauth` / `--api-key` (alias `--apikey`) / `--list` (alias `--ls`) off the tail, with the first bare positional treated as the provider.

```bash
indusr signin anthropic                       # browser sign-in preferred when capable
indusr signin openai --method api-key         # force the api-key flow
indusr signin --list                          # read-only list of saved accounts
indusr signout anthropic --account work
```

`PROVIDER_DIRECTORY` is the **14-provider** api-key directory (`anthropic`, `openai`, `google`, `xai`, `groq`, `cerebras`, `mistral`, `openrouter`, `minimax`, `kimi`, `sarvam`, `krutrim`, `nvidia`, `zai`); each `ProviderEntry` carries the conventional `env_key` (read by name via `env_api_key`, since the agent directory is wider than the framework `ProviderId` enum) and a `docs_url`. Flow: (1) resolve the provider (named via `--provider`/first positional, or a numbered pick from the merged login directory); (2) prefer browser sign-in when the provider `is_oauth_capable`, else the api-key flow, consulting the env key first; (3) validate with `validate_api_key` (non-empty, ≥ 20 chars, no `PLACEHOLDER_MARKERS`) or `validate_account_name` (≤ 50 chars, `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`); (4) persist through the injected `AuthVault`, returning a `CredentialResult` with a typed `CredentialFault` on failure — never panicking.

`CredentialFaultKind` is the closed union `UnknownProvider | InvalidKey | InvalidAccount | NameCollision | NotFound | Vault | Aborted`; `format_credential_fault` renders the single human-facing message (`label: message` + indented `hint`). The `CredentialIo` trait injects three console operations (`print`, `ask`, `ask_secret`). Secret hygiene is enforced by `SecretString`: its `Debug` and `Display` both emit `<redacted>`; the only cleartext path is `expose()`.

**The on-disk vault** — `DiskAuthVault` is the concrete `#[async_trait] AuthVault`, constructed over the `auth.json` path from `indusagi::core::Locator::auth_store_path()` (`<profile>/auth.json`). It reads and rewrites the whole tiny file behind a `tokio::sync::Mutex` per call. On-disk shape is a serde-tagged discriminated record keyed `provider -> account -> record`:

```rust
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "camelCase")]
enum AuthRecord {
    ApiKey { key: SecretString, #[serde(rename = "isDefault")] is_default: bool },
    Oauth  { #[serde(flatten)] credentials: OAuthCredentials,
             #[serde(rename = "isDefault")] is_default: bool },
}
```

Files are written `JSON.stringify(_, null, 2) + "\n"` (serde pretty + trailing newline) with mode `0o600` on Unix; `IndexMap` + `preserve_order` keeps insertion order so bytes match an installed build. The reader is permissive: a missing/malformed file reads as empty, a single bad record is skipped, the legacy pre-discriminant `{ apiKey, isDefault }` layout is tolerated by `normalise_record`, and a framework-written single-record `{ provider: { accessToken, … } }` store is **upgraded** to one `default` OAuth account by `upgrade_framework_record`. Removal promotes the first surviving account to default; `make_default` clears peers first. `status_entries()` enumerates every stored sign-in (both shapes) for an `auth status` report, labelling api keys and OAuth tokens with a freshness phrase (`describe_oauth_freshness`).

**OAuth browser sign-in** — the Rust framework ships only the OAuth *transport* skeleton, so `oauth.rs` (behind the `oauth` feature) owns the high-level provider *registry* and three real flows, building on `indusagi::llmgateway::{create_pkce_pair, build_auth_url, exchange_code, refresh_token, OAuthConfig, AuthUrlInputs, PkcePair}`.

- `register_built_in_oauth_providers()` is the **explicit prime** (Rust has no import-time side effect, so boot calls this once before any auth path). It idempotently registers `AnthropicProvider`, `OpenAiCodexProvider`, and `GithubCopilotProvider` into the process-global `OAuthProviderRegistry` (`OnceLock` + `RwLock<IndexMap>`) and returns the live ids. `register_oauth_provider` / `get_oauth_provider` / `get_oauth_providers` manage the registry; `is_oauth_capable(id)` reports whether a browser flow exists.
- the two paste-code flows (Anthropic, OpenAI Codex) share `paste_code_login`: generate a PKCE pair and CSRF state, build the consent URL, surface it through `OAuthLoginCallbacks::on_auth`, await a pasted code (cleaned by `extract_code`, which handles a bare code, `code#state`, or a full redirect URL with `?code=`), and exchange it. GitHub Copilot uses the RFC 8628 device grant; its poll FSM models the framework connectors-saas `ConnectAction` rule table via `classify_poll` (maps `authorization_pending` / `slow_down` / `access_denied` / `expired_token` to `PollStatus`) and `plan_poll` (returns `PollDecision::{Done, Poll{wait_ms, slowed}, Expired, Failed}`).
- `has_registered_oauth_client_id` / `resolve_client_id` gate every flow on the `<UNREGISTERED-…>` sentinel: no real client id ships in source, so a flow refuses with an actionable error naming the exact per-provider env var (`INDUSAGI_ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `INDUSAGI_OPENAI_CODEX_CLIENT_ID`, `INDUSAGI_GITHUB_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID`) when unset, rather than opening a doomed browser tab.
- `start_oauth_login(provider_id, callbacks, vault, account)` drives the provider's login and persists through an `OAuthVaultSink` (first stored account becomes default); `list_login_providers(api_key_directory)` is the merged sign-in directory (OAuth rows leading, then api-key rows). `open_login_url(url)` launches the consent URL but only for syntactically valid `http`/`https` URLs — `is_web_url` refuses any other scheme before spawning a process.

The stored `OAuthCredentials` (`access`/`refresh`/`expires`/`issued_at`/`provider` + flattened `extra` passthrough) is converted from the gateway wire `OAuthTokens` by `tokens_to_credentials`, and has a **redacting** `Debug`.

**Pickers (resume + settings + packages)** — `pickers.rs` holds picker **data** only (the ratatui session dialog belongs to the console), so the launch crate carries no `ratatui` dependency.

- `pick_resume_target(current, all, deps) -> ResumeOutcome` takes already-loaded current-directory and all-directory session lists (async store I/O stays at the boot edge), merges them with `merge_sessions` (de-dupes by path, current wins the key, sorts `last_modified` descending), and either returns the newest session on a non-interactive stdin (the `ResumeDeps::is_interactive` fast-path) or mounts the injected `ResumeDeps::mount_picker`. Returns `ResumeOutcome { path, fault }` — a typed `ResumeFault` is *returned*, never panicked.
- `render_settings_listing(opts) -> Vec<String>` is the pure line builder (working/profile directories, default model, extension-package count, discovered resource paths grouped/sorted by category); `browse_settings(opts, io)` prints it through the injected `SettingsBrowseIo` and pauses for a keypress.
- `run_package_command(argv, store, io) -> PackageResult` is the `install` / `remove` / `update` / `list` / `config` surface over the `extensionPackages` settings key, stored in the typed `Preferences::extension_packages` field via `crate::core::PreferenceStore`. Owns the first token only (`handled == false` on a miss) and never panics. `source_key` / `sources_match` classify a source for equality (an `npm:` spec ignores a trailing `@version`, a git url drops its scheme and `.git` suffix, a local path matches verbatim). `is_package_command(token)` is the routing predicate boot uses to short-circuit before a session is built.

```bash
indusr install npm:@scope/my-ext
indusr list
indusr remove npm:@scope/my-ext
indusr config
```

**Launch public API** (selected):

| Name | Kind | Source | Purpose |
|------|------|--------|---------|
| `read_invocation` / `read_file_references` | fn | `parser.rs` | Table-driven argv parser → `Invocation`; latter re-walks argv for `@file` refs |
| `render_usage` | fn | `usage.rs` | Generates the `--help` banner from `flag_specs()` / `FLAG_GROUPS` |
| `flag_specs` / `FLAG_GROUPS` / `FlagSpec` / `FlagKind` / `FlagGroup` | fn/const/type | `flags.rs` | The single 18-row option table, render groups, row types |
| `flag_key` / `token_index` / `short_booleans` | fn | `flags.rs` | Derived parse indexes over the table |
| `gather_attachments` / `AttachmentError` / `AttachmentErrorKind` | fn/type | `attachments.rs` | Expands `@file` refs → `Attachments`; typed error |
| `print_model_catalog` / `CatalogIo` / `CatalogModelSource` / `RegistrySource` / `SliceSource` / `CatalogRow` | fn/trait/type | `catalog.rs` | Aligned model table over the facade catalog with injectable seams |
| `resolve_model_id` / `model_provider` / `saved_model_usable` | fn | `catalog.rs` | Merged model-id resolution precedence + helpers |
| `run_credential_command` / `CredentialResult` / `CredentialIo` | fn/type/trait | `credentials.rs` | The `signin` / `signout` command |
| `PROVIDER_DIRECTORY` / `find_provider` / `validate_api_key` / `validate_account_name` / `format_credential_fault` / `as_signin_method` | const/fn | `credentials.rs` | 14-provider directory, lookup, validators, fault formatter |
| `AuthVault` / `DiskAuthVault` / `SecretString` / `OAuthCredentials` / `AuthKind` / `AuthStatusEntry` | trait/type | `credentials.rs` | Vault trait, on-disk multi-account impl, secret/record shapes |
| `register_built_in_oauth_providers` / `start_oauth_login` / `is_oauth_capable` / `list_login_providers` / `open_login_url` / `classify_poll` / `plan_poll` | fn | `oauth.rs` | Registry prime, login driver, merged directory, browser launcher, device-poll FSM (`oauth` feature) |
| `pick_resume_target` / `ResumeDeps` / `ResumeOutcome` / `merge_sessions` | fn/trait/type | `pickers.rs` | Merges resumable sessions |
| `render_settings_listing` / `browse_settings` / `SettingsBrowseIo` | fn/trait | `pickers.rs` | Settings listing builder + paused console dump |
| `run_package_command` / `PackageCommand` / `PackageResult` / `PackageIo` / `is_package_command` | fn/type/trait | `pickers.rs` | Package command over `extensionPackages` |

**Launch key concepts**: single declarative flag table (18 rows, test-pinned); frozen contract seam (shapes + inert helpers, no I/O); typed faults over sentinels (`CredentialFault` 7 kinds, `AttachmentError` 4 kinds, `ResumeFault`, `OAuthError`); total parsing (unknown flag tolerated as a loose boolean); injectable I/O seams (`CatalogIo`, `CredentialIo`, `PackageIo`, `SettingsBrowseIo`, `ResumeDeps`, `CatalogModelSource`, `OAuthSeam`); byte-compatible vault + explicit OAuth prime; secret redaction (`SecretString`/`OAuthCredentials` redact in `Debug`/`Display`; no real OAuth client id ships in source).

#### Boot

`induscode::boot` is the top-of-stack assembly layer: it turns a sliced `argv` plus an I/O seam into a running coding agent and a process exit code. It is ported over the framework templates `indusagi::shell_app::boot` (`Stage`, `run_stages`, `BootIo`, `OutputSink`, `InputSource`, `Closable`) and `indusagi::shell_app::runners` (`Runner`, `select_runner`). The design stance is **pipeline as data, not control flow**: stages are `Box<dyn Stage>` rows folded by `BootPipeline::run`, and dispatch is a first-accept scan over an ordered `RunnerRegistry`. Adding a stage or a mode is a one-line table edit.

`boot/mod.rs` re-exports the contract types so callers code against one surface:

```rust
pub use contract::{
    BootContext, BootIo, BootPipeline, Closable, InputSource, Invocation, OutputSink,
    Runner, RunnerId, RunnerRegistry, Stage, StartupResources,
};
```

Boot consumes the **launch** flag grammar (`launch::parser::read_invocation`), the **conductor** session engine, the **capability deck** for tools, **briefing** for the system prompt, **channels** for non-interactive transports, and the **console** only behind the `tui` feature. It types its resolved-resource graph against `indusagi::shell_app::Settings` and drives the agent loop through `indusagi::runtime`.

**Two layers of contract** exist deliberately: `induscode::core::boot_contract` (milestone M0) owns the **value shapes** (`BootContext`, `Invocation`, `RunnerId`, `StartupResources`, `CredentialGraph`, `ModelCatalog`, plus *sync* `Stage`/`Runner` skeletons) — it lives in the leaf `core` module because `launch`/`deck`/`settings` import these shapes, and putting them in `boot` would create a `boot ⇄ launch` cycle Cargo forbids. `induscode::boot::contract` re-states the **async orchestrator** form over the same value types (async `Stage`/`Runner` traits, the line-oriented `BootIo` seam, a future-returning `Closable`) because the framework `run_stages` fold and the runner turn loop are `async`.

**The boot orchestrator** — `boot_run(argv, io)` is the single async function the binary entry (`src/bin/main.rs`) calls:

```rust
pub async fn boot_run(argv: Vec<String>, io: BootIo) -> std::process::ExitCode;
```

The contract is explicit: `boot_run` **never** calls `process::exit` — it maps every outcome to an `ExitCode` returned by value (the only place a code reaches the OS) — and it **always** drains the context's `closables` in reverse on the way out, regardless of how the runner resolved.

```rust
pub async fn boot_run(argv: Vec<String>, io: BootIo) -> ExitCode {
    let seeded = seed_context(argv, io);

    let pipeline = pipeline::stages();
    let ctx = pipeline.run(seeded).await;

    let registry = runners::registry();
    let code = registry.select(&ctx.invocation).run(&ctx).await;

    drain_closables(&ctx).await;
    ExitCode::from(code as u8)
}
```

The **argv → ExitCode** flow: (1) **Seed** — `seed_context(argv, io)` builds the initial `BootContext`, resolving the `Workspace` via `core::create_workspace(Default::default())` (pure path computation), setting `BRAND`, seeding an empty `closables` list and a placeholder `Invocation::default()` (mode `None`), threading the `BootIo` seam. (2) **Fold** — `pipeline::stages()` builds the five-stage `BootPipeline`; `pipeline.run` folds it over the seed. (3) **Dispatch** — `runners::registry()` builds the `[repl, oneshot, link]` registry; `registry.select(&ctx.invocation)` returns the first runner whose `accepts` matches `mode` (repl is the total fallback), and `run(&ctx)` drives it to an `i32` exit code. (4) **Drain** — `drain_closables(&ctx)` runs every teardown, latest-registered first.

The **credential / package verbs** (`signin`, `signout`, `auth …`, `install`, `remove`, `update`, `list`, `config`) and the **meta short-circuits** (`--help` / `--version` / `--list-models`) are owned by the `route()` function in `src/bin/main.rs`, which renders usage and routes the auth subcommand through `launch` *before* calling `boot_run`. So by the time argv reaches `boot_run` it is always a session-bound launch.

`drain_closables` drains the list under the `Mutex` (recovering from a poisoned lock), then `await`s each teardown in reverse registration order; individual failures are swallowed:

```rust
pub async fn drain_closables(ctx: &BootContext) {
    let drained: Vec<Closable> = match ctx.closables.lock() {
        Ok(mut guard) => guard.drain(..).collect(),
        Err(poisoned) => poisoned.into_inner().drain(..).collect(),
    };
    for close in drained.into_iter().rev() {
        close().await;
    }
}
```

**The orchestrator contract** (`boot/contract.rs`):

| Name | Kind | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `BootContext` | struct | Threaded through the pipeline: `argv`, `workspace`, `brand`, `invocation`, `resources: Option<StartupResources>`, `io: BootIo`, `closables: Mutex<Vec<Closable>>` |
| `Invocation` | struct (from `core`) | The thin routing projection of the parsed command line |
| `RunnerId` | enum (from `core`) | `Repl` / `Oneshot` / `Link` |
| `StartupResources` | struct (from `core`) | Resolved `settings` (`indusagi::shell_app::Settings`) + `auth: CredentialGraph` + `models: ModelCatalog` |
| `Stage` | `#[async_trait]` trait | `fn name(&self) -> &str` + `async fn apply(&self, ctx: BootContext) -> BootContext` |
| `BootPipeline` | struct | `Vec<Box<dyn Stage>>` + `run(&self, initial) -> BootContext` |
| `Runner` | `#[async_trait(?Send)]` trait | `fn id() -> RunnerId`, `fn accepts(&Invocation) -> bool`, `async fn run(&self, &BootContext) -> i32` |
| `RunnerRegistry` | struct | Ordered runner table + the **total** `select` first-accept scan |
| `BootIo` | struct | `output: Arc<dyn OutputSink>` + `input: Arc<dyn InputSource>` |
| `OutputSink` | trait | `write(&str)` + `write_error(&str)` |
| `InputSource` | `#[async_trait]` trait | `async fn next_line(&self) -> Option<String>` — `None` at EOF |
| `Closable` | type alias | `Box<dyn FnOnce() -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = ()> + Send>> + Send>` |

`BootContext::closables` uses interior mutability (`Mutex<Vec<Closable>>`) because runners hold a shared `&BootContext` yet still need to register teardowns. `BootContext` exposes `push_closable(closable)` and a convenience `output_error(text)`. Each `Stage::apply` returns a *fresh* successor via struct-update, never in-place mutation. `Runner::run` is `?Send` because the future borrows the (intentionally non-`Sync`) `BootContext` and the launcher drives it inline on one task. The registry's `select` is **total** (repl is the first entry and the guaranteed fallback), differing from the framework's fallible `select_runner`:

```rust
pub fn select(&self, inv: &Invocation) -> &dyn Runner {
    self.runners
        .iter()
        .find(|r| r.accepts(inv))
        .map(|r| r.as_ref())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| self.runners.first().map(|r| r.as_ref()).expect("repl fallback"))
}
```

**The stage pipeline** (`boot/pipeline.rs`) — `stages()` assembles five `Box<dyn Stage>` rows; `BootPipeline::run` reduces a seed through each, awaiting strictly in order (never concurrently):

```rust
pub fn stages() -> BootPipeline {
    BootPipeline::new(vec![
        Box::new(LocateWorkspace),
        Box::new(ApplyUpgrades),
        Box::new(BuildInvocation),
        Box::new(ResolveResources),
        Box::new(SelectRunnerMarker),
    ])
}
```

| Stage | `name()` | Effect |
|-------|----------|--------|
| `LocateWorkspace` | `locate-workspace` | `ensure_dirs(&ctx.workspace)` — `mkdir -p`s the resolved layout. Best-effort: a `mkdir` failure is reported via `output_error` but never aborts boot |
| `ApplyUpgrades` | `apply-upgrades` | Folds the idempotent `apply_upgrades(&ctx.workspace)` registry; each warning printed, never fatal |
| `BuildInvocation` | `build-invocation` | Re-parses `argv` via `launch::parser::read_invocation`, then projects the launch `Invocation` onto the boot-routing `Invocation` via `map_invocation` |
| `ResolveResources` | `resolve-resources` | Attaches the best-effort `StartupResources` graph from `resources::resolve_startup_resources(&ctx)` onto `ctx.resources` |
| `SelectRunnerMarker` | `select-runner` | A marker / tracing no-op; real dispatch happens in `boot_run` after the pipeline so the chosen runner owns the exit code |
