A profile is a selection policy over the catalog (data, not control flow) — collapses to one `CapabilityCard::in_profile` filter (the TS `PROFILE_TABLE` is gone). `cards_for_deck_profile(profile)` is the selection `provision_deck` walks; `build_selected` builds each row and folds the checkpoint wrapper around mutating built-ins.

| Deck profile | Built-in membership selected | App-novel cards |
|--------------|------------------------------|-----------------|
| `Authoring` | read-only subset (read/ls/grep/find/websearch/webfetch/`todo_read`) | no |
| `Survey` | every built-in, mutating included | no |
| `All` | every built-in | yes (all 7) |

**Profile-name inversion (ported verbatim, pinned by tests — do not "fix").** Deck `Authoring` selects the framework *read-only* set; `Survey` selects *every* built-in; `All` adds the app cards. The read-only set of profiles is `[Authoring, Survey]`. Because `Profile` is closed, `cards_for_deck_profile` is total and infallible — the TS unknown-profile fault is structurally unrepresentable. `DeckResult` is kept for parity and to leave room for a `--tools` intersection later; build closures are infallible, so `build_selected` is a straight map and `DeckFault::BuildFailed` is reserved for fallible bridge enrollment.

The assembled `ToolDeck` exposes:

| Method | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `tools()` | Flat capability list as a fresh clone. |
| `graft(extra)` | Concatenate extra (bridge/MCP/addon) capabilities after the static selection. |
| `map_capabilities(f)` | Replace every capability with `f(cap)` — the addon interceptor-chain wrapping seam. |
| `retain(keep)` | Keep only capabilities `keep` returns true for — the `--tools` allow-list filter, applied before the MCP/addon graft. |
| `into_tool_box()` | Build the runtime `Box<dyn ToolBox>` the conductor consumes. |

A grafted MCP tool carries a qualified `"<server>__<tool>"` name, so a name collision with a built-in is not representable.

**Runtime ToolBox adapter.** `into_tool_box()` builds a `DeckToolBox`: an `indusagi::runtime::ToolBox` pairing the descriptors with a `DeckRunner`. The base `ToolContext` is minted once from `cwd` and the injected `read_state` handle (the only field the framework `Framework` exposes — checkpoint/delegate/saas/memory ride on the cards):

```rust
let base = make_local_context(
    ctx.cwd.clone(), None, None,
    Some(Framework { read_state: ctx.framework.read_state.clone() }),
);
```

`DeckRunner::run` resolves a `ToolCall` to its `Capability` by name from a `HashMap<String, Capability>`, threads the dispatch cancel token via `ToolContext::with_cancel` (preserving context identity so identity-keyed stores survive across calls — required so the framework `todo_read`/`todo_set` see one store across a session), runs the card, and projects the `ToolResult` back into a `ToolOutcome`. An unknown tool name surfaces as an `is_error` outcome, never a panic. `project_result` folds blocks into one output: single text block → JSON string, single JSON block → the value, zero-or-many → array of tagged `{type, …}` fragments.

**App-novel cards (`cards/`).** Seven in-house tools the framework does NOT provide, concatenated only for the `All` profile; order is load-bearing:

```rust
pub fn app_novel_cards() -> Vec<CapabilityCard> {
    vec![
        todo::todo_card(),
        bg_process::daemon_card(),
        task::task_card(),
        saas::saas_card(),
        memory::memory_card(),
        plan::enter_plan_mode_card(),
        plan::exit_plan_mode_card(),
    ]
}
```

| Card fn | Tool `name` | Actions | Behavior |
|---------|-------------|---------|----------|
| `todo_card` | `todo` | `read` \| `set` | In-deck `TodoLedger` (`Mutex<Vec<TodoItem>>`), distinct from the framework `todo_read`/`todo_set`; `set` wholesale-replaces. Items carry `TodoState` (pending/active/done/dropped) + `TodoWeight` (low/normal/high); glyphs `[ ]`/`[~]`/`[x]`/`[-]`. |
| `daemon_card` | `bg-process` | `start` \| `poll` \| `stop` \| `list` | Background-process table over framework `Shell::spawn` (not Node `child_process`), bounded ring buffers (`MAX_BUFFERED_LINES = 2_000`), capture files under `.indusvx-bg`, SIGTERM→SIGKILL after `STOP_GRACE_MS = 3_000`. |
| `task_card` | `task` | (objective + agent/context) | Sub-agent delegate over `DelegateRunner` (backed by `indusagi-swarm`, feature `swarm`); typed stub when handle absent. Threads `list_agents()` roster into the description. |
| `saas_card` | `saas-action` | `discover` \| `execute` | Connector tool over `SaasGatewayPort` (backed by `indusagi-connectors-saas`, feature `composio`); stub when absent. Vendor slugs (`GITHUB_CREATE_ISSUE`) pass through verbatim. |
| `memory_card` | `memory` | `read` \| `replace` \| `append` | Working-memory scratch-note tool over `MemoryStore`, defaulting to a card-owned `InMemoryStore` (`Mutex<String>`) when no handle is injected. |
| `enter_plan_mode_card` | `enter_plan_mode` | (none) | Read-only marker: returns `{ enterPlanMode: true, applied: false }` plus explore-only prose. |
| `exit_plan_mode_card` | `exit_plan_mode` | (plan) | Read-only marker: returns `{ exitPlan: true, plan }`; the conductor intercepts it to raise the user-approval prompt. |

Each card keys behavior on an `action` discriminant with defensive runtime guards returning `is_error` results, and joins only `Profile::All`. The `task` and `saas` cards are **always built** (stubs when `swarm`/`composio` is off) so catalog shape is stable; the feature gates only the REAL handle wiring (in `induscode-addons`). Stores (`TodoLedger`, `DaemonTable`, `InMemoryStore`) are per-built-capability, so two sessions never share state; background-process output is capped at 2000 lines per stream.

**Plan-mode tools.** Both plan tools are side-effect-free and marked `read_only` so the gate always permits them (including the tool used to request leaving plan mode). Neither flips the mode; the conductor watches the tool-result seam for `enterPlanMode`/`exitPlan` markers (the plan-mode gate is deferred to M-conductor). The TS optional in-context `PlanController` is dropped, so the entry detail's `applied` is always `false`. `plan.rs` also ships plan-file helpers:

```rust
pub const PLANS_DIRNAME: &str = "plans";
pub fn plan_slug(plan: &str) -> String;                         // first non-empty line → fs-safe slug, capped at 48 chars, "plan" fallback
pub fn plan_file_path(session_dir, slug) -> PathBuf;            // <session_dir>/plans/<slug>.md
pub fn write_plan(session_dir, plan) -> io::Result<PathBuf>;    // writes <base36-timestamp>-<slug>.md so repeats never collide
pub fn read_plan(path) -> Option<String>;                       // None on a missing/unreadable file
```

The timestamp prefix is base-36 epoch-millis (the JS `Number.toString(36)` analogue).

**The checkpoint wrapper (`cards/checkpoint.rs`).** The framework `Framework` context carries only `read_state`, so `write`/`edit` record nothing for a code-rewind. When `DeckContext` carries a `checkpoint` handle, `build_selected` folds each built `write`/`edit` inside a `CheckpointingCard` via `maybe_wrap_checkpoint`: the wrapper reads the target file's CURRENT on-disk content (through `ctx.fs`), files it into the injected `CheckpointStore` under the active transcript node, then delegates to the inner card. Every model-facing field is projected straight through (only `run` is augmented).

```rust
pub const CHECKPOINTED_TOOLS: &[&str] = &["write", "edit"];  // bash/process excluded
```

Mirrors the framework pre-write `record(abs_path, previous)`: `previous == None` records that the file did NOT exist (a restore then deletes it); the store enforces first-seen-wins per (node, path); reading prior content is best-effort. With no handle wired, `maybe_wrap_checkpoint` returns the same `Arc` identity-equal.

**The bridge ledger (`deck::mcp::ledger`, `mcp` feature).** MCP enrollment is event-sourced: an append-only event log folded into a derived snapshot via `reduce(state, ops) -> snapshot`.

| Type | Kind | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `BridgeOp` | enum | `Enroll` \| `Retire` — closed, exhaustive `match`, no `_` arm. |
| `BridgeKey` | newtype | Branded stable key of an enrolled bridge capability. |
| `BridgeEntry` | struct | One append-only event: `op`, `key`, `server`, `capability` (`Some` on enroll, `None` on retire), `seq`, `at`. |
| `LedgerSnapshot` | struct | Reduced view: `live: IndexMap<BridgeKey, BridgeCapability>`, `by_server: IndexMap<String, usize>`, `high_water: u64`. |
| `EnrollRequest` | struct | Fields an enrollment supplies (`capability`, `server`, optional `key`); the ledger stamps `op`/`seq`/`at`. |
| `BridgeLedger` | struct | Immutable value: the ordered `log`, its folded `snapshot`, and `next_seq`. |

Every transition returns a new ledger (input never touched):

| Method | Op | Behavior |
|--------|-----|----------|
| `BridgeLedger::empty()` | — | Empty ledger; sequence numbering starts at 1. |
| `BridgeLedger::from_log(log)` | — | Rehydrate from a persisted log (deterministic replay; resume past the high-water mark). |
| `enroll(req, at)` | enroll | **Upsert** — re-enrolling the same `BridgeKey` replaces its live entry. |
| `retire(key, server, at)` | retire | **Splice** — the fold drops the keyed entry; an unknown key is a harmless no-op (still recorded for audit). |
| `withdraw_server(server, at)` | retire ×N | Retire every live capability a server has, in one batch. |
| `live_capabilities()` | — | Flat list of every live capability. |
| `live_capabilities_for_server(server)` | — | Live capabilities a single server contributes. |

`reduce_ledger(&[BridgeEntry])` is the single sanctioned reducer: pure and total, sorts a borrowed index by `seq` (never mutating the caller's slice), lets a later sequence win on a repeated key (`Enroll` upsert), removes retired keys (`shift_remove`, matching JS `Map.delete`), derives per-server counts. `IndexMap` (not `HashMap`) keeps insertion order so `live_capabilities()` is stable, matching TS `Map` insertion-order parity.

`BridgeCapability` is the deck's adapted view of one grafted remote tool, `Arc`-shared so it lives in both the log entry and snapshot cheaply. It implements `Card`; its `name`/`label` are both the qualified `"<server>__<tool>"`; `run` hands the call to the box's shared `ToolRunner` under that qualified name and projects the opaque `ToolOutcome` via `project_outcome` (a `Value::String` verbatim, `Value::Null` → empty, anything else JSON-pretty-printed; `is_error` rides through). `bridge_box_to_capabilities(box_)` adapts every descriptor a mounted `ToolBox` advertises plus the box's shared runner into `BridgeCapability`s.

**Bridge keys (`ledger.rs`).** Keys are minted from the capability's identity, never from a working-directory digest, so the same external tool grafted from two sessions collapses to one key.

```rust
qualify_bridge_name(server, tool) -> String                              // "<server>__<tool>" using the framework QUALIFIER
bridge_content_key(server, tool, parameters: Option<&Value>) -> BridgeKey  // default: "bk_<32hex>"
bridge_ulid_key() -> BridgeKey                                           // opt-in: "bk_<ULID>", distinct/time-sortable events
server_of_qualified(name) -> &str                                       // recover the owning server from a qualified name
```

`bridge_content_key` digests the qualified name plus the parameter schema. The `{name, schema}` identity is key-sorted by a recursive `sort_keys` (so key-order-only schema differences yield the same key — the TS `canonicalize`, array order preserved), then hashed via `indusagi::core::content_hash` (sha256-over-canonical-json, 32 hex chars). A missing schema is `Value::Null`. A changed schema yields a new key. Cross-impl byte-parity with the TS hash is not required — only stability within/across runs of this binary. `bridge_ulid_key` uses a process-wide monotonic `ulid::Generator`.

**Mounting MCP servers (`deck::mcp/mod.rs`).** The framework `indusagi::interop::mount_protocol_bridge` does the protocol work (connect every configured server, list each ready endpoint's tools, normalize schemas, return a mounted bridge advertising every remote tool under its qualified name). This module adds enrollment, status, cataloging, lifecycle:

```rust
use induscode::deck::mcp::{attach_bridge_capabilities, bridge_config, detach_bridge};
use induscode::deck::mcp::ledger::BridgeLedger;
let config = bridge_config(servers);                 // Vec<ServerConfig> -> BridgeConfig
let result = attach_bridge_capabilities(BridgeLedger::empty(), config).await;
// result: AttachResult { ledger, fleet, status, enrolled, fault }
let tools = result.ledger.live_capabilities();       // Vec<BridgeCapability>
```

- **Enrollment.** `attach_bridge_capabilities(ledger, config)` mounts the fleet, adapts via `bridge_box_to_capabilities`, folds each capability into a new ledger as an `enroll` event. Returns `AttachResult { ledger, fleet (caller must tear down), status: FleetStatus, enrolled count, fault }`. Empty config is a no-op.
- **Detach.** `detach_bridge(ledger, fleet, servers)` withdraws named servers' live entries (or every server when `servers` is `None`) and best-effort tears the fleet down.
- **Status.** `bridge_tool_names(ledger)`, `bridge_tool_counts(ledger)` (both from the ledger snapshot, no live fleet handle), and `bridge_status(fleet)` (pass-through over `ServerFleet::status`).
- **Cataloging.** `bridge_capability_card(capability)` re-presents a grafted capability as a `CapabilityCard` (its `build` returns the already-live capability; `profiles` is empty `&[]` so it stays out of profile-filtered provisioning while still cataloged).

Unlike the TS, `mount_protocol_bridge` is **infallible** (returns a `MountedProtocolBridge` directly, not a `Result`) — per-server health is read from `fleet.status()`; a faulted server simply contributes no descriptors. `AttachResult.fault` (a `DeckFault::Bridge`) is reserved for config validation only.

**MCP config discovery.** `load_mcp_config(path_or_cwd)` reads the `.indusvx/mcp.json` family into a `Vec<ServerConfig>`, merged in precedence order (port of the framework `loadMCPConfig`):

1. Project: `<cwd>/.indusvx/mcp.json`
2. User (XDG): `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/indusvx/mcp.json` (default `~/.config`)
3. Legacy: `~/.indusvx/agent/mcp.json` and `~/.indusvx/agent/mcp-servers.json`

When `path_or_cwd` is an existing file, it is parsed directly. A malformed/unreadable file is skipped. `parse_config_file` supports both array (`{"servers": [{"name": …}]}`) and object (`{"servers": {"name": {…}}}`) formats, drops `"enabled": false` rows, and discriminates transports: a `"url"` field → `ServerConfig::Sse`, a `"command"` field → `ServerConfig::Stdio`; a row matching neither is skipped. `bridge_config(servers)` wraps a flat list into a `BridgeConfig`. The ledger's `at` audit field is an ISO-8601 UTC string derived from `indusagi::core::time::now_ms` via a dependency-free civil-from-days conversion.

**Faults.** `DeckFault` is a closed exhaustive enum (no `_` arm), `thiserror::Error`:

| Variant | Raised when |
|---------|-------------|
| `UnknownCapability(String)` | A requested capability id is not in the catalog (`--tools`/`build_builtin`). |
| `BuildFailed { id, message }` | A card's `build` failed (reserved for fallible bridge enrollment). |
| `Bridge(String)` | Connecting/listing/grafting an MCP server failed (config-validation; carried on `AttachResult`, not raised). |
| `Backend(String)` | A required injected backend handle was missing/invalid. |

`pub type DeckResult<T> = Result<T, DeckFault>`.

**Parity notes:** no callable `AgentTool` object (deck defines `Card`); wire-name rename `todo_read`/`todo_set` (pinned by `builtin_name_parity`); two extra app cards vs Python's five (the two plan-mode markers); arg-free factories (cwd/read-state/checkpoint via per-dispatch `ToolContext`); closed enums make faults unrepresentable (`Profile`, `BridgeOp`); infallible mount; per-session isolation of stores.

#### Channels

The channels module (`induscode::channels`) is the non-interactive driver surface — how the agent talks to a `Conductor` when no console is attached. It declares **one** contract — a JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope, a U+2028/U+2029-safe NDJSON framer, a data-driven operation registry, ask/tell dialog primitives, and a flat wire snapshot — and two channels written against it. The protocol op registry is consumed by **both** the server (data-driven dispatch, no `match` ladder) and the wire (the Boot `LinkRunner`'s read loop), so the served method set and dispatch path can never drift. The crate is **headless by design** — no `tui` dependency, so a `--no-default-features` build keeps the print/JSON path standing with the console absent. Every transport is an injected `LineSink`/`LineSource` seam, so the subsystem tests over in-memory pipes with zero real stdio.

**Two channels:**
- **One-shot** runs prompts to settlement and writes either clean final text (the `-p`/`--print` path, `OneshotShape::Text`) or a streamed NDJSON event log (`OneshotShape::Ndjson`, built and tested but **not yet wired to a CLI flag**).
- **Link** is a long-lived JSON-RPC 2.0 server over stdio (the `--json`/`--rpc` path) that a driving parent process steers turn by turn.

**Reaching the channels.** Boot's launch parser `derive_mode` returns `Rpc` when `--json`/`--rpc` is set, `Json` when `--print`/`-p` rides without `--interactive`, else `Text`. The boot pipeline's `map_invocation` maps the mode onto a `RunnerId` (`Rpc → Link`, `Json → Oneshot`, `Text → Repl`); the registry `[repl, oneshot, link]` first-accepts the runner whose `accepts` matches `inv.mode`:

| CLI invocation | `OutputMode` → `RunnerId` | Runner | Channel |
|----------------|---------------------------|--------|---------|
| `indusr -p "…"` | `Json` → `RunnerId::Oneshot` | `OneShotRunner` | one-shot, `OneshotShape::Text` |
| `indusr --json` | `Rpc` → `RunnerId::Link` | `LinkRunner` | link server over stdin/stdout |
| `indusr -p --json "…"` | `Rpc` → `RunnerId::Link` | `LinkRunner` | link server (`--json` wins over `-p`) |

`OneShotRunner` builds a `ChannelContext` over a `StdoutSink` (`LineSink`) + `inert_dialog()` and calls `run_oneshot`. The shape comes from `oneshot_shape(&inv)`, which **unconditionally returns `OneshotShape::Text`** at this milestone (the boot `Invocation` carries no structured-output flag yet — the M-launch deferral). `LinkRunner` assembles a `session_ops()` registry and pumps each framed line off the boot `InputSource` through `handle_link_line`. Channels owns no session/agent logic — every op delegates to the conductor; a channel only switches on the conductor's typed `SessionSignal` vocabulary, never a raw framework `RunEvent`.

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
indusr -p "summarise what changed on this branch"   # clean final text (one-shot, Text)
indusr --json                                        # JSON-RPC line protocol (parent-driven, link)
```

**The one-shot channel.** `run_oneshot(ctx, opts) -> i32` runs one request to settlement and returns a process exit code (`0` clean / `1` faulted). The output shape is a **strategy object** selected by `strategy_for(shape)`:

```rust
pub trait OneshotStrategy: Send + Sync {
    fn on_start(&self, _ctx: &ChannelContext) {}
    fn on_signal(&self, _signal: &SessionSignal, _ctx: &ChannelContext) {}
    fn set_fallback(&self, _text: String) {}
    fn finish(&self, state: &ConductorState, ctx: &ChannelContext) -> i32;
}
```

The runner is shape-agnostic: subscribes the strategy to `conductor.subscribe(...)`, runs `on_start`, seeds `state` with the current snapshot, submits each prompt in order via `conductor.submit(...)`, hands the final `ConductorState` to `finish`, and always tears the subscription down.

| Shape | `on_start` | `on_signal` | `finish` writes |
|-------|-----------|-------------|-----------------|
| `OneshotShape::Text` | — | accumulates each `SessionSignal::Text { delta }` | one clean final line (accumulated answer, or snapshot fallback) |
| `OneshotShape::Ndjson` | a `{"type":"signal","name":"start","body":{}}` frame | frames every signal via `signal_to_frame` | a `{"type":"signal","name":"end","body":{phase,usage,fault}}` frame |

```rust
pub struct OneshotRequest {
    pub shape: OneshotShape,        // Text | Ndjson
    pub prompts: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    pub images: Vec<ChannelImage>,  // mediaType + dataBase64, ride the first prompt
}
```

*Text shape:* `TextStrategy` collects every `SessionSignal::Text { delta }` into a `Mutex<String>` and emits the answer **once, clean** in `finish`. Thinking deltas, tool frames, bookkeeping signals are ignored. Two behaviours mirror the framework `OneShotRunner`: **snapshot fallback** — when nothing streamed and the run settled cleanly, `run_oneshot` resolves `ctx.conductor.final_assistant_text().await` and installs it via `set_fallback` before `finish` (the async read can't live in the sync `finish`); **fault report** — when settled state is `ConductorPhase::Faulted`, `finish` writes a single `run failed: <message>` line to `LineSink::write_error` (stderr) then returns exit `1`.

*NDJSON shape:* `NdjsonStrategy` streams every conductor signal as one framed line. Reachable only by constructing `OneshotRequest { shape: OneshotShape::Ndjson, … }` directly (not from a CLI flag). Emits:

```text
{"type":"signal","name":"start","body":{}}
{"type":"signal","name":"text","body":{"kind":"text","delta":"…"}}
{"type":"signal","name":"tool_start","body":{"kind":"tool_start","id":"…","name":"bash"}}
… {"type":"signal","name":"end","body":{"phase":"…","usage":{…},"fault":null}}
```

`on_start` emits the opening `start`; `on_signal` frames each `SessionSignal` through `signal_to_frame` (separator-safe `encode_line`); `finish` emits the closing `end` carrying settled `phase`, cumulative `usage`, and `fault` (`null` when none).

`inert_dialog()` is the shared `DialogBridge` for headless runs: every `ask()` resolves immediately with the caller's fallback and every `tell()` is dropped, so the agent never wedges with no driver attached.

**The link channel.** A long-lived bidirectional JSON-RPC 2.0 conversation; `LinkRunner` serves `session_ops()` over stdin/stdout:

```text
-> {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"lnk-1","method":"submit","params":{"input":"hi"}}
<- {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"lnk-1","result":{"model":"…","streaming":false,"sessionId":"…","usage":{…}}}
```

`LinkRunner::run` builds one `Conductor`, mints `session_ops()` once, and pumps complete framed lines off the boot `InputSource` (which splits on `\n`) in arrival order:

```rust
while let Some(line) = ctx.io.input.next_line().await {
    let trimmed = line.trim();
    if trimmed.is_empty() { continue; }   // ignore blank lines
    handle_link_line(&registry, &channel, trimmed).await;
}
EXIT_OK                                   // EOF ends the loop with a success exit code
```

Each line is handled to settlement before the next is read (the framework `WireRunner`'s serialized discipline) — a sequential pump, one request at a time. (The TS `ChannelContext` doc-comment notes a concurrent `inflight` discipline; the Rust crate ships no such standalone server — the only link path is this sequential loop.)

`handle_link_line(registry, channel, line)` mirrors the framework `WireRunner::handle_line`:
- A **malformed** line → a single `Reply::Err` carrying `op_error::PARSE` (`-32700`), message `"malformed JSON request line"`, empty-string id (`RequestId::Str(String::new())`); loop continues.
- A well-formed `OpRequest` has `params` extracted (`request.params.clone().unwrap_or(Value::Null)`) and dispatched via `dispatch(registry, &request.method, params, channel)`.
- A request with an `id` gets exactly one correlated reply — `Reply::Ok` on success, `Reply::Err` on failure — framed through `encode_line`.
- A request with **no** `id` is a notification: dispatched for effect, never replied to.

A malformed line, unknown method, invalid params, or handler error all keep the loop alive; EOF (`next_line()` → `None`) ends it with `EXIT_OK`.

**The wire contract (`channels::contract`).** Frozen type seam (only shapes + inert pure constants). JSON-RPC 2.0: a request is `OpRequest { jsonrpc, id?, method, params? }`; a reply is `Reply::Ok(ReplyOk { jsonrpc, id, result })` or `Reply::Err(ReplyErr { jsonrpc, id, error })`. `Reply` is `#[serde(untagged)]` (serde discriminates by presence of `result`/`error` — the TS `isReplyOk` narrowing; `Reply::is_ok()` is the Rust accessor).

```rust
pub const PROTOCOL_VERSION: &str = "2.0";       // stamped on every framed envelope
pub const REQUEST_ID_PREFIX: &str = "lnk-";     // driver mints lnk-<base36 now>-<seq>
```

`RequestId` is `#[serde(untagged)]` over `Str(String)`/`Num(i64)`. The driver mints string ids; numeric ids are accepted and round-trip.

The `op_error` module pins the closed JSON-RPC error code set:

| Constant | Code | Meaning |
|----------|------|---------|
| `op_error::PARSE` | `-32700` | the framed line was not valid JSON |
| `op_error::INVALID_REQUEST` | `-32600` | the frame was not a well-formed request |
| `op_error::UNKNOWN_OP` | `-32601` | no operation registered under `method` |
| `op_error::INVALID_PARAMS` | `-32602` | `params` failed the operation schema |
| `op_error::HANDLER_FAILED` | `-32000` | the operation handler errored |

`OpError { code: i32, message: String, data: Option<Value> }` frames as `{code, message, data?}` (`data` omitted when absent). Typed dialog frames: `Ask` (`type:"ask"`), `AskAnswer` (`type:"answer"`), `Tell` (`type:"tell"`), `Signal` (`type:"signal"`), each carrying a zero-variant tag enum (`AskTag::Ask`, `AnswerTag::Answer`, `TellTag::Tell`, `SignalTag::Signal`) so the `"type"` literal is type-pinned.

```rust
#[derive(Clone)]                                  // cheap: every field is Arc-shared
pub struct ChannelContext {
    pub conductor: Arc<Conductor>,
    pub out: Arc<dyn LineSink>,
    pub dialog: Arc<dyn DialogBridge>,
}
```

Unlike the TS contract, the Rust context does NOT carry a framer — framing is the pure `crate::core::ndjson` primitive (re-homed by `channels::framer`), so the sink only receives already-framed lines.

The injectable transport seams:

```rust
pub trait LineSink: Send + Sync {
    fn write(&self, chunk: &str);            // one already-framed, \n-terminated line
    fn write_error(&self, chunk: &str) { /* default routes to process stderr */ }
}
#[async_trait::async_trait]
pub trait LineSource: Send + Sync {
    async fn next_chunk(&self) -> Option<String>;   // None at end-of-stream
}
```

The production sink is `boot::runners::StdoutSink` (implements `LineSink` over `print!`, inherits default `write_error` to stderr). `ChannelTimings` carries `Duration` budgets — `DEFAULT_CHANNEL_TIMINGS` is `startup` 1500 ms · `shutdown` 1200 ms · `request` 45 s · `dialog` 90 s (TS carried these as milliseconds; Rust holds `Duration`).

**The operation registry (`channels::protocol`).** One data-driven registry:

```rust
pub struct Op {
    pub method: &'static str,
    pub handle: Box<
        dyn for<'a> Fn(Value, &'a ChannelContext)
            -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<Value, OpError>> + Send + 'a>>
            + Send + Sync,
    >,
}
pub type OpRegistry = HashMap<&'static str, Op>;
```

Keyed by the same string as each op's `method`, so dispatch is one lookup and the served set is exactly the keys. Helpers: `dispatch(registry, method, params, ctx)` (lone dispatch path; an unregistered method → `UnknownOpError::new(method).into_op_error()` carrying `op_error::UNKNOWN_OP` `-32601` and `data: {"method": <name>}`), `has_op(registry, method)`, `methods_of(registry)` (sorted names). `UnknownOpError::CODE` is the frozen `-32601`. Per-op params deserialize through a private `parse_params::<P>(params)` that lowers a schema mismatch to `op_error::INVALID_PARAMS` — a typed validation failure becomes a `Reply::Err`, never a panic.

**Session ops and the snapshot.** `session_ops() -> OpRegistry` builds the concrete frozen registry; each op delegates to `ctx.conductor`:

| Method | Conductor call | Params | Reply |
|--------|----------------|--------|-------|
| `submit` | `ctx.conductor.submit(p.input).await` | `SubmitParams { input }` | `LinkSnapshot` |
| `abort` | `ctx.conductor.abort().await` | — | `LinkSnapshot` |
| `snapshot` | `ctx.conductor.snapshot()` | — | `LinkSnapshot` |
| `resume` | (params parsed; current snapshot) | `ResumeParams { sessionId }` | `LinkSnapshot` |
| `listModels` | reads `ctx.conductor.model_id()` | — | `[{ "id", "active": true }]` |
| `cycleModel` | `ctx.conductor.select_model(p.model_id)` | `CycleModelParams { modelId }` | `LinkSnapshot` |

Method names and snapshot field casing are kept **verbatim** (`submit`, `listModels`, `cycleModel`, `sessionId`, `autoCondense`, `messageCount`, `queuedCount`, …) for cross-host compatibility. Param structs carry serde renames:

```rust
pub struct SubmitParams { pub input: String }
pub struct ResumeParams { #[serde(rename = "sessionId")] pub session_id: String }
pub struct CycleModelParams { #[serde(rename = "modelId")] pub model_id: String }
pub struct ModelEntry { pub id: String, pub active: bool }
```

`listModels` currently returns only the single active model entry; `cycleModel` routes through `select_model` (TS `cycleModel`/`selectModel` share one path); `resume` parses params for wire-validity but replies with the current snapshot at this milestone.

`project_snapshot(state, extra) -> LinkSnapshot` reshapes a `ConductorState` into the flat wire snapshot:

```rust
pub struct LinkSnapshot {
    pub model: String,
    pub thinking: ThinkingLevel,
    pub streaming: bool,
    pub condensing: bool,
    pub faulted: bool,
    #[serde(rename = "sessionId")] pub session_id: String,
    #[serde(rename = "sessionFile", default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub session_file: Option<String>,
    #[serde(rename = "autoCondense")] pub auto_condense: bool,
    #[serde(rename = "messageCount")] pub message_count: u64,
    #[serde(rename = "queuedCount")] pub queued_count: u64,
    pub usage: Usage,
}
```

Busy flags read off the coarse `ConductorPhase`: `streaming` is `Streaming | Tooling` (tooling counts as streaming on the wire), `condensing` is `Condensing`, `faulted` is `Faulted`. `thinking` defaults to `DEFAULT_THINKING = ThinkingLevel::Off`; `auto_condense` defaults `true`, counts to `0`. `usage` rides through as `indusagi::llmgateway::contract::Usage`. Field **order** is the serde struct order (with `serde_json`'s `preserve_order`), mirroring TS `JSON.stringify` — the byte-compat contract golden tests pin; `sessionFile` is **omitted** (not nulled) when absent. `SnapshotExtra` supplies fields the conductor doesn't surface on bare state (`thinking`, `session_file`, `auto_condense`, `message_count`, `queued_count`).

**NDJSON framing (`channels::framer`).** One JSON value per line; a pure encoder (`encode_line`) plus a stateful cross-chunk decoder (`LineCodec`/`decode_lines`), both I/O-free. Correctness pin: **U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR)** and **U+2029 (PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR)** are legal inside a JSON string but break a naive splitter, and `serde_json` (like TS `JSON.stringify`) emits them raw. `encode_line` rewrites both to `\uXXXX` escapes; the decoder splits strictly on line feed (U+000A) only.

```rust
pub fn encode_line<T: Serialize + ?Sized>(value: &T) -> String {
    let json = serde_json::to_string(value).unwrap_or_else(|_| "null".to_string());
    let mut line = escape_separators(&json).into_owned();   // U+2028/U+2029 escaped
    line.push('\n');                                          // exactly one terminator
    line
}
```

`encode_line` never panics (a serialize failure folds to a `null` line); the fast path is allocation-free when neither separator is present. `LineCodec` is the pull-model decoder: `push(chunk) -> Result<Vec<Value>, DecodeError>` buffers a chunk and returns every complete line (parsed as `serde_json::Value`), retaining a partial trailing line; `flush() -> Result<Option<Value>, DecodeError>` drains a final newline-unterminated frame at EOS. Whitespace-only lines are skipped; an invalid line short-circuits with a `DecodeError` carrying the offending text. `decode_lines(source)` drains a whole `LineSource` to ordered values. `NdjsonFramer` is the bundled zero-sized handle proxying `encode_line`/`codec`/`decode_lines`. (At M-channels the one-shot NDJSON strategy carries a local behaviour-identical `encode_line` inside `channels::protocol`, to be folded onto `channels::framer::encode_line`.)

**The dialog bridge.** The whole dialog surface (multiple-choice, confirm, free-text, editor sessions, notifications, status, titles) reduces to two primitives on the `DialogBridge` trait:

```rust
pub trait DialogBridge: Send + Sync {
    fn ask<'a>(
        &'a self, kind: &'a str, payload: Option<Value>, fallback: Value,
    ) -> Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Value> + Send + 'a>>;
    fn tell(&self, kind: &str, payload: Option<Value>);
}
```

`ask` is the round-trip primitive (emits an `Ask` frame, resolves with the matching answer or its `fallback` on timeout/dismissal). `tell` is fire-and-forget. Every concrete dialog method is expressed in these two; the seam carries the value as a `Value`, the caller deserializes its `T`. The headless impl is `InertDialog` (`inert_dialog() -> Arc<dyn DialogBridge>`): every `ask` resolves immediately with its fallback, every `tell` is dropped. When a console is attached, the interactive Dialogs supply a live bridge.

**Signal to frame mapping.** `signal_to_frame(signal: &SessionSignal) -> Signal` projects a conductor signal onto a wire frame: `name` is the signal's `kind` discriminant, `body` is the whole serialized signal. `SessionSignal` is `#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]`, so kind is read off the serde-tagged JSON:

```rust
pub fn signal_to_frame(signal: &SessionSignal) -> Signal {
    let body = serde_json::to_value(signal).unwrap_or(Value::Null);
    let name = body.get("kind").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();
    Signal { frame: SignalTag::Signal, name, body }
}
```

The eleven `SessionSignal` kinds that flow onto the wire:

| `name` | Body fields | Meaning |
|--------|-------------|---------|
| `prompt` | `text` | the user's turn was accepted |
| `text` | `delta` | a chunk of assistant answer text |
| `thinking` | `delta` | a chunk of reasoning text |
| `tool_start` | `id`, `name` | a tool invocation began |
| `tool_end` | `id`, `name`, `ok`, `output?`, `diff?` | a tool invocation finished |
| `turn_end` | `usage` | the assistant turn settled |
| `persisted` | `entry_id` | the latest node was committed |
| `compacted` | — | the transcript was condensed |
| `fault` | `fault` | a typed `ConductorFault` occurred |
| `queue` | `count` | the pending-input queue depth changed |
| `idle` | — | the conductor is ready for input |

The one-shot `start`/`end` frames are channel-synthesized (not conductor signals), carrying `body:{}` and `body:{phase,usage,fault}`.

**Source files:** `channels/mod.rs` (module map + crate-root re-export barrel); `channels/contract.rs` (JSON-RPC envelope, `RequestId`, dialog frames, `Signal`, `LinkSnapshot`, one-shot shapes, session-op param shapes, `ChannelContext` + `LineSink`/`LineSource`, `ChannelTimings`, constants); `channels/framer.rs` (`encode_line`, `LineCodec`/`decode_lines`, `DecodeError`, `NdjsonFramer`); `channels/protocol.rs` (`Op`/`OpRegistry`/`dispatch`/`has_op`/`methods_of`/`UnknownOpError`, `session_ops` + `project_snapshot`, the one-shot strategies + `run_oneshot` + `inert_dialog`, `signal_to_frame`). The runners wiring these into CLI modes live in `boot::runners` (`OneShotRunner` for `-p`/`--print`, `LinkRunner` + `handle_link_line` for `--json`) over the `StdoutSink` `LineSink`.

#### Sessions

`induscode::core::sessions` is the catalog-and-navigation layer over a workspace's persisted conversations. Where the conductor drives one live transcript, `SessionLibrary` owns the whole directory of saved sessions — enumerating, opening, renaming, deleting them, and projecting a loaded session DAG into the flat shapes a chooser UI resumes, branches, and forks from. It re-implements **no** transcript parsing: it sits directly on the framework session DAG (`indusagi::runtime::store::SessionStore`), reads its `.jsonl` files, and reduces nodes to short display previews. Reached as `use induscode::core::sessions::SessionLibrary;`.

The framework `SessionStore` is the writer of the append-only DAG (one content-hashed node per turn, plus a head marker tracking the active leaf). `SessionLibrary`'s own logic is purely directory enumeration, tree flattening, and text reduction. The framework `Turn` carries the `user`/`assistant`/`tool` roles every projection needs; the conductor's richer 6-role node is a future swap, with the `SessionStore` seam staying identical.

**Module layout** — three files under `crates/induscode/src/core/sessions/`:

| Module | Path | Contents |
|--------|------|----------|
| `sessions` | `core/sessions/mod.rs` | Barrel; `pub use` of `BranchNode`, `PriorTurn`, `SavedSession`, `SessionLibrary`, `SessionLibraryOptions`. |
| `sessions::contract` | `core/sessions/contract.rs` | The three pure value types — display-only projections with stable string ids + short previews, no framework message objects. |
| `sessions::library` | `core/sessions/library.rs` | `SessionLibrary`, `SessionLibraryOptions`, and the pure helpers. |

**Public API:**

| Name | Kind | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `SessionLibrary` | struct | Collection-level handle over a workspace `sessions/` dir. `async list`/`open`/`rename`/`remove` manage files; pure `tree`/`prior_turns` project a loaded `SessionGraph`; `path_of`/`directory` expose locations. |
| `SessionLibraryOptions` | struct | Construction input: a single `sessions_dir: PathBuf` at the workspace `sessions/` dir. |
| `SavedSession` | struct | Catalog row: `id` (filename stem), `path`, plus best-effort `name`/`last_modified`/`size`/`message_count`/`preview` that are `None` on a shallow listing. |
| `BranchNode` | struct | Row in the flattened DAG: `id`, `parent`, render-ready `label`, `depth`, `is_leaf`, `is_current`. |
| `PriorTurn` | struct | Fork candidate — a past user turn with `entry_id` (fork-target node id), full `text`, trimmed single-line `preview`. |

```rust
pub struct SessionLibrary { dir: PathBuf, store: SessionStore }

impl SessionLibrary {
    pub fn new(options: SessionLibraryOptions) -> Self;
    pub fn directory(&self) -> &Path;
    pub async fn list(&self, deep: bool) -> Vec<SavedSession>;
    pub async fn open(&self, id: &str) -> Option<SessionGraph>;
    pub async fn rename(&self, from_id: &str, to_id: &str) -> std::io::Result<PathBuf>;
    pub async fn remove(&self, id: &str) -> std::io::Result<bool>;
    pub fn path_of(&self, id: &str) -> PathBuf;
    pub fn tree(&self, graph: &SessionGraph) -> Vec<BranchNode>;
    pub fn prior_turns(&self, graph: &SessionGraph) -> Vec<PriorTurn>;
}
```

`SessionLibrary::new` builds a framework `SessionStore` rooted at `sessions_dir`. All disk I/O runs on `tokio::fs` so the `async` surface never blocks the runtime. The value structs are minimal display-only records (stable string ids + short previews, no framework `Turn` payloads). Field names are idiomatic snake_case (`last_modified`, `message_count`, `entry_id`, `is_leaf`, `is_current`), unlike TS/Python camelCase.

```rust
pub struct SavedSession {
    pub id: String,
    pub path: std::path::PathBuf,
    pub name: Option<String>,
    pub last_modified: Option<u64>,   // epoch milliseconds
    pub size: Option<u64>,            // bytes on disk
    pub message_count: Option<usize>, // conversational nodes on the active branch
    pub preview: Option<String>,      // opening-turn excerpt
}
pub struct BranchNode {
    pub id: String, pub parent: Option<String>, pub label: String,
    pub depth: usize, pub is_leaf: bool, pub is_current: bool,
}
pub struct PriorTurn { pub entry_id: String, pub text: String, pub preview: String }
```

All three derive `Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq`.

**The branchable session DAG.** The framework `SessionStore` persists a conversation as a content-addressed branchable DAG, not a flat list. Each `indusagi::runtime::contract::SessionNode` carries one `Turn`, names its `parent` by hash, and has an `id` that is a content hash of the turn plus its lineage (`hash_node(parent, turn, created_at)`):

```rust
pub struct SessionNode {
    pub id: String,            // content hash of (turn + parent + created_at)
    pub parent: Option<String>, // None for a root
    pub turn: Turn,            // User | Assistant | Tool
    pub created_at: i64,       // epoch milliseconds
}
```

Branching is two nodes sharing a parent. `SessionGraph` verbs:

| Method | Signature | Role |
|--------|-----------|------|
| `all` | `fn all(&self) -> Vec<SessionNode>` | Every node; the source `tree` flattens. |
| `get` | `fn get(&self, node_id: &str) -> Option<&SessionNode>` | Look up one node; the library walks the parent chain. |
| `leaf` | `fn leaf(&self) -> Option<&str>` | The active head's leaf id; drives `is_current` + the active-branch walk. |
| `size` | `fn size(&self) -> usize` | Node count. |
| `append` | `fn append(&mut self, turn: Turn) -> SessionNode` | Chain a new turn onto the head; the conductor's write verb. |
| `branch_from` | `fn branch_from(&mut self, node_id: &str) -> Result<SessionNode, String>` | Move the head to an existing node so the next `append` forks there. |
| `path_to` | `fn path_to(&self, leaf: &str) -> Result<Vec<Turn>, String>` | The linear root→leaf turn context (turns only, no ids). |
| `resume` | `fn resume(&mut self, leaf: &str) -> Result<Vec<Turn>, String>` | `branch_from` + `path_to`. |

Forking is repointing the head at an earlier node: `graph.branch_from(id)` advances the head so the next `append` becomes that node's child, leaving every existing node untouched. `SessionLibrary` gives a UI two views: `tree(graph)` flattens the **whole** DAG into an ordered `Vec<BranchNode>`; `prior_turns(graph)` walks **only** the active root→leaf branch and returns its user prompts as `Vec<PriorTurn>` fork candidates.

**Listing: shallow vs deep.** `list(false)` returns rows from file metadata only (`id`, `path`, `size`, `last_modified`) so a large directory lists fast. `list(true)` also opens each transcript to fill `message_count` (count of conversational `User`/`Assistant`/`Tool` nodes along the active branch) and the opening-turn `preview`/`name`. Internally `list` calls `session_ids` (async dir scan via `tokio::fs::read_dir`, keeps only `.jsonl`, strips suffix to the bare stem — missing dir yields `[]`), builds a `shallow_row` or `deep_row` per id, then sorts with `by_most_recent` (most-recently-modified first, ties by id ascending). `deep_row` opens the session; if the graph hydrates, walks active-branch nodes, counts conversational ones, finds the first `User` node, reduces its text into `preview` (also copied into `name`, matching TS); if `open` returns `None`, falls back to a shallow row. A console picker seeds with a shallow list, loads deep lazily.

**Opening and resuming.** `open(id)` hydrates a saved session into a live `SessionGraph`, or returns `None` when no file exists. It delegates to `self.store.load_session(id)` (reads the `.jsonl`, replays each line through the migrator pipeline, collects node records, tracks the last head marker as the leaf, reconstructs via `SessionGraph::hydrate`; a blank/corrupt line is skipped). The library first checks the file exists (private `missing`) to preserve the TS `null`/`None` result for an unknown id (the store would otherwise hand back an empty graph). `id` is always the **bare filename stem**, never a path.

**Navigation projections** (`tree`, `prior_turns`) are **pure** — no I/O, require a pre-opened `SessionGraph`. `tree(graph)` reads `graph.all()` + `graph.leaf()`, builds a `children_of` map keyed by parent id (`None` for roots), tracks a `has_children` set, then depth-first preorder-walks every root emitting one `BranchNode` per node: `label` (depth-indented role-aware one-liner via `label_for`), `depth` (root = 0), `is_leaf` (no node names it parent), `is_current` (id equals the active head leaf). `prior_turns(graph)` walks the active branch via the private `active_branch_nodes`, keeps `Turn::User` nodes with non-empty reduced text, emits one `PriorTurn` each with `entry_id`, full trimmed `text`, single-line `preview`. Because `path_to` returns bare `Vec<Turn>` without ids, `prior_turns` cannot use it directly — it needs nodes (id + turn) to honor `PriorTurn.entry_id`, so `active_branch_nodes` walks the parent chain from the head; an empty graph yields `[]`.

**Forking from a prior turn.** Pick a `PriorTurn` and hand its `entry_id` to `graph.branch_from(...)` — the library produces the candidate, the graph performs the fork:

```rust
let mut graph = lib.open("alpha").await.expect("session");
let candidates = lib.prior_turns(&graph);
graph.branch_from(&candidates[0].entry_id).unwrap();  // Err on an unknown id
// the next graph.append(...) becomes a child of that node, on a new branch
```

The library's job ends at projection — it never mutates the DAG. Forking (`branch_from`), resuming (`resume`), appending (`append`) are all framework `SessionGraph` verbs, persisted by the conductor through the `SessionStore`.

**Rename and delete** (both on `tokio::fs`). `rename(from_id, to_id)` validates the source exists and target id is absent, ensures the directory exists, then `tokio::fs::rename`; returns the new abs path. Errs `ErrorKind::NotFound` (`SessionLibrary.rename: no session "<from_id>"`) or `ErrorKind::AlreadyExists` (`SessionLibrary.rename: session "<to_id>" already exists`). Rename does **not** rewrite the in-file head marker (which still names the old leaf id) — the store tolerates this because the leaf is content-derived, not the filename. `remove(id)` unlinks idempotently: `Ok(true)` when removed, `Ok(false)` when nothing to delete (including a racing `NotFound`), propagating only other I/O errors.

**On-disk layout.** Each session is its own append-only `.jsonl` file under the workspace `sessions/` root. Every line is one JSON record of two shapes, written by `SessionStore::append_node`:

```jsonl
{"type":"node","node":{"id":"<hash>","parent":null,"turn":{"role":"user","blocks":[{"kind":"text","text":"…"}]},"createdAt":1700000000000}}
{"type":"head","leaf":"<hash>"}
```

Appending writes a node record followed by a fresh head record naming it, so the **last** head marker always names the live leaf. On-disk wire fields stay camelCase (`createdAt`, `sessionId`) for JSONL parity across editions, even though in-memory Rust structs are snake_case.

```rust
const SESSION_FILE_EXT: &str = ".jsonl";   // matches SessionStore's SESSION_EXT
const PREVIEW_LIMIT: usize = 72;           // single-line preview cap
```

The TS agent hard-coded `.ndjson`; the Rust library matches the framework `SessionStore`'s `.jsonl`, closing the historical mismatch. Sessions are partitioned **per working directory**. `SessionLibrary` always receives the already-scoped directory (e.g. `…/sessions/--my-proj--`) — it does no slugging. The slug helper lives in boot:

```rust
// induscode::boot::resources
pub fn session_scope_dir(sessions_root: &Path, cwd: &str) -> PathBuf {
    sessions_root.join(format!("--{}--", slug_cwd(cwd)))
}
```

Both writer (conductor) and reader (library) reach it through this one shared helper.

**How boot wires it.** In `induscode::boot::runners`, `session_scope_dir_for(inv, &ctx.workspace)` computes the scoped directory; the conductor's `SessionStore` is rooted there for writes, and a `SessionLibrary` rooted at the same dir serves the console's resume/branch/fork overlays:

```rust
let sessions_dir = session_scope_dir_for(inv, &ctx.workspace);
let store = indusagi::runtime::store::SessionStore::new(sessions_dir.clone());
// the same sessions_dir is also handed to a SessionLibrary for the console reads.
```

Resume flags (parsed by launch `FLAG_SPECS` into the boot `Invocation`):

| Flag | Aliases | Behavior |
|------|---------|----------|
| `--continue` | `-c` | `Invocation.continue_latest` — resume the newest session in this cwd (first row of the newest-first `list()`, by bare id). |
| `--resume` | `-r` | `Invocation.resume` — open a picker over the listed sessions and resume the chosen id (or start fresh). |

Both loaders share the single `list()` call and the cwd-scoped directory; resume always goes by the bare session **id** (filename stem), never a path.

**Pure helpers** (free functions at the bottom of `library.rs`, each a 1:1 TS port):

| Helper | Signature | Purpose |
|--------|-----------|---------|
| `active_branch_nodes` | `fn(graph: &SessionGraph) -> Vec<SessionNode>` | Walk the parent chain from the head leaf and reverse → root→leaf nodes; `[]` for empty graph. |
| `is_conversational` | `fn(node: &SessionNode) -> bool` | `true` for `Turn::User`/`Assistant`/`Tool` — the roles counted into `message_count`. |
| `by_most_recent` | `fn(a, b: &SavedSession) -> Ordering` | Newest `last_modified` first (a `None` mtime sorts as 0 = last), ties by id ascending. |
| `label_for` | `fn(node, depth) -> String` | Depth-indented role-aware label: `user: <preview>`, `assistant`, or `tool: <name>`. |
| `tool_name_of` | `fn(_turn: &Turn) -> String` | Returns the `"tool"` placeholder — a framework tool turn carries `ToolResult` blocks keyed by `call_id`, no tool *name* field. |
| `message_text` | `fn(turn: &Turn) -> String` | Concatenate `Block::Text` segments, ignoring thinking/image/tool blocks; `""` for none. |
| `preview_of` | `fn(text, limit) -> String` | Collapse whitespace; if over `limit`, cut to `limit - 1` by char (UTF-8 safe) and append `…` (U+2026). |
| `collapse_whitespace` | `fn(text: &str) -> String` | `split_whitespace().join(" ")` (Rust analogue of TS `text.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim()`). |

`label_for` only renders the three framework roles; the TS `condense`/`system`/`note` arms belong to a future 6-role conductor node and are omitted.

**Parity notes** (a clean port of TS `src/sessions`, mirrored by Python `induscode.sessions`; contracts match field-for-field):

| Concern | TS / Python | Rust |
|---------|-------------|------|
| Field casing | camelCase (`lastModified`, `messageCount`, `entryId`, `isLeaf`, `isCurrent`) | snake_case |
| File extension | `.ndjson` (TS hard-coded) | `.jsonl` (matches framework `SessionStore`) |
| Backing store | conductor `TranscriptStore` over `fsBackend` + `replay` | `indusagi::runtime::store::SessionStore` / `SessionGraph` |
| Node roles | 6-role conductor node (incl. `condense`/`system`/`note`) | 3-role framework `Turn`; richer node a future swap |
| Async runtime | `asyncio.to_thread` / Promises | `tokio::fs` directly |
| List signature | `list(deep=False)` keyword | `list(deep: bool)` positional |

On-disk JSONL wire fields stay camelCase across all editions, so a `.jsonl` written by the TS/Python agent loads unchanged in Rust (modulo the extension rename).

**Gotchas:** `last_modified` is epoch-MS file mtime (`duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).as_millis() as u64`), `created_at` is `i64` epoch ms; `.jsonl` not `.ndjson`; newest-first listing; `tree`/`prior_turns` are pure (call `open` first); `open` returns `None` for an unknown id; rename does not rewrite the head; forking is a framework verb; `tool:` label is always `tool: tool` (no name field); scoping is boot's job.

#### Window budget

`window_budget` is `induscode`'s own context-window budgeting and compaction engine — a 1:1 port of the TS `src/window-budget` onto the Rust gateway/runtime primitives. It measures transcript tokens, decides **when** and **where** to cut, folds the dropped head into one synthetic digest via an injectable `ModelInvoker`, and reclaims context with a free microcompact pre-pass and a recently-read-file rehydrate post-pass. The factory `create_condenser` yields a `Condenser` structurally identical to the Conductor's `CondenseFn`, so it drops into the auto-compaction seam with no adapter — and runs fully network-free by default. It is built **on top of** the framework but is deliberately a *separate* engine from the framework's own `runtime` memory compactor.

**The pipeline.** The bare `create_condenser` factory ties three pure pieces; the full *runner* pipeline (in the conductor glue) wraps two more passes around them:

| Stage | Question | Entry point | Where it runs |
|-------|----------|-------------|---------------|
| **Microcompact** | What stale tool output can we blank for free? | `clear_stale_tool_results(messages, keep_recent)` | runner only (pre-pass) |
| **Gate** | *When* are we over budget? | `is_over_budget(messages, card, policy)` | factory + runner |
| **Slice** | *Where* do we cut? | `plan_slice(messages, policy)` → `CondensePlan` | factory + runner |
| **Condense** | *How* do we compress the head? | `summarize(dropped, deps)` → `Summary` | factory + runner |
| **Rehydrate** | What freshly-read files should we restore? | `rehydrate_recent_reads(dropped, kept, opts)` | runner only (post-pass) |

`create_condenser` stitches gate + slice + condense into one boxed async `Condenser`. On any no-op path it returns the **input unchanged**; otherwise `[summary.message, ...kept]`, a strictly smaller transcript. The runner-level `condense_transcript` additionally microcompacts before slicing, honors a `force` flag for manual `/compact`, and rehydrates dropped reads under a strict-shrink count guard.

**The Message enum (`message.rs`).** The rich `AgentMessage` analog the whole crate dispatches on. The framework only ships the gateway-neutral 3-role `Turn` (`indusagi::llmgateway::contract::Turn`), whose tool results are *nested* as a `Block::ToolResult` inside a `Turn::Tool`. The agent's transcript is richer: **seven variants**, and decisively `ToolResult` and `BashExecution` are **top-level messages, not nested blocks** — the single fact forcing its own enum:

```rust
pub enum Content { Text(String), Blocks(Vec<Block>) }

pub enum Message {
    User { content: Content, timestamp: i64 },
    Assistant { content: Vec<Block>, error_message: Option<String> },
    ToolResult { tool_call_id: String, tool_name: String, content: Vec<Block>, is_error: bool },
    BashExecution { command: String, output: String, exit_code: Option<i32> },
    Custom { custom_type: String, content: Content },
    BranchSummary { summary: String, from_id: String },
    CompactionSummary { summary: String, tokens_before: u64 },
}
```

Owned **here** and re-exported (`pub use message::{Content, Message}`), so both consumers reach it without a cycle (the conductor sees `crate::window_budget::Message`). `Block` is reused from the gateway (`indusagi::llmgateway::contract::Block`). `BranchSummary` and `CompactionSummary` are kept **distinct** because the flattener's `digest:` case re-reads both on an iterative re-condense pass.

**The contract layer (`contract.rs`).** Only value shapes — no behavior, I/O, or prompt strings:

| Name | Kind | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| `BudgetPolicy` | `Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq` struct | `trigger_ratio: f64` (fraction in `(0, 1]`), `keep_recent: u64` (**tokens** of recent tail kept verbatim), `reserve_tokens: Option<u64>`. No magic literals. |
| `TokenEstimate` | `Clone, Copy` struct | `context_tokens: u64`, `context_window: u64`, `anchored: bool` (`true` when based on a real provider `Usage`). |
| `CondensePlan` | `Clone, Debug, PartialEq` struct | `cut: usize`, `kept: Vec<Message>` (`messages[cut..]`), `dropped: Vec<Message>` (`messages[..cut]`). `cut == 0` means nothing condensable. |
| `Summary` | `Clone, Debug, PartialEq` struct | A single synthetic `message: Message` + `covered_count: usize`. |
| `CondenseScope` | `Clone, Copy, Default` enum | `Session` (`#[default]`, in-place condense) / `Branch` (abandoned-branch archival, no verbatim tail). |

`TokenEstimate::anchored` is **declared for parity and unused by the gate** — `is_over_budget`/`budget_limit` consult only the heuristic. The conductor tracks real usage (`CondenseOpts.context_tokens`) but does not feed it to the gate (heuristic-only gate ships for v0.2). `contract.rs` composes the framework vocabulary (`Block`/`Turn`/`ModelCard`/`Conversation`/`Emission`/`StreamOptions` from `indusagi::llmgateway::contract`) rather than re-declaring it; the completer seam chooses the framework's object-safe `ModelInvoker` trait (over a bare `Fn`) for parity with the framework's own `memory::compactor::summarize`.

**Budget math (`budget/`, pure arithmetic, no I/O).** *Estimate (`budget/estimate.rs`):* no tokenizer call. `estimate_message_tokens` walks each message's serialized payload:

```text
cost = ceil(serialized_chars / CHARS_PER_TOKEN) + framing + images * IMAGE_TOKENS
```

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|----------|-------|---------|
| `CHARS_PER_TOKEN` | `3.6` | Average serialized chars per token (conservative, skews high). |
| `IMAGE_TOKENS` | `1024` | Flat per-image cost (resolution-agnostic; base64 `data_base64` **not** measured). |
| `MESSAGE_FRAMING_TOKENS` | `4` | Per-message role/turn framing. |
| `BLOCK_FRAMING_TOKENS` | `2` | Per structured block. |
| `TOOLCALL_ENVELOPE_TOKENS` | `6` | Per tool call/result envelope (id + name framing). |

`weigh_block` accounts each gateway `Block`: `Text`/`Thinking` bill inner text length; `Image` bills flat (`1` image, `0` chars); `ToolCall` bills `name.chars().count() + safe_stringify(input).chars().count()` (a JSON `null` input contributes nothing); other blocks (`ToolResult`/`Command`) fall through to a generic serialized measurement. Char counting uses `.chars().count()` (Unicode scalar values); `safe_stringify` is the never-panic `serde_json::to_string` analog. `weigh_message` dispatches all seven variants: `User`/`Assistant`/`ToolResult` accumulate per-block framing (assistant tool-call + tool-result both add `TOOLCALL_ENVELOPE_TOKENS`); the four custom variants (`BashExecution`, `Custom`, `BranchSummary`, `CompactionSummary`) weigh string fields plus one block of framing. The estimate is **conservative** (biased high). `estimate_tokens` sums every message (empty → `0`); `prefix_tokens` builds the forward cumulative array (length `n+1`, `result[i]` = tokens of `messages[0..i)`, `result[0] == 0`), monotonically non-decreasing — the invariant the binary search depends on.

*Gate (`budget/gate.rs`):*

```rust
pub fn budget_limit(card: &ModelCard, policy: &BudgetPolicy) -> f64 {
    let reserve = policy.reserve_tokens.unwrap_or(0);
    let usable = card.context_window.saturating_sub(reserve);
    usable as f64 * policy.trigger_ratio
}
pub fn is_over_budget(messages: &[Message], card: &ModelCard, policy: &BudgetPolicy) -> bool {
    estimate_tokens(messages) as f64 > budget_limit(card, policy)
}
```

Optional fixed headroom is carved off the window first (`saturating_sub`, so a reserve larger than the window can never yield a negative limit), then scaled by `trigger_ratio`. Reads `ModelCard.context_window` and fires once the estimate **strictly** exceeds the limit.

*Slice (`budget/slice.rs`):* `plan_slice` partitions into a `dropped` prefix and `kept` suffix via **forward prefix-sum + binary search**: (1) build the cumulative array (total = `prefix[n]`); (2) binary-search the lower bound of `total - keep_recent` over the monotonic `prefix` (O(log n), `lower_bound`); (3) **snap the cut forward** past any leading `ToolResult` (`snap_forward`). **Tool-pair safety**: a `ToolResult` must stay glued to the assistant turn that issued its `tool_call`, so the kept tail may never begin with one — `is_legal_tail_start` returns `false` only for `Message::ToolResult`. If the whole transcript fits in `keep_recent`, or snapping consumes everything (`cut >= n`), `cut` is `0`. `last_user_turn_start(messages)` is the **force-path** boundary: `rposition` of the last `Message::User`, or `None` when no user turn. `/compact` folds everything *before* this index and keeps the final user turn verbatim, always reclaiming context on a multi-turn session.

**The summarize path (`summarize/`).** Does the model call. `summarize` is the **single condensing primitive** — one path for both `Session` and `Branch`; the scope flag only changes the prompt framing line and digest header.

*Prompt assembly (`summarize/prompt.rs`):* `build_summary_prompt(messages, scope, prior)` produces one user-turn string (joining blocks with `\n\n`): a scope framing line; an optional `<carried-digest>…</carried-digest>` block (only when `prior` non-blank); a `<scrollback>…</scrollback>` block holding the flattened transcript; the fixed `SECTION_TEMPLATE` (`# Objective`, `# Guardrails`, `# Status (Shipped / Active / Stuck)`, `# Rationale`, `# Plan`, `# Carryover`). `flatten_transcript` renders each message into `» role:` lines (`TURN_MARK = '»'`): `» you`, `» agent`, `» agent.plan` (thinking), `» agent.call <name>: <json>`, `» tool (<name>)` / `» tool!err (<name>)`, `» shell$ <cmd> [exit N]`, `» note (<type>)`, `» digest`. A `tidy` helper normalizes CRLF and strips trailing horizontal whitespace; empty-rendering messages are skipped. `CONDENSER_BRIEF` is the system prompt framing the model as a *transcript recorder*, not a chat continuation:

```rust
pub const CONDENSER_BRIEF: &str = "You are a transcript recorder for a long-running coding session.\n\
The text you receive is archival data, not a live chat — do NOT reply to it,\n\
continue it, run tools, or ask questions. Your sole job is to distill it into\n\
a compact, faithful digest under the exact headings requested below.\n\
...";
```

*Summarize core (`summarize/condense.rs`):*

```rust
pub async fn summarize(messages: &[Message], deps: SummarizeDeps) -> Summary
pub async fn condense_scope(messages: &[Message], mut deps: SummarizeDeps) -> Summary
```

`summarize` builds a `Conversation { system: Some(CONDENSER_BRIEF.to_string()), turns: vec![Turn::User { blocks: vec![Block::Text { text: prompt }] }], tools: None }` (the gateway `Turn::User` carries `blocks: Vec<Block>`, not a `prompt` field), runs it through the injectable completer once with `StreamOptions { thinking: Some(ThinkingLevel::High), max_output_tokens, cancel, .. }`, folds streamed text via `collect_text`, and wraps the digest as a synthetic `Message::User` stamped with a scope header. Returns `Summary { message, covered_count }`.

| Scope | Digest header |
|-------|---------------|
| `Session` | `[session digest — older turns condensed]` (`DIGEST_HEADER`) |
| `Branch` | `[branch digest — archived from a path not taken]` (`BRANCH_HEADER`) |

`SummarizeDeps` carries `invoke: Option<Arc<dyn ModelInvoker>>`, `scope: CondenseScope` (default `Session`), `prior_digest: Option<String>`, `cancel: Option<CancellationToken>` (→ `StreamOptions.cancel`), `max_tokens: Option<u64>` (→ `StreamOptions.max_output_tokens`); derives `Default`. `collect_text` mirrors the framework `memory::compactor::collectText`: prefer the terminal `Emission::Done` reply's concatenated `Block::Text`, else the accumulated `Emission::Text` deltas; a terminal `Emission::Error` yields `None`. **Network-free and never-raising**: with no `invoke` bound, `summarize` emits a deterministic `local_fallback_digest` (a `# Carryover` section recording the count of elided messages, plus any carried prior digest). An empty reply, stream error, or cancelled stream all degrade to the same local digest — a `Summary` is **always** produced; `summarize` never throws. `condense_scope` pins `CondenseScope::Branch`.

**The condenser factory (`condenser.rs`).**

```rust
pub type Condenser = Box<dyn Fn(Vec<Message>) -> BoxFuture<'static, Vec<Message>> + Send + Sync>;
pub fn create_condenser(deps: CondenserDeps) -> Condenser
pub async fn condense(messages: &[Message], mut deps: SummarizeDeps) -> Summary
```

`create_condenser(deps)` returns a boxed async `Condenser` (structurally the conductor's `CondenseFn`):

```rust
Box::new(move |messages: Vec<Message>| {
    Box::pin(async move {
        let Some(card) = card.as_ref() else { return messages; };          // no window → identity
        if !is_over_budget(&messages, card, &policy) { return messages; }   // under budget → identity
        let plan = plan_slice(&messages, &policy);
        if plan.cut == 0 || plan.dropped.is_empty() { return messages; }    // nothing condensable → identity
        let summary = condense(&plan.dropped, SummarizeDeps {
            invoke, scope: CondenseScope::Session, prior_digest: None, cancel: None, max_tokens: None,
        }).await;
        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(1 + plan.kept.len());
        out.push(summary.message);
        out.extend(plan.kept);
        out
    })
})
```

`CondenserDeps` is all-optional — `invoke: Option<Arc<dyn ModelInvoker>>` (`None` ⇒ network-free local digest), `card: Option<ModelCard>` (`None` ⇒ no window ⇒ identity), `policy: Option<BudgetPolicy>` (default `AUTO_CONDENSE_POLICY`) — so `create_condenser(CondenserDeps::default())` yields a working network-free no-op condenser. `condense` is exported alongside (pins `scope = Session`). **Microcompact and rehydrate are deliberately NOT called here** — the runner applies them, matching TS `createCondenser`.

```rust
pub const AUTO_CONDENSE_POLICY: BudgetPolicy = BudgetPolicy {
    trigger_ratio: 0.75,   // condense once ~¾ of the window is used
    keep_recent: 6000,     // keep ~the last 6k TOKENS of turns verbatim
    reserve_tokens: Some(2048),
};
```

This is the **single** policy the gate and slicer share, so the trigger and cut never disagree.

**Microcompact (`microcompact.rs`).** Blanks stale tool-result bodies for free (no model call) *before* slicing:

```rust
pub fn clear_stale_tool_results(messages: Vec<Message>, keep_recent: usize) -> Option<Vec<Message>>
pub fn compactable_tool_names() -> &'static HashSet<&'static str>
pub const CLEARED_TOOL_RESULT: &str = "[Old tool result content cleared]";
pub const DEFAULT_KEEP_RECENT: usize = 6;
```

`clear_stale_tool_results` walks newest→oldest, keeps the last `keep_recent` (floored at `1`) compactable results verbatim, replaces every older non-cleared one's `content` with a single `CLEARED_TOOL_RESULT` text block. It gates on the **owning assistant `tool_call` id + name** — `collect_compactable_tool_ids` collects `tool_call_id`s whose owning call named a compactable tool; a result whose call is absent is non-compactable. Non-tool messages, control-tool results (e.g. `todo`/`memory`), and already-cleared results are left untouched. The compactable set (read-style + reconstructable edit tools): `read`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`, `glob`, `bash`, `websearch`, `webfetch`, `edit`, `write`. **Identity no-op**: returns `Option<Vec<Message>>` — `None` means "nothing cleared; reuse your input"; the runner does `clear_stale_tool_results(msgs.clone(), 6).unwrap_or(msgs)`.

**Rehydrate (`rehydrate.rs`).** Re-attaches recently-read files dropped by a condense, as synthetic user messages:

```rust
pub fn rehydrate_recent_reads(dropped: &[Message], kept: &[Message], opts: &RehydrateOpts) -> Vec<Message>
pub const RESTORED_FILE_PREFIX: &str = "[Restored file after compaction]";
pub struct RehydrateOpts {
    pub max_files: usize,        // default 5
    pub token_budget: u64,       // default 8000
    pub read_tool_name: String,  // default "read"
}
```

Scans `dropped` for `read` calls + their result bodies (`collect_dropped_reads`, pairing call → result by `tool_call_id`, skipping error/empty bodies, keeping the freshest body when a path is read twice), dedups against paths still visible in `kept` (`collect_visible_read_paths`), sorts survivors most-recent-first, takes up to `max_files`, emits each as a `RESTORED_FILE_PREFIX`-stamped `Message::User` — stopping once the running token estimate (via `estimate_message_tokens`) would exceed `token_budget`, but **always restoring at least the single freshest** even if it alone blows the budget. Restored messages are returned **oldest-first** so they read naturally spliced after the summary. `[]` on nothing to restore.

**How the conductor wires it.** The real consumer is the Conductor's `CondenseFn` seam (`conductor/contract.rs`):

```rust
pub struct CondenseOpts {
    pub force: bool,            // true for manual /compact (cut at last user turn)
    pub model: Option<String>,
    pub context_tokens: u64,    // live occupancy at gate time
}
#[async_trait::async_trait]
pub trait CondenseFn: Send + Sync {
    async fn condense(&self, messages: Vec<Turn>, opts: CondenseOpts) -> Vec<Turn>;
}
```

The default binding is `IdentityCondense` (returns its input unchanged) so a conductor built without a window-budget dep never condenses. When an engine is wired, the conductor binds `WindowBudgetCondense` (`conductor/session_ops.rs`), which adapts the framework-`Turn` model to the rich `Message`, runs the **full** runner pipeline, and bridges back to `Vec<Turn>` via `turn_to_message`/`message_to_turn`/`content_to_blocks` (a framework `Turn::Tool` maps to a `Message::User` carrying the tool-result blocks, because the estimator only needs textual weight).

The runner pipeline `condense_transcript(deps, messages, opts)` (port of TS `condenseTranscript`, distinct from `create_condenser`):

```rust
async fn condense_transcript(deps: &CondenserDeps, messages: Vec<Message>, opts: &CondenseOpts) -> Vec<Message> {
    let cleared = clear_stale_tool_results(messages.clone(), DEFAULT_KEEP_RECENT).unwrap_or(messages.clone());
    let policy = deps.policy.unwrap_or(AUTO_CONDENSE_POLICY);
    let (dropped, kept) = if opts.force {
        match last_user_turn_start(&cleared) {
            Some(cut) if cut > 0 => (cleared[..cut].to_vec(), cleared[cut..].to_vec()),
            _ => return messages,                       // 0/1 turn → nothing to fold
        }
    } else {
        let plan = plan_slice(&cleared, &policy);
        if plan.cut == 0 || plan.dropped.is_empty() { return messages; }
        (plan.dropped, plan.kept)
    };
    let summary = crate::window_budget::condense(&dropped, SummarizeDeps {
        invoke: deps.invoke.clone(), scope: CondenseScope::Session, prior_digest: None, cancel: None, max_tokens: None,
    }).await;
    let restored = restore_under_count_guard(&dropped, &kept);
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(1 + restored.len() + kept.len());
    out.push(summary.message);
    out.extend(restored);
    out.extend(kept);
    out
}
```

**Strict-shrink contract**: the condense replaces `dropped.len()` messages with one digest; rehydration adds `restored.len()` back. The conductor rebinds only when `after.len() < before.len()`, i.e. `1 + restored.len() < dropped.len()`. So `restore_under_count_guard` caps the restored count at `dropped.len() - 2` (`max_files = headroom.min(5)`), guaranteeing the net transcript is strictly shorter. `WindowBudgetCondense::condense` short-circuits to the verbatim input `Turn`s when the pipeline returns an unchanged length, keeping `/compact` idempotent on an already-tight window. The **auto** path is budget-gated (folds only the head beyond the ~6k-token tail); the **manual** `/compact` force path folds everything before the last user turn (cutting at a user-message boundary keeps tool call/result pairs intact). Because the summarizer emits a deterministic local digest with no completer bound, compaction never depends on a provider key.

**Two compaction engines.** `window_budget` is the app's conductor `CondenseFn` seam. The framework ships its own compactor in `runtime` `memory` (`should_compact`/`find_cut_point`/`summarize`/`compact`), but it is a **different engine never wired into the conductor**:

| | `window_budget` (this crate) | `runtime` memory (framework) |
|--|------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| message type | `Message` (rich 7-variant `AgentMessage` analog) | gateway `Turn` |
| `keep_recent` | **tokens** (default `6000`) | **turns** (default `8`) |
| trigger | ratio **0.75** of the window | ratio **0.8** |
| completer | injectable `ModelInvoker` (shared trait) | `ModelInvoker` |
| digest header | `[session digest …]` / `[branch digest …]` | `[condensed earlier context]` |

The `keep_recent` unit warning is baked into the `BudgetPolicy` doc comment: it is **tokens**, not turns. The policies, prompts, and digest headers differ (tests pin this crate's headers); do not substitute one for the other.

**Source layout:**

```text
window_budget/
├── mod.rs               # public barrel + the re-exported Message/Content seam
├── message.rs           # Message enum (AgentMessage analog) + Content
├── contract.rs          # frozen value shapes (no behavior): BudgetPolicy, CondensePlan, …
├── condenser.rs         # create_condenser, condense, Condenser, CondenserDeps, AUTO_CONDENSE_POLICY
├── microcompact.rs      # clear_stale_tool_results (free pre-pass)
├── rehydrate.rs         # rehydrate_recent_reads (read-restore post-pass)
├── budget/              # pure budget arithmetic (no I/O)
│   ├── mod.rs
│   ├── estimate.rs      # token heuristic + forward prefix-sum
│   ├── gate.rs          # is_over_budget / budget_limit
│   └── slice.rs         # plan_slice + last_user_turn_start
└── summarize/           # model-driven summarization
    ├── mod.rs
    ├── prompt.rs        # CONDENSER_BRIEF, flatten_transcript, build_summary_prompt, SECTION_TEMPLATE
    └── condense.rs      # summarize core, SummarizeDeps, condense_scope, local fallback digest
```

The produced `Condenser` and runner pipeline are consumed by the Conductor's `CondenseFn` seam and assembled in Boot; the messages bridge to/from the gateway `Turn`, and the default completer is the framework's `ModelInvoker` over the llm-gateway.


### Subsystems — transcript export, briefing, addons, insight

These four subsystems live in the `induscode` crate (binaries `indusr` / `indusagir`, both `[[bin]]` targets in `src/bin/main.rs` sharing one `main` branded off `argv[0]`'s basename). Each composes the frozen `indusagi` framework workspace rather than modifying it.

#### Transcript export

`induscode::transcript_export` is the self-contained-HTML transcript publisher. `publish_transcript(entries, opts)` renders a session's turns into one standalone `<!doctype html>` string — Markdown through `pulldown-cmark`, fenced code through `syntect`, terminal-styled (ANSI/SGR) tool output painted to safe `<span>`s, with everything baked into a base64 JSON payload at publish time so the page opens with zero external runtime dependencies. It is a pure, synchronous, offline leaf: no I/O lives inside the subsystem (the single file write belongs to the caller). Reached from the crate via `induscode::transcript_export`, or from the live console with the `/export`, `/share`, and `/copy` slash commands.

It owns three concerns end to end: **painting** SGR tool output into HTML spans via a table-driven machine; **computing** export colors from a theme token bag through a precomputed WCAG relative-luminance lookup table; and **assembling** a themed page-shell template whose `{{TOKEN}}` slots are filled at publish time.

**Module layout** (`crates/induscode/src/transcript_export/`):

| Module | Concern |
|--------|---------|
| `mod.rs` | Public barrel — re-export the whole surface from here, never from individual files. |
| `contract.rs` | The **frozen value surface** — `struct`/`enum` types and inert constants only; no string assembly, no theme math. Ports the `src/briefing/contract.ts:431-790` slice the TS lumped into the briefing contract. |
| `sgr.rs` | The **ANSI/SGR painter** — three-stage pipeline (`tokenize_sgr` → `fold_sgr` → `paint_sgr`) converting a terminal byte stream into HTML-escaped text and styled `<span>` runs through a `OnceLock` dispatch table. |
| `theme_bridge.rs` | The **export color service** — parses CSS colors, reads WCAG luminance from a 256-entry `LazyLock` LUT, reports light/dark mode, derives surface variants, picks readable ink, projects tokens to `--x-*` CSS custom properties. |
| `template.rs` | The **standalone page** — `PAGE_SHELL`, `PAGE_STYLES`, the JS `CLIENT_SCRIPT`, and `fill()` (substitutes only known `{{TOKEN}}` slots). |
| `publish.rs` | The **orchestrator** — `publish_transcript` wires the `pulldown-cmark` + `syntect` pipeline, renders each entry, base64-encodes the turns, resolves the theme, fills the shell; also owns the publisher's `MessagePart` / `PublishContent` / `PublishMessage` / `PublishEntry` input model. |

**Cargo dependencies** (workspace-pinned): `pulldown-cmark` (markdown→HTML), `syntect` (fenced-code highlighting), `two-face` (the framework's syntax set), `base64` (payload), `serde_json` (tool-call args + payload JSON), `thiserror` (`PublishError`).

**Public surface** (all re-exported from `mod.rs`):

| Name | Kind | Source | Purpose |
|------|------|--------|---------|
| `publish_transcript` | fn | `publish.rs` | Render `&[PublishEntry]` + `&PublishOptions` to `Result<String, PublishError>` — a complete standalone HTML document. |
| `paint_sgr` | fn | `sgr.rs` | Convert a raw ANSI/terminal byte stream into HTML-escaped text + styled `<span>` runs; drives `tokenize_sgr` + `fold_sgr`. |
| `tokenize_sgr` | fn | `sgr.rs` | Split a terminal stream into an ordered `Vec<SgrToken>` of text runs and SGR command lists; drops non-SGR CSI sequences. |
| `fold_sgr` | fn | `sgr.rs` | Fold one SGR numeric parameter list into a running `SgrState` via the dispatch table; handles parametric `38`/`48` introducers inline. Pure. |
| `DefaultThemeBridge` | struct | `theme_bridge.rs` | The color service: `luminance` / `mode` / `derive_surface` / `readable_ink` / `to_css_vars`. |
| `fallback_export_theme` | fn | `theme_bridge.rs` | Materialize `FALLBACK_EXPORT_THEME` (the `&'static`-string view) into an owned `ExportTheme` — the rebuild's deep-slate dark palette. |
| `parse_color` / `format_color` | fn | `theme_bridge.rs` | Parse a CSS color (`#rgb`/`#rrggbb`/`#rgba`/`#rrggbbaa`, `rgb()`/`rgba()`) into an `Rgb`, or render an `Rgb` back to `#rrggbb`. |
| `LUMINANCE_LUT` | static | `theme_bridge.rs` | The 256-entry `LazyLock<[f64; 256]>` sRGB→linear lookup table for the WCAG luminance formula. |
| `PAGE_SHELL` / `PAGE_STYLES` / `CLIENT_SCRIPT` | const | `template.rs` | Page shell with `{{TOKEN}}` markers, the inlined stylesheet (reads `--x-*`), and the JS client renderer — all `const &str`, carried byte-verbatim from TS. |
| `fill` | fn | `template.rs` | Replace each known `{{TOKEN}}` with its value (walks `SHELL_SLOTS`, not an open scan). |
| `SHELL_SLOTS` | const | `contract.rs` | `[&str; 9]` — page-shell slot names in fill order. |

The contract also exports the type surface: `SgrState` / `SGR_INITIAL_STATE`, `SgrToken`, `SgrMutation`, `ExportTheme` / `FALLBACK_EXPORT_THEME`, `Rgb`, `ThemeMode`, `ShellSlot`, `WidgetRender`, `PublishOptions`, `PublishRole`, `PublishError`. The input model (`MessagePart`, `PublishContent`, `PublishMessage`, `PublishEntry`) is re-exported from `publish.rs`.

`publish_transcript(entries, opts)` is synchronous and infallible in practice — it returns `Result<String, PublishError>` so any assembly failure surfaces as a typed fault rather than a panic. It builds a `DefaultThemeBridge`, indexes the widgets, renders every entry to a `RenderedTurn`, serializes the turns into a base64 payload, projects the theme into the `THEME_VARS` block, and returns `fill(PAGE_SHELL, &slots)`.

```rust
use induscode::transcript_export::{
    publish_transcript, PublishContent, PublishEntry, PublishMessage,
    PublishOptions, PublishRole,
};

let entries = vec![
    PublishEntry {
        role: PublishRole::User,
        message: PublishMessage {
            role: "user".to_string(),
```
