```rust
            content: PublishContent::Text("Fix the **bug** in `app.rs`".to_string()),
            tool_call_id: None,
            tool_name: None,
        },
    },
    PublishEntry {
        role: PublishRole::Assistant,
        message: PublishMessage {
            role: "assistant".to_string(),
            content: PublishContent::Text("Done:\n```rust\nlet x = 1;\n```".to_string()),
            tool_call_id: None,
            tool_name: None,
        },
    },
];

let html = publish_transcript(
    &entries,
    &PublishOptions { title: Some("Session Transcript".to_string()), ..Default::default() },
)?;
std::fs::write("transcript.html", html)?;
```

`PublishOptions` is fully optional (`default()` yields a themed, self-contained file):

| Field | Type | Default | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|---------|
| `theme` | `Option<ExportTheme>` | `None` → `FALLBACK_EXPORT_THEME` | Override the export color palette. |
| `title` | `Option<String>` | `None` → `"Session Transcript"` | Document title baked into the payload and page heading. |
| `out_dir` | `Option<String>` | `None` | Directory hint (the write is the caller's). |
| `widgets` | `Vec<WidgetRender>` | `vec![]` | Pre-rendered custom-tool blocks (`WidgetRender { call_id, html }`), spliced by tool-call id. |

**Input model** — read structurally, never coupling to the framework message union:

```rust
pub enum MessagePart {
    Text(String),
    Image { mime_type: String, data: String },
    Thinking(String),
    ToolCall { id: String, name: String, arguments: serde_json::Value },
}
pub enum PublishContent { Text(String), Parts(Vec<MessagePart>) }
pub struct PublishMessage { pub role: String, pub content: PublishContent, pub tool_call_id: Option<String>, pub tool_name: Option<String> }
pub struct PublishEntry { pub role: PublishRole, pub message: PublishMessage }
```

A `PublishContent::Text` is coerced to a single text part at render time by `parts_of`. The `PublishRole` enum (`User` / `Assistant` / `Tool` / `System` / `Condense` / `Note`) carries attribution; `PublishRole::from_role(&str)` maps a framework role string, folding anything unrecognized to `Note`. Each role has a wire name (`as_str`, baked into the payload `role`) and a human label (`label`): `You` / `Assistant` / `Tool` / `System` / `Summary` / `Note`.

**The table-driven SGR painter.** ANSI styling is treated as data, not control flow. Each handled SGR code maps to an `SgrMutation` (the data form of TS's `Partial<SgrState>`) in a process-wide `OnceLock<HashMap<u16, SgrMutation>>`; extending the machine means adding a table row, never editing a `match`. Three stages:

1. `tokenize_sgr(input: &str) -> Vec<SgrToken>` — splits the raw stream into alternating text runs (`SgrToken::Text`) and SGR parameter lists (`SgrToken::Sgr(Vec<u16>)`), dropping any CSI sequence whose final byte is not `m` and any bare escape. Scans Unicode scalar values, never emits an empty text run, parses each field with a `parseInt`-style numeric-prefix reader (empty/non-numeric reads `0`, overflow saturates at `u16::MAX`).
2. `fold_sgr(state: SgrState, params: &[u16]) -> SgrState` — folds one parameter list left-to-right. A fixed-meaning code resolves through the table; the `30`–`37` / `40`–`47` / `90`–`97` / `100`–`107` color runs come from a built-in 16-color palette; the parametric `38`/`48` extended-color introducers (24-bit `;2;r;g;b` and 256-index `;5;n`) are read inline by `read_extended_color`, not from the table. An empty list is the bare `ESC[m` reset.
3. `paint_sgr(input: &str) -> String` — drives both, wrapping each text run in a `<span>` with `sgr-*` classes and inline color styles, resolving inverse swap and hidden conceal at render time (`styles_for`), and emitting neutral runs bare (no span).

```rust
use induscode::transcript_export::paint_sgr;
let html = paint_sgr("\x1b[1;31mhot\x1b[0mcalm\x1b[38;5;196mx");
// "hot" → <span class="sgr-bold" style="color:#c14a4a">hot</span>
// "calm" → bare run (no span) after the reset
// "x"   → <span style="color:#ff0000">x</span>
```

Palette colors are concrete CSS strings (ANSI red `#c14a4a`; 256-index 196 → `#ff0000`), so spans are self-contained — the page never ships an ANSI palette. A reset (`SGR 0`) returns to `SGR_INITIAL_STATE` via whole-state replace (`SgrMutation::Reset`); a `SgrMutation::Set` patches only its `Some(..)` fields. Output is byte-exact with the TS painter: the 16-color BASE/BRIGHT palette, the `16`–`231` 6×6×6 cube over `{0, 95, 135, 175, 215, 255}`, the `232`–`255` gray ramp, the off-switches (`22`/`24`/`27`/`28`/`29`/etc.), and per-character HTML escaping of the five significant characters. The 256-color `color256` and SGR `clamp_byte` **truncate** (`| 0`), deliberately distinct from the theme bridge's **rounding** `clamp_byte_round` (both byte-observable, kept separate, plan G-3).

**The theme bridge.** `DefaultThemeBridge` holds a resolved `ExportTheme` (a ten-token color bag — `page_surface` / `card_surface` / `note_surface` / `ink` / `ink_muted` / `accent` / `border` / `user_role` / `agent_role` / `tool_role`) answering every color query against the shared `LUMINANCE_LUT`:

| Method | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `luminance(color: &str) -> f64` | WCAG relative luminance (0–1); unparseable input reads `0.0`. |
| `mode() -> ThemeMode` | `Light` if page-surface luminance ≥ `MODE_THRESHOLD` (`0.18`), else `Dark`. |
| `derive_surface(base: &str, amount: i32) -> String` | Step every channel by a signed amount (positive lightens); unparseable base falls through to the card surface. |
| `readable_ink(background: &str) -> String` | Pick whichever of `ink` / `ink_muted` has higher WCAG contrast vs. a background. |
| `to_css_vars() -> Vec<(&'static str, String)>` | Project the theme to its ten CSS custom properties in fixed `THEME_TOKENS` order, returned as an **ordered** `Vec` (not a map) so the `--x-*` block is byte-stable. |

The luminance read is fast: the per-channel sRGB→linear gamma step is precomputed once by `LUMINANCE_LUT` (`LazyLock<[f64; 256]>`), so a read is three table lookups plus the weighted sum `0.2126·R + 0.7152·G + 0.0722·B`, never a `powf` per channel. Black pins to `0.0`, white to `1.0`. `create_theme_bridge(Option<ExportTheme>)` is the convenience factory — `None` yields a bridge over the deep-slate fallback. The console caller passes only `{ title }` and never a theme, so `FALLBACK_EXPORT_THEME` is the parity default.

**Code highlighting and markdown.** Prose runs through `pulldown-cmark` with GFM tables enabled and hard line breaks off (`{gfm: true, breaks: false}`, replacing TS `marked`). `render_markdown` intercepts code-block events and routes fenced code through `highlight_code` (mirroring marked's overridden `code()` renderer), emitting `<pre><code class="language-…">` with `xhl-*` spans; prose events are buffered (`into_static`) and flushed via `pulldown_cmark::html::push_html`. Fenced code is highlighted by `syntect` over the framework's own syntax set (`two_face::syntax::extra_newlines`, loaded once into a `LazyLock<SyntaxSet>`). `resolve_syntax` maps a language tag through an `EXTENSION_LANGUAGES` alias table (`ts`/`tsx` → TypeScript, `py` → Python, `rs` → Rust, `sh`/`bash`/`zsh` → bash, etc.) before falling back to syntect's lookup. `highlight_with_syntax` walks `ParseState` / `ScopeStack` line-by-line (cribbing the framework's apply-then-read idiom and `split_inclusive('\n')` handling), and `scope_to_xhl` buckets each TextMate scope onto one of five page classes:

| `xhl-*` class | Scopes |
|---------------|--------|
| `xhl-comment` | `comment*` |
| `xhl-number` | `constant.numeric*` |
| `xhl-string` | `string*`, `constant.character*`, `constant.other.symbol*` |
| `xhl-keyword` | `keyword*`, `storage.modifier*`, `constant.language*`, `variable.language*` |
| `xhl-literal` | `entity.name.type/class/namespace/tag*`, `entity.other.attribute-name*`, `support.type/class*`, `storage.type*` |

Specific `constant.numeric` is tested before generic buckets; the `type`-family folds to `xhl-literal` (no `xhl-type` rule, plan G-7). An unrecognized language is **not** auto-detected (plan G-2 — no cheap syntect auto-detect); it falls back to plain escaped code, as does any internal parse failure. The MIT license notices for `pulldown-cmark` and `syntect` are embedded verbatim into `MARKED_LIB` / `HIGHLIGHT_LIB`, swapping the stale `marked` (MIT) and `highlight.js` (BSD-3) notices the TS carried (plan G-4).

**The page shell and slots.** `PAGE_SHELL` carries closed `{{TOKEN}}` placeholders; `SHELL_SLOTS` is the `[&str; 9]` list; `fill()` does literal `str::replace` only over known names, so any stray `{{...}}` in user/tool content survives untouched. Because `str::replace` is value-literal, a `$` in a value is inserted verbatim (the regression the TS escaped-regex guarded against, now free):

| `ShellSlot` | `{{TOKEN}}` | Filled with |
|-------------|-------------|-------------|
| `ThemeVars` | `THEME_VARS` | The `--x-*` CSS custom-property block (`pageSurface`/`page_surface` → `--x-page-surface`). |
| `PageSurface` / `CardSurface` / `NoteSurface` | `PAGE_SURFACE` / `CARD_SURFACE` / `NOTE_SURFACE` | Resolved surface colors. |
| `Styles` | `STYLES` | `PAGE_STYLES` — the inlined stylesheet (`.turn` / `.tool-frame` / `.aside-note` / `sgr-*` / `xhl-*`). |
| `Script` | `SCRIPT` | `CLIENT_SCRIPT` — the JS that decodes the payload and injects each turn into `#xscript-root`. |
| `Payload` | `PAYLOAD` | The base64-encoded JSON of rendered turns. |
| `MarkedLib` / `HighlightLib` | `MARKED_LIB` / `HIGHLIGHT_LIB` | The `pulldown-cmark` and `syntect` license notices, verbatim. |

The `THEME_VARS` block is built by `theme_vars_block`, hyphenating each token name (`hyphenate` handles camelCase boundaries and `_` separators). Turns are rendered to HTML at publish time, JSON-serialized by `payload_json`, base64-encoded by `to_base64` (standard base64 of the UTF-8 JSON, round-tripping through the page's `JSON.parse(decodeURIComponent(escape(atob(...))))` chain, plan G-6), and spliced into `PAYLOAD`. The embedded `CLIENT_SCRIPT` only decodes and injects the already-built `turn.html` — its `window.marked` / `window.hljs` re-hydration paths are inert fallbacks that never fire (plan G-5). This makes the file parser-free and dependency-free.

**Content-part dispatch** (`render_entry`, on `MessagePart` discriminant):

- **`Text`** — Markdown for user/assistant turns (`render_markdown`); for `Tool` turns, `render_tool_text` paints ANSI-bearing text (detected by `has_ansi`, the `ESC[` introducer) with `paint_sgr` inside `<pre class="tool-frame">`, or escapes plain text into the same frame.
- **`Image`** — an inline `data:{mime};base64,{data}` URI `<img>` (`render_image`).
- **`Thinking`** — a muted `<div class="aside-note">`, not prose.
- **`ToolCall`** — `render_tool_call` emits a labeled `<div class="tool-frame">` with the tool name and pretty-printed (HTML-escaped) JSON arguments.

A `Tool` result entry is first checked against the widget index keyed by `tool_call_id`; a matching pre-rendered `WidgetRender` block is spliced in whole. `System` and `Condense` roles become standalone notes (`kind: "note"`); every other role becomes a styled turn card. The `RenderedTurn` carries `{ kind, role, label, html }`, serialized as `{ title, turns: [...] }`.

**The `/export` slash command.** `induscode::console::slash` registers `/copy`, `/export [path]`, and `/share`, each minting a `ConductorAction` the live loop in `console/mount.rs` services. `/export` raises `ConductorAction::ExportTranscript { path }`; the mount handler projects the live transcript onto `PublishEntry` via `to_publish_entries` and calls `export_transcript_html`.

```bash
# indusr REPL
/export                    # writes transcript-<stamp>.html into the cwd
/export docs/session.html  # writes to an explicit (relative-to-cwd) path
/share                     # export, then publish a secret GitHub gist via `gh`
/copy                      # copy the last assistant reply to the OS clipboard
```

`to_publish_entries` (porting `toPublishEntries`) flattens each `Turn`'s `Block`s to prose — `Block::Text` / `Block::Thinking` directly, `Block::ToolResult` through `stringify_tool_output`, `Block::ToolCall` as `name(input)` — and surfaces a tool turn's first `ToolResult` call id for attribution. `export_transcript_html` resolves the target (a bare/empty path → `transcript-<epoch_stamp>.html` in cwd; relative → joined to cwd; absolute → used as-is), calls `publish_transcript(..., PublishOptions { title: Some("Session Transcript"), ..default })`, and writes. An empty transcript is a typed failure — **no** file is written and the console never toasts "Exported". `/share` exports first, then runs `gh gist create … --public=false`, falling back to the local HTML path when `gh` is missing or unauthenticated.

**Faults.** The only failure surfaced is `PublishError::Publish { message, cause }` (a `thiserror::Error`), mirroring the `"publish"` `BriefingFaultKind` the TS raised. Minted by `PublishError::publish(message)` or `PublishError::publish_with(message, cause)` (the latter carries a `Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>` as `#[source]`). `render_entry`, the SGR painter, the theme bridge, and `fill` are all infallible by construction.

**Relationship to the framework.** Reuses the framework only through its dependency graph — the `syntect` loader and the `scope_to_role` bucketing pattern from `indusagi::tui_render`'s markdown highlighter — and otherwise emits every byte itself. It consumes the framework's `Block` / `Turn` types only at the console boundary (`console/mount.rs`'s `to_publish_entries`), never inside the subsystem. It is the Rust analogue of the TS `transcript-export` and Python `transcript_export` subsystems, ported byte-exact where it matters (SGR palette, 256-color cube, page shell, base64 chain) and deliberately diverged elsewhere (pulldown-cmark + syntect for marked + highlight.js, no fenced-language auto-detect, swapped license notices).

#### Briefing

`induscode::briefing` is the budget-aware system-prompt assembler: four pure, synchronous engines that fold a read-only `BriefingInput` into the single system-prompt `String` fed to the model as `AgentConfig.system`. The prompt is **not** a `{{TOKEN}}` template — it is a declarative recipe of `SectionFn` pointers (`BRIEFING_SECTIONS`), each gating *and* rendering itself in one call (inspecting `BriefingInput`, returning `None` when it does not apply, `Some(fragment)` otherwise). Reshaping the prompt is a data edit to `BRIEFING_SECTIONS`, never a change to the composer. Alongside live the `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` context-doc loader with `@import` expansion, the single-pass `$arg` / `{{arg.…}}` macro engine, and the Agent-Skills `SKILL.md` card loader. It stands on `indusagi::core::time`'s clock and consumes the deck's tool schemas as input data — never the deck crate itself.

**Module layout** (`crates/induscode/src/briefing/`, no I/O in the type seam):

```
├── mod.rs           # public barrel re-exporting the contract vocabulary
├── contract.rs      # FROZEN type seam: ToolDoc, BriefingInput, SectionFn, Macro*, Skill*, BriefingFault, limits
├── compose.rs       # compose_briefing(+_with_options), BRIEFING_SECTIONS, section renderers, TOOL_SUMMARIES, footer clock
├── context_docs.rs  # gather_context_docs: ancestor-chain CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md walk + @import expansion
├── macros.rs        # single-pass {{arg.…}}/$arg scanner + resolver + loader + split_frontmatter
└── skills.rs        # SKILL.md / *.md walk, validate, project, gather into SkillCards
```

The briefing depends only on `induscode::core`, `indusagi::smithy`, and `indusagi::core` — it receives tool schemas as **input data** (`ToolDoc`), so there is no edge to the capability deck. The composer touches no disk; the three loaders use blocking `std::fs` and run once at boot. Third-party deps: `serde_json`, `regex` (the `@import` grammar), `thiserror` (`BriefingFault`).

**Naming note.** The milestone roadmap names the primary types `BriefingInput`, `ToolDoc`, `MacroDef`, `ComposeOptions`; the TS source called these `BriefingContext`, an `AgentTool` projection, `Macro`, and the override half of `BriefingInputs`. TS names are retained as documented `type` aliases — `BriefingContext` (for `BriefingInput`) and `Macro` (for `MacroDef`). Only `Macro` is re-exported from `mod.rs`; `BriefingContext` lives on `contract.rs`, reached as `induscode::briefing::contract::BriefingContext`.

**Public surface** (selected; full list in source):

| Name | Kind | Source | Purpose |
|------|------|--------|---------|
| `compose_briefing` | fn | `compose.rs` | Fold the default recipe + a `BriefingInput` into the system-prompt string. |
| `compose_briefing_with_options` | fn | `compose.rs` | As above, honouring `--system` / `--append-system` / `prelude` overrides on `ComposeOptions`. |
| `compose_with` | fn | `compose.rs` | The bare reducer: fold a `&[SectionFn]` + context + optional prelude/append. |
| `BRIEFING_SECTIONS` | `const &[SectionFn]` | `compose.rs` | The default 10-entry recipe, in render order. |
| `BRIEFING_SECTION_IDS` | `const &[&str]` | `compose.rs` | Stable section ids, parallel to `BRIEFING_SECTIONS`. |
| `SectionFn` | type alias | `contract.rs` | `fn(&BriefingInput) -> Option<String>` — one section that gates AND renders. |
| `BriefingSection` | type alias | `contract.rs` | Alias of `SectionFn`. |
| `BriefingInput` | struct | `contract.rs` | The all-defaulted read-only data bag every section reads. |
| `ComposeOptions` | struct | `contract.rs` | The `--system` / `prelude` / `--append-system` override hooks. |
| `ToolDoc` | struct | `contract.rs` | A tool the model may invoke (`name` + `description` + `parameters`). |
| `ContextDoc` | struct | `contract.rs` | A project-context document (`path` heading + verbatim `body`). |
| `SubagentBrief` | struct | `contract.rs` | A named delegate role (`name`, `purpose`, optional `when`). |
| `Macro` / `MacroDef` | struct | `contract.rs` | A loaded slash macro: `name`, `description`, `body`, `origin`, `source`. |
| `MacroScope` | struct | `contract.rs` | The argument environment: `args` vector, joined `all`, verbatim `raw`. |
| `MacroToken` | enum | `contract.rs` | `Literal` / `Positional(u32)` / `All` / `Slice { start, length }`. |
| `MacroOrigin` | enum | `contract.rs` | `User` / `Project` / `Path` / `Builtin`, with `.label()`. |
| `SkillCard` | struct | `contract.rs` | A validated `SKILL.md` card — documentation, not a callable. |
| `SkillFrontmatter` | struct | `contract.rs` | Parsed header (name, description, license, compatibility, metadata, allowed_tools, disable_model_invocation). |
| `SkillLoad` / `SkillDiagnostic` / `SkillOutcomeKind` | struct/struct/enum | `contract.rs` | Aggregate load (`cards` + `diagnostics`); per-candidate outcome (`kind`/`location`/`detail`); `Loaded`/`Skipped`/`Invalid`/`Collision`. |
| `SkillRoot` | struct | `contract.rs` | One skill directory root + its `MacroOrigin`. |
| `SKILL_NAME_LIMIT` / `SKILL_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` | `const usize` | `contract.rs` | Agent-Skills limits: `64` and `1024`. |
| `BriefingFault` | enum | `contract.rs` | Closed `thiserror::Error`: `MacroInvalid` / `SkillInvalid`. |
| `scan_macro_body` / `resolve_tokens` / `build_macro_scope` / `apply_macros` / `apply_macros_reporting` / `expand_invocation` / `load_macros` / `read_macro_file` / `split_frontmatter` | fn | `macros.rs` | The macro engine. |
| `gather_context_docs` / `GatherContextDocsOptions` | fn/struct | `context_docs.rs` | The ancestor-chain context-doc walk + per-walk tuning. |
| `gather_skill_cards` / `load_skill_cards` / `model_invocable_cards` | fn | `skills.rs` | Load/merge/filter skill cards. |

**The declarative section pipeline.** A section is a plain function pointer (`pub type SectionFn = fn(&BriefingInput) -> Option<String>`), not a trait object — collapsing the TS `applies` predicate + `render` method into one fn. `None` means it does not apply or rendered empty (an empty/whitespace fragment is also dropped); `Some(frag)` is its fragment. `compose_with(sections, ctx, prelude, append)` is the reducer: it walks the recipe in order, trims each fragment, drops empties, joins survivors with blank-line gaps (`join_blocks`, `\n\n`), prepends a trimmed `prelude`, appends a trimmed `append`. `compose_briefing(ctx)` calls `compose_with(BRIEFING_SECTIONS, ctx, None, None)`.

**The default recipe** (`BRIEFING_SECTIONS`, 10 entries in render order; parallel `BRIEFING_SECTION_IDS`):

| Section | id | Gate | Renders |
|---------|----|------|---------|
| `section_role` | `role` | always | `You are a terminal-based software engineering assistant…` |
| `section_tools` | `tools` | `!ctx.tools.is_empty()` | `# Tools` + each tool as `` `name` — summary `` from `TOOL_SUMMARIES` (fallback: tool's `description`). |
| `section_guidelines` | `guidelines` | always (each bullet gated) | `# Working guidance`; each tool-specific bullet gated on `read`/`edit`/`write`/`grep`/`find`/`ls`/`bash`; two always-on bullets close it. |
| `section_task` | `tasks` | `todo_set` or `todo_read` present | `# Task tracking`. |
| `section_subagents` | `subagents` | `!ctx.subagents.is_empty()` | `# Delegates` — each `SubagentBrief` as `**name** — purpose. Use it when …`. |
| `section_plan` | `plan-mode` | `enter_plan_mode` or `exit_plan_mode` present | `# Plan mode` — read-only research-then-propose loop. |
| `section_connectors` | `connectors` | any tool name starts `connector_`/`saas_` | `# Connectors`. |
| `section_project_context` | `project-context` | `!ctx.context_docs.is_empty()` | `# Project context` — inlines each `ContextDoc` under `## {path}` (body trimmed). |
| `section_skills` | `skills` | `!ctx.skills.is_empty()` | `# Skills` — XML-escapes each card into an `<available_skills>` block of 2-space-indented `<skill>` entries. |
| `section_footer` | `footer` | always | Stamps `Working directory: {cwd ?? workspace}` (omitted when neither set) and `Current time: {iso}`. |

Every heading and guideline sentence is reproduced byte-for-byte from the TS source (golden-identical prompt; the milestone Verify diffs the whole prompt). The Rust recipe carries a `plan-mode` section the Python edition does not (gates on the deck's `enter_plan_mode`/`exit_plan_mode`). With an empty `BriefingInput::default()`, only `role`, `guidelines` (its no-tool branch — the two always-on bullets), and `footer` survive.

**`BriefingInput`** is the all-defaulted, immutable bag:

```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct BriefingInput {
    pub workspace: Option<String>,      // absolute working directory (footer fallback)
    pub tools: Vec<ToolDoc>,            // capabilities advertised this turn (deck input data)
    pub cwd: Option<String>,            // display path; preferred over workspace in the footer
    pub skills: Vec<SkillCard>,         // model-invocable cards for the skills block
    pub subagents: Vec<SubagentBrief>,  // delegate roles for # Delegates
    pub context_docs: Vec<ContextDoc>,  // CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md docs for # Project context
    pub now_ms: Option<u64>,            // injectable footer clock (epoch ms); None ⇒ wall clock
}
```

`now_ms == None` reads `indusagi::core::time::now_ms()` at render time.

**Tool docs and summaries.** `ToolDoc { name, description, parameters: serde_json::Value }` — only `name` + `description` carry prompt meaning; `parameters` (Null when no args) is retained verbatim but unused by default sections. `section_tools` renders each via `describe_tool`, mirroring the TS `summary ?? description?.trim() ?? ""` chain: a `TOOL_SUMMARIES` hit wins; else the tool's trimmed `description`; else just the back-ticked name. `TOOL_SUMMARIES` (the briefing's own re-authored one-liners):

| Tool name | Summary |
|-----------|---------|
| `read` | Open a file's contents for inspection. |
| `write` | Create a new file or overwrite an existing one wholesale. |
| `edit` | Apply a precise in-place change by matching exact existing text. |
| `bash` | Run a shell command in the workspace. |
| `grep` | Search file contents by pattern across the tree. |
| `find` | Locate files and directories by name or glob. |
| `ls` | List the entries of a directory. |
| `task` | Hand a self-contained sub-task to a delegate agent. |
| `todo_read` | Read back the current task checklist. |
| `todo_set` | Record or revise the task checklist. |
| `webfetch` | Retrieve and read the contents of a URL. |
| `websearch` | Query the web for current information. |

**Parity-critical wire names:** the checklist keys are the framework's real Rust wire names `todo_read` / `todo_set` — NOT the TS `todoread` / `todowrite`. Keying off TS names would silently drop the summaries and the `# Task tracking` section would never render. The guidance gates (`read`/`edit`/`write`/`grep`/`find`/`ls`/`bash`) and connector prefixes (`connector_` / `saas_`) match the deck's real capability names.

**The footer clock.** `section_footer` stamps `Working directory:` (preferring `ctx.cwd`, falling back to `ctx.workspace`, omitted when neither set) and `Current time:`. The timestamp matches JS `new Date(ms).toISOString()` byte-for-byte — always UTC, millisecond precision, trailing `Z` (e.g. `2026-06-04T12:00:00.000Z`). Conversion is hand-rolled (Howard Hinnant's public-domain `civil_from_days`) so the crate needs no `chrono`/`time` dependency:

```rust
fn format_iso8601_millis(epoch_ms: u64) -> String {
    let total_secs = (epoch_ms / 1000) as i64;
    let millis = (epoch_ms % 1000) as u32;
    let days = total_secs.div_euclid(86_400);
    let secs_of_day = total_secs.rem_euclid(86_400);
    let (year, month, day) = civil_from_days(days);
    format!("{year:04}-{month:02}-{day:02}T{hour:02}:{minute:02}:{second:02}.{millis:03}Z")
}
```

`format_iso8601_millis(0)` is `1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z`; `1_709_251_199_123` is `2024-02-29T23:59:59.123Z`.

**Compose overrides** (`ComposeOptions`):

```rust
pub struct ComposeOptions {
    pub system: Option<String>,         // --system: REPLACES the whole composed prompt; recipe skipped
    pub prelude: Option<String>,        // prepended ahead of the rendered sections
    pub append_system: Option<String>,  // --append-system: appended after the sections / the override
}
```

| Field | Effect |
|-------|--------|
| `system` | Replaces the built-in briefing entirely; the recipe is skipped (only `prelude`/`append_system` still bracket it). |
| `append_system` | Appends a trailing block after the base. |
| `prelude` | Prepends a leading block. |
| none | The tool-aware built-in renders from `BRIEFING_SECTIONS`. |

```rust
let opts = ComposeOptions { system: Some("BODY".into()), prelude: Some("PRE".into()), append_system: Some("POST".into()) };
assert_eq!(compose_briefing_with_options(&ctx, &opts), "PRE\n\nBODY\n\nPOST");
```

**Context docs.** `gather_context_docs(cwd, home, opts)` walks the cwd's ancestor chain from filesystem root **down** to the cwd (so the cwd's own files land last, and since the renderer treats vector order as priority, the closest file wins); the home directory is scanned after the chain as a global fallback. Within each directory, candidate filenames are read in this load-bearing order:

```rust
const CANDIDATE_FILES: &[&str] = &[
    "AGENTS.md", "CLAUDE.md", "INDUSAGI.md", "CLAUDE.local.md",
    "AGENTS.local.md", ".indusagi/CLAUDE.md", ".claude/CLAUDE.md",
];
```

Each file may pull additional files inline via `@import`, resolved by `extract_imports` against `IMPORT_REGEX` `(?:^|\s)@((?:[^\s\\]|\\ )+)`: targets are unescaped (`\ ` → ` `) with trailing `#fragment` stripped; `~/…` resolves against `home`, absolute used as-is, relative resolved lexically against the importing file's directory (Node-style, no filesystem access); non-text extensions are dropped (`is_text_file` vs `TEXT_FILE_EXTENSIONS`, a bare no-extension name like `LICENSE` allowed); `load_doc_tree` emits parent first then each child recursively, a `seen` set keyed by realpath making cyclic/repeated imports a no-op. Two clamps (both `None`-substitutes-default):

| Option | Default const | Purpose |
|--------|---------------|---------|
| `max_import_depth` | `DEFAULT_MAX_IMPORT_DEPTH` = `5` | `@import` recursion ceiling. |
| `max_bytes_per_doc` | `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES_PER_DOC` = `40_000` | Per-document body clamp (post-trim). |

The byte clamp uses `floor_char_boundary` so a cut never splits a UTF-8 codepoint. The walk **never errors** — any read/permission failure folds into a skip and the function returns whatever it gathered. Heading labels are shortened by `shorten_path` (`./…` under-cwd, `~/…` under-home, else verbatim).

**Slash macros.** A macro is a named prompt body from a `*.md` file. Invoking `/<name> rest-of-line` resolves the body against the line's arguments in **one left-to-right scan**: `scan_macro_body` walks the body's bytes once into a flat `Vec<MacroToken>`, `resolve_tokens` substitutes against a `MacroScope`. Expanded argument text is inserted verbatim and **never re-scanned** (avoiding the multi-pass re-interpretation footgun). The scanner walks a `&[u8]` cursor (the TS indexed UTF-16 but only matched ASCII delimiters).

Primary placeholder syntax — indus double-curly `{{arg.…}}` (whitespace optional inside braces):

| Placeholder | Token | Resolves to |
|-------------|-------|-------------|
| `{{arg.1}}`, `{{arg.2}}`, … | `Positional(N)` | one positional (1-based; out of range ⇒ empty) |
| `{{arg.all}}` | `All` | every positional, re-joined with single spaces |
| `{{arg.slice N L}}` | `Slice { start: N, length: Some(L) }` | at most `L` positionals from 1-based offset `N` |
| `{{arg.slice N}}` | `Slice { start: N, length: None }` | positionals from `N` onward |
| `{{arg.rest N}}` | `Slice { start: N, length: None }` | alias of `slice N`; `N` defaults to `2`, so `{{arg.rest}}` = "everything after `arg.1`" |
| `{{{{` | `Literal("{{")` | a literal `{{` (escape) |

A compatibility shim recognises legacy `$arg` forms and fires the threaded `report` callback once per recognised form (for a deprecation notice):

| Legacy form | Token | Notes |
|-------------|-------|-------|
| `$1`, `$2`, … | `Positional(N)` | 1-based positional |
| `$@` | `All` | every positional, joined |
| `$ARGUMENTS` | `All` | exact bareword (`$ARGUMENTSX` does not partial-match) |
| `${@:N}` | `Slice { start: N, length: None }` | from `N` onward |
| `${@:N:L}` | `Slice { start: N, length: Some(L) }` | bounded sub-range |
| `${@}` | `All` | brace spelling of `$@` |
| `$$` | `Literal("$")` | escape — a literal `$` |

Unlike the TS module-global `legacyReporter` singleton, the reporter is threaded as an explicit `&mut dyn FnMut(&str, &str)` (callers pass `&mut |_, _| {}`). Any unparseable placeholder (`${foo}`, dangling `$`, stray `{{` not opening `{{arg.`, `{{foo}}`) is treated as literal text. `build_macro_scope` does a quote-aware split of the raw line (single/double quotes group; quotes stripped; empty runs dropped) → `MacroScope { args, all, raw }`.

`load_macros(dir, origin, label)` reads the **direct `*.md` children** of a dir (non-recursive — slash macros are flat files), sorts, skips dotfiles/non-`.md`, parses each via `read_macro_file`, dedupes by name (first wins). Missing dir → empty `Vec`; unreadable file → `Err(BriefingFault::MacroInvalid)`. `read_macro_file` derives the name from the basename (minus `.md`, case-insensitive) and the description from frontmatter `description` (suffixed with the origin's `label`), or from the first non-blank body line capped at `DERIVED_DESCRIPTION_BUDGET` (72) **chars** (not bytes) with a trailing `…`.

```rust
let macros = load_macros(Path::new("/repo/.indusagi/commands"), MacroOrigin::Project, None)?;
assert_eq!(expand_invocation("/deploy staging fast", &macros), "ship staging in mode fast");
assert_eq!(apply_macros("all: {{arg.all}} | rest: {{arg.rest}}", "a b c"), "all: a b c | rest: b c");
```

`expand_invocation` only rewrites lines opening with `/` that name a known macro (first match wins); ordinary turns pass through. These become dynamic `/template` slash commands. `split_frontmatter` is the shared minimal `---`-fenced YAML-ish reader: recognises a block only when the first line is exactly `---` and a later line is exactly `---`, turns each `key: value` into a flat entry (ordered `Vec<(String, String)>`, last value of a duplicate key kept), strips matching surrounding quotes via `unquote_scalar`, skips blank/`#`-comment lines.

**Skill cards.** A `SkillCard` is documentation the model reads, not a callable: a markdown file in Agent-Skills format whose frontmatter names a skill and one-line-describes when it applies, with a body of on-demand instructions.

```rust
pub struct SkillCard {
    pub name: String, pub description: String, pub body: String,
    pub location: PathBuf, pub origin: MacroOrigin, pub frontmatter: SkillFrontmatter,
}
```

`load_skill_cards(dir, origin)` walks one root; `gather_skill_cards(roots)` merges several `SkillRoot`s. The walk (`walk_candidates` → `walk_level`) sorts entries, skips dotfiles, prunes `PRUNED_DIRS` (`node_modules`, `.git`), breaks symlink cycles by canonical realpath. Two shapes: at a **root** level a loose `*.md` child is a single-file skill (name inferred from the enclosing directory, skips the directory-match check when no `name` declared); in any **subdirectory** a `SKILL.md` (compared case-sensitively against `SKILL_MANIFEST`) is a packaged skill whose declared name **must match** its enclosing directory. `fs::metadata` (not `symlink_metadata`) is used so a symlinked candidate is followed. Validation:

| Rule | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Name pattern | `check_name` hand-matches `^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$` — lowercase-alphanumeric words joined by single hyphens |
| Name length | ≤ `SKILL_NAME_LIMIT` (64) chars |
| Name vs. directory | a declared name on a packaged skill (or a loose root `*.md` declaring one) must equal the enclosing directory |
| Description | required, ≤ `SKILL_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` (1024) chars |
| Frontmatter keys | every key must be in `KNOWN_FRONTMATTER_KEYS`; a stray key marks the file `Invalid` |
| Kebab → snake | `project_frontmatter` maps `allowed-tools` → `allowed_tools` (split on whitespace/commas) and `disable-model-invocation` → `disable_model_invocation` (only `"true"` sets it) |

The walk **never panics** (an unreadable file → `Invalid` via `parse_candidate`). Each candidate yields a `SkillDiagnostic` with one of four `SkillOutcomeKind`s. `gather_skill_cards` dedupes by name first-root-wins and emits explicit `Collision` diagnostics for later claimants; `load_skill_cards` does **not** dedupe across roots. To keep exactly one `Loaded` diagnostic per surviving card, the merge loop forwards only `kind != Loaded` diagnostics and re-emits the `Loaded`/`Collision` line itself (Gotcha G-5). `model_invocable_cards` drops cards flagged `disable-model-invocation` — those remain available as explicit `/skill:<name>` commands but never appear in the briefing block. The rendered skills block XML-escapes each card's `name`, `description`, and `location` into 2-space-indented `<skill>` entries inside `<available_skills>…</available_skills>`.

**Faults.** `BriefingFault` is the closed `thiserror::Error`: `MacroInvalid(String)` (a macro file could not be read/parsed) and `SkillInvalid(String)` (a `SKILL.md` failed format validation). These are agent-domain errors, deliberately NOT folded into `indusagi::core::errors::CoreError`. The TS `BriefingFaultKind` also carried `publish`/`theme` kinds; those now live in the transcript-export crate's own fault vocabulary.

**The live call site.** The only runtime composer is `compose_session_briefing` in `induscode::boot::runners`, driven by every run mode (interactive, `-p` print, `--json` link):

```rust
fn compose_session_briefing(inv: &Invocation, cwd: &str,
    descriptors: &[indusagi::llmgateway::contract::ToolDescriptor]) -> String {
    let tools: Vec<ToolDoc> = descriptors.iter().map(|d| ToolDoc {
        name: d.name.clone(), description: d.description.clone(), parameters: d.parameters.clone(),
    }).collect();
    let input = BriefingInput { workspace: Some(cwd.to_string()), cwd: Some(cwd.to_string()), tools, ..Default::default() };
    let opts = ComposeOptions { system: inv.system.clone(), append_system: inv.append_system.clone(), ..Default::default() };
    compose_briefing_with_options(&input, &opts)
}
```

The deck's `ToolDescriptor`s become `ToolDoc`s by copying `name`/`description`/`parameters`. The `context_docs`, `skills`, and `subagents` fields are fully implemented and unit-tested but populated by separate console/boot wiring (`gather_context_docs`, `gather_skill_cards`/`model_invocable_cards`, delegate briefs feed through their own discovery sites). The result is the agent's `AgentConfig.system`.

**Framework anchors.** `indusagi::core::time::now_ms()` (footer timestamp when `now_ms` is `None`) and `indusagi::llmgateway::contract::ToolDescriptor` (the deck/gateway tool schema projected into `ToolDoc`). The TS lineage additionally hosted the SGR machine and HTML transcript palette in the briefing contract; this rebuild relocated those to the transcript-export crate, leaving briefing carrying only sections, context docs, macros, skills, `ContextDoc`, and `BriefingFault`.

#### Addons

The addons layer is `induscode`'s loadable-extension contract — it discovers, loads, registers, and folds locally-authored extensions under a workspace's `.indus/addons` directory into one conflict-resolved runtime of lifecycle hooks, tool-boundary interceptors, contributed slash commands, and contributed tools, with every fault isolated so one broken addon never aborts the others. Reached as `induscode::addons`; the Rust port of `indus-code-rebuild/src/addons` (PLAN/75). An addon **records, never mutates**: its single `register` entry point describes intent onto a per-addon `AddonApi` surface; the `AddonHost` reads each `RegisteredManifest` back out and folds the four contribution streams (subscriptions, interceptors, commands, tools) into one shared registry, then builds the `EventDispatcher` and `InterceptorChain` over it. Every failure path is captured as a typed `AddonFault` routed to listeners rather than raised.

**Module layout** (`src/addons/`, all against the frozen `contract.rs` seam):

| Module | Role |
|--------|------|
| `contract` | The frozen type surface: `Addon`, `AddonManifest`, the `AddonApi` limited-surface trait, the `HookEvent` taxonomy, the interceptor enter/exit types, `SubagentProfile`, `AddonFault`, the `ModuleLoader` trait. Declares only shapes plus inert minters (`AddonId::new`, `AddonFault::new`, `RegisteredManifest::empty`). Composes (never re-declares) `indusagi::capabilities::{Tool, ToolResult}`. |
| `host` | The assembly point — discovery (`discover_addons`/`discover_sources`), the per-addon `RecordingSurface`, the fold into an `AddonBundle` carrying the dispatcher + chain. |
| `manifest` | The Tier-0 declarative `manifest.toml` schema (`AddonDescriptor`) and the v1 default `DeclarativeLoader`. |
| `dispatch` | The two runtimes: `EventDispatcher` (observe/transform/gate fan-out) and `InterceptorChain` (tool-boundary enter/exit), plus the `subscription`/`interceptor` minters. |
| `sandbox` | The capability policy (`SandboxPolicy`, FS denied by default) plus path-hygiene helpers (`scrub_invisible`/`expand_path`/`resolve_path`). |
| `subagents` | Subagent profiles + crew/ticket-board coordination over `indusagi::swarm` (feature `swarm`). |

`mod.rs` re-exports the contract types and runtime entry points; `#[cfg(feature = "swarm")] pub use subagents::SubagentCrew;`.

**The tiered loading story.** The one thing that does not survive the TS port verbatim is `ModuleLoader.load` = "compile arbitrary TypeScript". Rust runs no JS (no jiti, no virtual-module bridge, no `alias` injection). The `ModuleLoader` trait stays; its default is tiered (PLAN/75 §4):

- **Tier 0** — the declarative TOML loader (`DeclarativeLoader`, the v1 default). Data, not code: a `manifest.toml` parses into contributions; nothing third-party executes in-process, so there is no escape surface. The only tier shipped today.
- **Tier 1** — a subprocess JSON-RPC host (behind a feature; a typed stub at present). The fault seams in `EventDispatcher`/`InterceptorChain` (`report`/`handler_fault`) are retained precisely for this tier, whose handler RPC *can* fail.
- **Tier 2** — WASM components: explicitly **deferred**.

This is a strict upgrade over the TS lineage (which ran addon code in the host process with full ambient authority). Because Tier 0 executes no third-party closure, a `register` "throw" (the TS `Register` fault) cannot occur for it — the `Register` fault kind is reserved for in-proc tiers.

**Authoring a Tier-0 addon.** A directory holding a `manifest.toml`, dropped under `<workspace>/.indus/addons/`. The manifest declares an `id`, optional `version`, declarative slash-command aliases, and declarative event gate policies — **no executable body**: a command's effect is a shell `exec` string run through `FrameworkHandles::exec` (the same gate the native `bash` tool goes through), and a gate is a rule, not a closure.

```toml
# <workspace>/.indus/addons/safety/manifest.toml
id = "safety"
version = "1.0.0"

[[command]]
name = "deploy"
summary = "run the project deploy script"
exec = "./scripts/deploy.sh"

[[gate]]
event = "tool:before"
match-tool = "bash"
reason = "blocked by safety addon"
```

The `DeclarativeLoader`'s produced `AddonManifest::register` is the agent's own replay closure — it captures the parsed (cloned) contributions and records them onto whatever surface the host hands it. It holds no third-party code, so it cannot throw.

**The registration surface.** The host hands each addon a fresh `RecordingSurface` scoped to that addon's `AddonId` and the session's `FrameworkHandles`. The surface is the trait `AddonApi` — the deliberately-narrow limited API. Each method *records* a contribution; nothing dispatches, loads, or resolves conflicts here:

```rust
pub trait AddonApi: Send {
    fn id(&self) -> &AddonId;
    fn on(&mut self, event: HookEvent, handler: HookHandler);
    fn intercept_tool(&mut self, match_: ToolMatch, enter: Option<EnterFn>, exit: Option<ExitFn>);
    fn add_command(&mut self, name: String, summary: String, run: CommandFn);
    fn add_tool(&mut self, card: AddonTool);
    fn handles(&self) -> &FrameworkHandles;
    fn manifest(self: Box<Self>) -> RegisteredManifest;
}
```

| Method | Records |
|--------|---------|
| `on(event, handler)` | An `EventSubscription` — a `HookHandler` bound to a `HookEvent`, stamped with the owning `AddonId`. |
| `intercept_tool(match_, enter, exit)` | A `ToolInterceptor` — an enter/exit stage pair for a `ToolMatch` (named tool or `Any`). |
| `add_command(name, summary, run)` | An `AddonCommand` (no leading slash, one-line summary, `run` callback). |
| `add_tool(card)` | An `AddonTool` — an `Arc<dyn Tool>` from `indusagi::capabilities`, supplied directly, not wrapped. |
| `handles()` | Read-only access to the `FrameworkHandles`. |
| `manifest()` | Consumes the surface and returns the accumulated `RegisteredManifest` for the host to fold. |

`RecordingSurface` appends each call to the accumulating `RegisteredManifest` (seeded by `RegisteredManifest::empty`), stamping every shape with the owning `AddonId` so a later fault is attributable.

**The manifest and the declarative loader.** `manifest.rs` owns the Tier-0 schema plus the v1 default `ModuleLoader`. Canonical filename `MANIFEST_FILENAME = "manifest.toml"`.

```rust
pub struct AddonDescriptor {
    pub id: String, pub version: Option<String>,
    pub commands: Vec<CommandDescriptor>,  // TOML [[command]]
    pub gates: Vec<GateDescriptor>,        // TOML [[gate]]
}
```

- `CommandDescriptor` — `name` (no leading slash), `summary`, optional `exec`. `AddonDescriptor::into_manifest` records each as a real `AddonCommand` whose `run` invokes the declared `exec` through `ctx.handles.exec` (raw `args` appended). A command with no `exec` (or no exec handle) is an inert no-op that still lists in the palette.
- `GateDescriptor` — an `event` (`HookEvent`), optional `match-tool`, a `reason`. Recorded as a `HookHandler::Gate`: a `tool:before` gate with `match-tool` returns `{ stop: true, reason }` only when the running tool's name matches the `Payload::Tool`; an unconditional gate stops the event whenever it fires; a tool-scoped gate against a non-tool payload never fires.

`AddonDescriptor::parse` deserializes and validates: `id` non-empty, every `[[command]]` a non-empty `name`. Failures surface as `ManifestError` (`Toml` for malformed TOML, `Invalid` for empty id/name). `DeclarativeLoader` is the stateless v1 `ModuleLoader`: given a directory holding `manifest.toml` or the manifest file itself, it reads + parses + validates and returns the `AddonManifest`. A bare `.ts`/`.js` path is **not** loadable here — rejected with `LoaderError::Unsupported` naming the tier the author must pick. No code execution: a parse/I/O failure is the only failure mode, surfaced as a `LoaderError` the host turns into an `AddonFault` of kind `Load`.

**Discovery and loading.** `discover_sources(&AddonDiscovery)` walks `<workspace>/.indus/addons` one level deep via `discover_addons`, concatenates `explicit_paths`, collapses duplicate paths (first wins), and stamps each surviving path with a derived `AddonId` into an `AddonSource`.

```rust
pub struct AddonDiscovery {
    pub workspace: Option<PathBuf>,     // root whose .indus/addons is scanned
    pub dir: Option<String>,            // override the per-workspace dir (defaults to ADDONS_DIR)
    pub explicit_paths: Vec<PathBuf>,   // additional absolute entry paths, loaded as-is
}
pub const ADDONS_DIR: &str = ".indus/addons";          // verbatim from the lineage
pub const ADDON_MANIFEST_FIELD: &str = "indusAddon";   // package.json entry pointer (back-compat)
```

`discover_addons(dir)` recognizes three top-level shapes (skipping dot-prefixed entries, sorting results; a missing/unreadable dir yields an empty list):

1. A **directory holding `manifest.toml`** → the Tier-0 canonical shape (resolves to the directory).
2. A **bare module file** carrying one of `ENTRY_EXTENSIONS` (`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.mts`/`.cts`/`.js`/`.mjs`/`.cjs`) → resolved to its path for the loader to decide the tier (the `DeclarativeLoader` rejects it).
3. A **package directory** declaring an entry via the `indusAddon` field in `package.json`, or holding a conventional `index.*` → recognized for back-compat; resolves to a Tier-1 subprocess, never an in-proc import.

`derive_addon_id` stamps the id: a directory entry uses its folder name; a conventional `index.*` uses the enclosing folder name; otherwise the file's stem. Loading is abstracted behind the injectable `ModuleLoader` trait — `async fn load(&self, path) -> Result<AddonManifest, LoaderError>` (`LoaderError` lives in `contract`, not re-exported at `addons`). A test injects a scripted fake.

**Hosting addons.** `AddonHost` is the assembly point; build with `create_addon_host(AddonHostDeps)`:

```rust
pub struct AddonHostDeps {
    pub loader: Box<dyn ModuleLoader>,
    pub handles: Arc<FrameworkHandles>,
    pub reserved_actions: Option<Vec<String>>,
}
pub const RESERVED_ACTION_NAMES: &[&str] = &["help", "quit", "exit", "clear", "model", "compact"];
```

`load_all(discovery)` discovers, loads, registers, folds every addon, returns the wired `AddonBundle`. `load_one(source)` grafts an explicitly-resolved addon without directory discovery. `on_fault(listener)` registers a fault listener returning an idempotent unsubscribe. The per-source pipeline isolates each step:

1. **Load** — resolve the source path through the injected loader. A failure → `AddonFault` (`kind: Load`, attributed to the source id, `LoaderError` as `cause`); the source is skipped.
2. **Register** — mint a `RecordingSurface` scoped to the addon's id (manifest's declared `id` wins; source-derived id is fallback) and host's handles, then `register`.
3. **Fold** — read the surface's `RegisteredManifest` and merge its four streams.

The fold preserves registration order across addons (dispatcher middleware order and chain onion order equal load order). Subscriptions and interceptors append unconditionally. Commands and tools are name-checked against the claimed sets — `claimed_commands` is *seeded with the reserved names*, so an addon command named `help` is rejected with a `Conflict` fault distinct from a duplicate-command conflict; tools dedupe on `Tool::name()`. First claimant wins.

```rust
pub struct AddonRegistry {
    pub subscriptions: Vec<EventSubscription>,  // load order = dispatch order
    pub interceptors: Vec<ToolInterceptor>,     // load order = onion order
    pub commands: Vec<AddonCommand>,            // name-deduped, first-claimant-wins
    pub tools: Vec<AddonTool>,                  // name-deduped
}
pub struct AddonBundle {
    pub dispatch: EventDispatcher, pub interceptors: InterceptorChain,
    pub commands: Vec<AddonCommand>, pub tools: Vec<AddonTool>, pub loaded: Vec<AddonId>,
}
```

`host.registry()` exposes the merged registry before bundling consumes it. The dispatcher and chain built by `bundle()` are wired to the host's *same* fault sink, so a later runtime fault reaches listeners registered before `load_all` ran. The fault sink guards every listener with `catch_unwind` so a panicking listener cannot break fan-out.

**The event dispatcher.** `EventDispatcher` is one fan-out/transform/veto engine over the colon-named taxonomy, built once from the folded `EventSubscription`s; per `dispatch` it walks an event's subscriptions in registration order. The handler kind selects behavior:

- `HookHandler::Observe` — fire-and-forget; sees a clone of the live payload, cannot alter or veto.
- `HookHandler::Transform` — returns a replacement `Payload` threaded forward and back to the caller.
- `HookHandler::Gate` — returns a `GateDecision`; the first `stop: true` short-circuits into `DispatchOutcome::gate`.

The `HookEvent` vocabulary is a real exhaustive enum (de)serializing to colon-segmented wire names:

| Event | Gate-bearing (`guards`) | Meaning |
|-------|-------------------------|---------|
| `session:start` / `session:end` | — | A session opened / closed. |
| `turn:start` / `turn:end` | — | An assistant turn began / settled. |
| `tool:before` / `tool:after` | `tool:before` | Straddle a single tool execution. |
| `chat:params` | — | The model request options being built. |
| `chat:message` | — | An assistant message was assembled. |
| `shell:env` | — | The environment for a shell action being prepared. |
| `input:submit` | yes | User input entering the loop. |
| `context:build` | — | The message context being assembled. |
| `compact:build` | — | The condensed summary being built. |
| `compact:before` | yes | The transcript about to be condensed. |

The Rust `Payload` is a checked enum keyed by event group (`Tool { name, args }`, `Chat { params }`, `Message`, `Shell { env }`, `Input { text }`, `Context { messages }`, `Compact { reason }`, `Lifecycle`) — so a handler can't be wired to the wrong shape (additive parity, not divergence). The gate-bearing set is data-sourced from `HookEvent::guards()` (a single `matches!`, the analogue of the TS `EVENT_TRAITS` table); `EventDispatcher::reserved()` exposes the derived set (`tool:before`, `input:submit`, `compact:before`). The in-proc boxed closures return infallible futures, so the Tier-0 reduce cannot synthesize a handler fault — the fault seam is retained for the Tier-1 subprocess loader. `dispatch.has(event)` queries whether any addon subscribed.

**The tool interceptor chain.** `InterceptorChain` folds matching `ToolInterceptor` stages around a single tool execution as a reduce. A stage's `match_` is `ToolMatch::Named(name)` or `ToolMatch::Any`:

1. **enter, forward.** Each matching stage's `enter` runs in registration order, returning an `EnterOutcome`: `Continue` / `Rewrite(Value)` (replace decoded args) / `Block(GateDecision)` (veto). A block short-circuits — no later enter runs, the tool never executes, `InterceptResult` carries `blocked` with `result == None`.
2. **execute, once.** With the final (possibly rewritten) args, the real tool runner is invoked exactly once.
3. **exit, reverse.** Each matching stage's `exit` runs in reverse order (onion), returning an `ExitOutcome`: `Continue` / `Rewrite(ToolResult)`. A rewrite threads into the next earlier stage.

When no stage matches, `execute` runs directly with the original args. The chain ships two run variants: `run(ctx, execute)` takes a `'static` `ToolResultProducer` (host-level boundary); `run_with(ctx, execute)` threads the identical reduce but lets `execute` return any non-`'static` future — the variant the capability deck's tool-boundary wrapper needs (so a wrapper can call `|args| inner.run(args, ctx)` without lifting the borrowed `&ToolContext` to `'static`). `chain.matches(tool)` answers whether any interceptor applies. In the Tier-0 path the `ToolResultProducer` resolves a `ToolResult` (using its `is_error` flag rather than a throw), so `ToolExitContext::error` is left `None`; the Tier-1 loader will populate it.

**Slash commands and framework handles.** Addon commands describe an effect, not a console state transition; the model never calls a command, the user does, by name. An `AddonCommand` carries a `name` (no leading slash), one-line `summary`, owning `addon`, and `run: CommandFn` over a `CommandContext`:

```rust
pub struct CommandContext {
    pub args: String,              // raw argument string after the command name
    pub cwd: PathBuf,              // absolute working directory
    pub handles: Arc<FrameworkHandles>,
}
```

`FrameworkHandles` is the controlled channel an addon acts through. Every handle is optional (`None` when absent; a print/JSON run mode supplies fewer than an interactive TUI):

| Handle | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| `send_message(String)` | Inject an assistant-visible message into the active turn. |
| `set_model(String)` | Switch the active model by canonical id. |
| `set_thinking(String)` | Adjust the reasoning-effort level for subsequent turns. |
| `exec(String)` | Run a shell command and resolve its captured `ExecOutcome` (`stdout` / `stderr` / `code: Option<i32>`). |

These handles and the colon `HookEvent` taxonomy are the intended seams with the conductor session, the capability deck tool boundary, and the console command registry. (The TS layer's `render(component)` handle is dropped — interactive rendering is not part of the Rust handle set.)

**The sandbox.** `sandbox.rs` ports the non-jiti half of the TS `addons/sandbox.ts`. `SandboxPolicy` is deny-by-default:

```rust
pub struct SandboxPolicy {
    pub allow_fs: bool,                  // default false
    pub workspace_root: Option<PathBuf>, // confinement root
    pub timeout_ms: u64,                 // per-call wall-clock (Tier-1 subprocess), default 30_000
    pub env_allowlist: Vec<String>,      // env names passed to a Tier-1 subprocess; empty = none
}
```

- `SandboxPolicy::deny_all()` (also `Default`) grants nothing.
- `SandboxPolicy::confined_to(root)` grants FS access confined to `root`.
- `permits_path(path)` enforces deny-by-default in order: FS-denied → never; no confinement root → never; otherwise the path, resolved and **lexically normalized** so `..` cannot climb out, must lie at or under the root (the classic escape `<root>/../etc/passwd` is rejected rather than slipping through a naive `starts_with`). Symlinks are not resolved (no I/O); normalization is purely lexical and deterministic.
- `permits_env(name)` honors the allowlist; an empty allowlist inherits nothing.

Path-hygiene helpers (the single normalizer every loader/policy entry funnels through):

| Helper | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| `scrub_invisible(raw)` | Strip invisible/non-standard whitespace (an explicit `INVISIBLE_CODE_POINTS` list: NBSP, zero-width space/joiner/non-joiner, LTR/RTL marks, word joiner, BOM, fixed-width typographic spaces, narrow/medium/ideographic spaces) and trim ASCII edges. Astral characters (emoji) survive intact. |
| `expand_path(raw, home)` | Scrub, then expand a *leading* `~` (or `~/`) to home (a `~` mid-path is ordinary); falls back to the literal on an unresolvable home. |
| `resolve_path(raw, base, home)` | Scrub + expand-home + anchor against `base` (default: process cwd) when not already absolute. |

**Subagents** (`subagents.rs`, feature `swarm`). The coordination half — no TS source (PLAN/75 §4.3, a Rust-design adapter onto the already-complete `indusagi::swarm` and `indusagi::smithy`; crew coordination is never rebuilt). A `SubagentProfile` (declared in `contract.rs`, ungated) is the `.indus/agents/<name>.toml` shape — `name` (defaults to the file stem), optional `model`, optional `tool_collection`, optional `prompt`. `AGENTS_DIR = ".indus/agents"` (a sibling of `ADDONS_DIR`). `discover_profiles(workspace)` walks it one level deep, deserializing each `*.toml`, isolating a malformed file (returning its `Err` alongside the parsed profiles). The adapter:

| Function | Maps a profile onto |
|----------|---------------------|
| `to_agent_spec(profile)` | an `indusagi::smithy::AgentSpec` (partial spec merged by `define_agent`). |
| `to_blueprint(profile)` | a validated `indusagi::smithy::AgentBlueprint` via smithy's single validation gate (a non-kebab/empty `name` surfaces `BlueprintError`). |
| `to_member_draft(profile)` | an `indusagi::swarm::MemberDraft` (the crew mints the id; `name` is the member's `role`). |

`DelegateRunner` is the handle the deck/boot delegate-runner wiring calls (the `DeckFramework.delegate` handle deferred from the deck milestone). Given discovered profiles and a crew directory, `run(tasks)` enrolls a crew over `indusagi::swarm::create_crew`, posts the tasks, drives `Crew::run_round` until the board quiesces or the `DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS = 64` cap is hit, returning a flattened `DelegationReport` (`crew_id`, `completed`, `failed`, `rounds`). Per-teammate git-worktree isolation is framework-given (via `with_base_repo`). `SubagentCrew` is the standing-roster view.

**Faults.** `AddonFault` is a typed record (not raised) — always routed to `on_fault` listeners and swallowed. It carries a `kind` (`AddonFaultKind`), a one-line `message`, an optional `addon`, and optional `cause`:

| Kind | Raised when |
|------|-------------|
| `Load` | Resolving/loading an addon module failed (the `LoaderError` rides as `cause`). |
| `Register` | An addon's `register` threw (reserved for in-proc Tier-1+ loaders; impossible for Tier-0). |
| `Handler` | An event handler or interceptor stage threw at runtime (the Tier-1 RPC seam). |
| `Command` | A slash command handler threw. |
| `Conflict` | Two addons claimed the same command/tool name, or an addon claimed a reserved action name. |

Construct with `AddonFault::new(kind, message)`, attributing with `.with_addon(id)` / `.with_cause(err)`. It implements `std::error::Error` (exposing `cause`) and `Display` (`[Kind] message (addon: id)`). `AddonFaultListener` is `Arc<dyn Fn(&AddonFault) + Send + Sync>`.

**Reachability.** `mod.rs` re-exports the contract types plus runtime entry points directly at `induscode::addons`; the remaining items are reached through their full module path (e.g. `induscode::addons::host::create_addon_host`, `induscode::addons::manifest::DeclarativeLoader`, `induscode::addons::contract::ToolResultProducer`). `AddonTool` is a plain alias of `Arc<dyn indusagi::capabilities::Tool>`, so the deck merges a contributed tool like any native/MCP tool. **Built-but-unwired:** as checked in, the layer has a standalone test suite across its modules but is the contract + runtime; the `FrameworkHandles` bag, the `HookEvent` taxonomy, and `InterceptorChain::run_with` mark the intended integration points with the conductor, deck, and console.

#### Insight (observability)

`induscode::insight` is the agent's single observability plane (`src/insight`) — a thin wrapper crate over the already-built framework `indusagi::tracing` that re-expresses the agent's vocabulary (trail / probe / signal) at the surface and adds only the four pieces the framework lacks: a multi-consumer **fan-out** channel, an in-memory **collector** sink, an **agent scrubber** (TS-style value-run redaction + length caps + omit-keys), and an **NDJSON replay** reader over a durable `{v,phase,probe,at}` envelope. It is the lower-level distributed-tracing plane: timed probes, sampling gates, secret redaction, fan-out to sinks, and replay of persisted traces. It is **not** a re-port — `ProbeKind`, `Probe`, `Signal`, `TrailId`, and `ProbeId` are zero-cost aliases/bijections onto the framework's `Segment`, `TraceSignal`, `SegmentKind`, and plain-`String` ids.

**What this is NOT:** there is no cost, token, or usage accounting code anywhere in `src/insight`. Footer usage/cost/token/context statistics are rendered by the framework's status widgets through the console status bar — conceptually adjacent but with **no code dependency** on this subsystem.

**Module layout** (eight modules behind `insight/mod.rs`, from PLAN/80 §4.1):

| Module | Role |
|--------|------|
| `model.rs` (PLAN: `vocab`) | The agent vocabulary aliased onto the framework — `Probe`/`ClosedProbe`/`Signal`/`TrailId`/`ProbeId` aliases, the `ProbeKind` enum + `PROBE_KINDS`, the kind map (`to_segment`/`from_segment`), `SignalPhase`, and the `signal_phase`/`signal_segment`/`is_close_signal`/`is_closed_probe` guards. |
| `serialize.rs` | The durable NDJSON `{v,phase,probe,at}` record format shared by file sink + replay reader; canonical-JSON byte parity + U+2028/U+2029 escaping. |
| `recorder.rs` | `AgentRecorder`: the framework `Recorder` plus the scrub-before-sink interposition (a pump task) and sink-drain ownership the framework lacks. |
| `redaction.rs` | `AgentScrubber` over the framework `SecretScrubber`: key-path detection, value-run replacement, length caps, omit-keys, fault scrubbing. |
| `sinks/` | Re-exports the framework console/file/stream sinks + the agent's `CollectorSink` and `AgentFileSink`. |
| `replay.rs` | `read_lines`/`read_records`/`replay_signals`/`replay_probes`/`replay_trails` over the envelope format. |
| `sampling.rs` | `always_gate`/`never_gate`/`ratio_gate(fraction)` facades over `SampleGate` + the `verdict` helper. |
| `fanout.rs` | `FanoutChannel`: N independent readers off one producer — multi-consumer fan-out the single-consumer framework channel cannot do. |

The four agent-built pieces are exactly: `fanout.rs`, `sinks::collector` (sink + agent file sink), `redaction.rs`, and `replay.rs`. Everything else is a thin re-expression of the framework surface.

**The vocabulary aliases.** `model.rs` ports the frozen TS `insight/contract.ts` surface as zero-cost aliases onto `indusagi::tracing`:

```rust
pub type TrailId = String;       // branded string naming a trail (transparent)
pub type ProbeId = String;       // branded string naming a probe
pub type Probe = Segment;        // an immutable timed segment within a trail
pub type ClosedProbe = TraceRecord;  // exported serializable form of a closed probe
pub type Signal = TraceSignal;   // the closed wire-event union, discriminated by phase
```

Id byte widths (single source of truth in `model::id_widths`, matching W3C Trace Context sizing): `TRAIL = 16` bytes → 32 hex chars (128-bit); `PROBE = 8` bytes → 16 hex chars (64-bit). Two predicates narrow the aliases: `is_closed_probe(probe)` (`true` when `status != SegmentStatus::Open && ended_at.is_some()`) and `is_close_signal(signal)` (`true` for a terminal `TraceSignal::Close`).

**The kind map.** The agent thinks in **run / turn / tool / model / custom**; the framework persists **run / inference / action / recall / custom**. `ProbeKind` is bijective with `SegmentKind` (`ProbeKind::from_segment(k.to_segment()) == k`, the `kind_map_round_trips` test):

```rust
pub enum ProbeKind { Run, Turn, Tool, Model, Custom }
pub const PROBE_KINDS: [ProbeKind; 5] = [Run, Turn, Tool, Model, Custom];
```

| App `ProbeKind` | Framework `SegmentKind` |
|-----------------|-------------------------|
| `Run` | `Run` |
| `Turn` | `Inference` |
| `Tool` | `Action` |
| `Model` | `Recall` |
| `Custom` | `Custom` |

**Signals and phases.** On the wire a probe transition is a `Signal` (alias of `TraceSignal`). The framework discriminates by its serde `type` tag rather than a `phase` field, so `model.rs` re-expresses that as `SignalPhase` (serializing to the TS literals so the envelope `phase` is byte-identical):

```rust
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum SignalPhase { Open, Update, Close } // → "open" / "update" / "close"
pub fn signal_phase(signal: &Signal) -> SignalPhase;
pub fn signal_segment(signal: &Signal) -> Option<&Probe>;
```

`signal_segment` is load-bearing for **Gotcha G-2**: `Open` carries the full segment and `Close` carries `record.segment()`, but a framework `Update` carries only `{id, attributes}` — not the full probe the TS `UpdateSignal.probe` did — so `signal_segment` returns `None` for an update. The recorder/serializer re-materializes the live segment for that line instead.

**The recorder.** `AgentRecorder` is the head of the pipeline (the TS `InsightRecorder`). It wraps the framework `Recorder` (which owns the raw, pre-scrub `SignalChannel` every opened `SegmentHandle` emits onto), interposes the `AgentScrubber` via a pump task, fans the scrubbed stream out to N sinks through a `FanoutChannel`, and owns every drain `JoinHandle`.

```rust
pub struct RecorderOptions {
    pub service: String,                  // DEFAULT_SERVICE = "insight"
    pub enabled: bool,                    // master switch; a disabled recorder is all no-ops
    pub gate: Option<SampleGate>,         // admission gate; defaults to always_gate when enabled
    pub scrubber: Option<AgentScrubber>,  // None ⇒ AgentScrubber::passthru()
}
```

Methods: `new`, `enabled`, `service`, `channel`, `open_trail(kind, name, trail_id)`, `scope_open(trail_id, kind, name)`, `scope_child(trail_id, parent_id, kind, name)`, `attach_sink<S>`, `async flush`, `async shutdown`.

- **Scrub-before-sink pump (G-4):** the framework `Recorder` emits raw segments with no redaction hook, so the recorder spawns a pump task that *is* the seam — it drains the raw framework channel, runs every signal through `AgentScrubber::scrub_signal`, and re-emits onto the fanout (`fan.emit(scrubber.scrub_signal(signal))`); when the raw channel drains it calls `fan.close()`. No sink ever sees a secret.
- **Gates, scope, sampling-out:** `new` resolves the gate as `enabled ? options.gate.unwrap_or(always_gate) : never_gate()` — a disabled recorder forces `never_gate`. `open_trail` maps the agent kind via `to_segment`, supplies `OpenOptions { trace_id, .. }`, and the gate decides on the minted-or-supplied trace id ("mint first, then admit", G-6). A sampled-out trail collapses to `SegmentHandle::noop` so its whole subtree is free; `scope_open`/`scope_child` join a known trail by id.
- **Sink attachment and shutdown (G-5):** `attach_sink` spawns each sink's `drain` loop on an independent `FanoutChannel::reader` and retains the `JoinHandle`. Because the framework `Sink::drain` is a bare `async fn` in a trait (whose future carries no auto-`Send` bound provable for a generic `S`, and stable Rust cannot name it), each drain runs on its own dedicated blocking thread via a current-thread runtime (`tokio::task::spawn_blocking`); only the captured `sink` + `reader` cross the thread boundary, never the future. `shutdown` flushes, closes the framework channel (ending the pump loop → closing the fanout → driving every drain to terminal `None`), then joins the pump and every drain (the `Promise.allSettled` analogue — joining never panic-propagates).

**The fanout channel.** The framework `SignalChannel` is explicitly single-consumer (a second `reader()` shares the same FIFO queue). `FanoutChannel` reproduces the TS `createChannel` multiplex without re-implementing the transport: it owns a `Vec<SignalChannel>`, one framework channel per subscriber, preserving per-subscriber FIFO back-pressure (so a slow sink never starves another) — chosen over `tokio::sync::broadcast`, which would collapse the buffers into one shared ring (OQ-4).

```rust
pub struct FanoutChannel { /* Arc<Inner> of subscriber channels + a closed latch */ }
impl FanoutChannel {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
    pub fn reader(&self) -> SignalChannelReader;  // attach a fresh independent channel
    pub fn emit(&self, signal: TraceSignal);      // clone onto every subscriber; no-op once closed
    pub fn close(&self);                          // close every subscriber channel; idempotent
    pub fn size(&self) -> usize;
    pub fn is_closed(&self) -> bool;
}
```

Cheaply `Clone`able (every clone shares the same `Arc<Inner>`). A subscriber only sees signals emitted *after* it attaches; a reader attached after `close` finishes at once.

**Sampling gates** (`sampling.rs`, one-line facades over `indusagi::tracing::SampleGate`):

| Facade | Behaviour |
|--------|-----------|
| `always_gate()` | Admit every trail (`SampleStrategy::Always`); the recorder default when enabled. |
| `never_gate()` | Reject every trail (`SampleStrategy::Never`). |
| `ratio_gate(fraction: f64)` | Admit a deterministic fraction (`SampleStrategy::Ratio(fraction)`), keyed on the trail id. |
| `fixed_gates()` | Bundle `{ always, never }` (`FixedGates`) for the recorder fallback. |
| `verdict(gate, trail_id)` | The sticky, id-keyed verdict the recorder consults (over `SampleGate::decide`). |

`ratio_gate` is FNV-1a-keyed on the trail id and **bit-identical** to the TS `trailScore` (same constants `0x811c9dc5` / `0x01000193` / `2^32`, same byte fold). Edge fractions short-circuit (`<= 0` rejects all, `>= 1` admits all); a `NaN` fraction **fails closed to 0**. The verdict is a pure function of the id — never a coin flip. The TS `ratioGate.admit(rootName)` name-only fallback is intentionally not reproduced (the recorder always has the trace id before deciding, G-6).

**Secret redaction.** `AgentScrubber` is the attribute processor the pipeline runs before a sink (the `route()` step with no framework seam). Three things trigger a redaction on a single depth-first walk that tracks the enclosing key as it descends (so nested secrets like `{ http: { headers: { authorization: "…" } } }` are caught by key):

1. a **key-path** match — the key contains a secret-bearing fragment → the whole subtree tokenizes;
2. a **value** match — a string looks like a credential regardless of its key → **only the matched run** is replaced;
3. an **omit** — a key in `omit_keys` is dropped entirely.

```rust
pub const REDACTED_TOKEN: &str = "[insight:scrubbed]";        // NOT the framework's ‹redacted›
pub const DEFAULT_MAX_STRING_LENGTH: usize = 4096;
pub const TRUNCATION_SUFFIX: &str = "...[insight:truncated]";

pub struct AgentScrubber { /* key_fragments, compiled value_patterns, max_len, omit_keys, passthru */ }
impl AgentScrubber {
    pub fn new(max_len: usize, omit_keys: Vec<String>) -> Self;
    pub fn passthru() -> Self;                          // PASSTHRU_REDACTOR (identity)
    pub fn scrub_value(&self, value: &Value) -> Value;
    pub fn scrub_attributes(&self, attributes: &Map<String, Value>) -> Map<String, Value>;
    pub fn scrub_fault(&self, fault: &SegmentError) -> SegmentError;  // scrubs the single `message`
    pub fn scrub_segment(&self, segment: &Segment) -> Segment;        // attributes + fault
    pub fn scrub_signal(&self, signal: TraceSignal) -> TraceSignal;   // the pump's per-signal step
}
pub fn default_redactor() -> AgentScrubber;   // DEFAULT_REDACTOR: default rules + caps
```

It composes the agent's behaviours over the framework rule vocabulary (referencing the framework `REDACTION_TOKEN` const to keep the dependency edge real), layering on the four behaviours the framework lacks: TS-style value-run replacement, `max_string_length` truncation, `omit_keys` wholesale drop, `SegmentError` fault scrubbing. The walk never mutates its input; output is always freshly allocated, and scrubbing is **idempotent**. `scrub_signal` is G-2-aware (scrubs the full segment for `Open`/`Close`, only the attribute bag for an `Update`). Default rules:

| Rule kind | Examples |
|-----------|----------|
| `SECRET_KEY_FRAGMENTS` (case-insensitive substring of the key) | `apikey`, `api_key`, `secret`, `password`, `passwd`, `authorization`, `auth_token`, `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `session_token`, `private_key`, `credential`, `cookie`, `set-cookie`, `bearer` |
| `SECRET_VALUE_SOURCES` (compiled `regex`, run-level replacement) | `Bearer`/`Basic`/`Token` scheme prefixes; provider keys (`sk-…`, `pk-…`, live/test variants); GitHub tokens (`ghp_`/`gho_`/`ghs_`/`github_pat_`); AWS access key ids (`AKIA…`); JWTs (three base64url segments); PEM private-key blocks |

**The NDJSON envelope.** `serialize.rs` defines the durable format shared by file sink + replay reader. The agent envelope is `{v, phase, probe, at}` written for **every** phase (open/update/close) — not the framework's bare close-only `TraceRecord(Segment)`, because replay of in-flight probes needs the open/update lines (G-3):

```rust
pub const RECORD_VERSION: u8 = 1;
pub const LINE_FEED: char = '\n';
pub struct TraceRecord {
    pub v: u8,             // RECORD_VERSION; a future reader can branch on it
    pub phase: SignalPhase,
    pub probe: Probe,      // the framework Segment (camelCase serde matches TS field names)
    pub at: u64,           // emission clock, epoch ms
}
// record_from_parts, signal_to_record (None for a framework Update, G-2),
// encode_record, encode_signal (open/close fast path; None for Update),
// decode_record, record_is_close (phase == Close), signal_is_close
```

Field declaration order is `v, phase, probe, at` (matching the TS object-literal key order). **Byte parity** with TS `JSON.stringify` is guaranteed by routing every encode through `indusagi::core::canonical_json` (JS key order + number formatting + string escaping) rather than `serde_json::to_string`. U+2028 (LINE SEPARATOR) and U+2029 (PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR) are escaped so a strictly-newline reader recovers each line intact. Each line is terminated by exactly one `\n`.

**Sinks and the collector.** `sinks/mod.rs` re-exports the framework `Sink` trait, `ConsoleSink`, `FileSink`, `StreamSink<W>` (and their `*Options`) unchanged, and adds two sinks (both in `sinks/collector.rs`):

| Sink | Source | Role |
|------|--------|------|
| `ConsoleSink` / `FileSink` / `StreamSink` | `indusagi::tracing` (re-exported) | The framework's console / NDJSON-file / generic-writer sinks, which persist **close records only**. |
| `CollectorSink` | `sinks/collector.rs` | The in-memory test/inspection sink: drains a channel into a shared `Vec<TraceSignal>`, capturing **every** phase in arrival order. |
| `AgentFileSink` | `sinks/collector.rs` | The agent's durable file sink: writes the `{v,phase,probe,at}` envelope for every probe-carrying phase (vs. the framework `FileSink`'s close-only bare `Segment`). |

`CollectorSink` (`Arc<Mutex<Vec<TraceSignal>>>`; `Clone` shares the backing buffer): `new`, `signals()` (every drained signal, arrival order), `close_records()` (the cooked terminal-only view), `len`, `is_empty`. `AgentFileSink`:

```rust
pub struct AgentFileSinkOptions {
    pub path: PathBuf,
    pub mkdirp: bool,    // create parent dir if missing; default true
    pub truncate: bool,  // truncate on open instead of appending; default false
}
// AgentFileSink::new(path), ::with_options(options)
```

The file is opened **lazily** on the first probe-carrying signal (an unused sink touches no disk); `drain` flushes the OS buffer when the stream ends; the separate idempotent `Sink::close` flushes-then-shuts the handle. Each signal is written via the shared `encode_signal` codec (writer and replay reader provably agree). `at` is the segment's own timing — `started_at` for an open, `record.ended_at()` for a close. Update signals (no full probe, G-2) are **skipped**. Writing the open lines is exactly what makes the replay round-trip work.

**Replay.** `replay.rs` is a pure reader over the envelope with no framework dependency beyond `Probe`/`TraceRecord`. It never imports the recorder; a malformed line is, by default, **skipped** rather than fatal:

```rust
pub struct ReplayOptions { pub strict: bool }   // error on a malformed line instead of skipping
pub enum ReplayError { Json(serde_json::Error), Malformed }
```

| Function | Yields |
|----------|--------|
| `read_lines<S>(source)` | Chunk → line splitter over a `Stream<Item = String>`: splits on `\n` only, drops blank lines, emits a trailing unterminated final line. |
| `read_records<S>(source, options)` | Decodes each line, validating `v == RECORD_VERSION` + a known phase; skips a malformed line by default, or yields one `Err` and stops under `strict`. |
| `replay_signals<S>(source, options)` | The flat `{ phase, probe, at }` records in file order (`ReplaySignal`, since the framework `Update` cannot carry phase+probe, G-2). |
| `replay_probes<S>(source, options)` | The final value of each probe, keyed by id (close wins over open) in first-seen insertion order (`IndexMap`). |
| `replay_trails<S>(source, options)` | The collapsed probes grouped into per-trail parent→children trees. |

```rust
pub struct ReplaySignal { pub phase: SignalPhase, pub probe: Probe, pub at: u64 }
pub struct ReplayedTrail {
    pub trail_id: TrailId,
    pub root: Option<Probe>,                              // the parentless probe, if seen
    pub probes: IndexMap<ProbeId, Probe>,                 // every probe, first-seen order
    pub children: HashMap<Option<ProbeId>, Vec<ProbeId>>, // parent→children; roots under the None key
    pub complete: bool,                                   // true iff every probe is terminal
}
```

`replay_trails` first collapses to final probe values (close wins, file order preserved via `IndexMap`), buckets by `trace_id`, assembles each `ReplayedTrail` via `build_trail` (walks the collapsed map, builds parent→children adjacency, locates the root where `parent_id.is_none()`, sets `complete = false` if any probe is not closed). Because the file sink writes opens too, the reader tolerates a foreign writer that persists open records.

**Notable behaviour.** (1) No cost/token/usage/footer accounting lives here. (2) Wrapper, not re-port — only four pieces are agent-built (fanout, collector + agent file sink, scrubber, replay). (3) Scrub-before-sink is the seam (G-4). (4) A framework `Update` carries no full probe (G-2): `signal_segment` returns `None`, `encode_signal` declines it, the file sink skips update lines; fault info is on `Segment.error` (`SegmentError.message`, the single field `scrub_fault` scrubs). (5) Per-subscriber FIFO fan-out (chosen over `tokio::sync::broadcast`). (6) Drains run on dedicated blocking threads via `spawn_blocking`; `shutdown` joins them (G-5). (7) Byte-faithful NDJSON through `canonical_json`. (8) Crash-tolerant replay.

**On the framework.** Everything below this wrapper belongs to `indusagi`: the transport (`SignalChannel`/`SignalChannelReader`), the `Recorder` + `SegmentHandle` + `OpenOptions`, the `Segment`/`SegmentKind`/`SegmentStatus`/`SegmentError`/`TraceRecord`/`TraceSignal` value types, the `SampleGate`/`SampleStrategy` admission engine, the `SecretScrubber` + `REDACTION_TOKEN`, and the three console/file/stream `Sink`s are all consumed from `indusagi::tracing`; the canonical-JSON encoder is `indusagi::core::canonical_json`.
