The insight subsystem adds exactly four things on top: a multi-consumer fan-out channel, an in-memory collector sink, an agent secret scrubber, and an NDJSON replay reader over a durable per-phase envelope.


### Configuration

The Rust `induscode` agent (docs area `/rust-cli`, user-facing commands `indus` / `indusagi`, cargo `[[bin]]` targets `indusr` / `indusagir`) reads its configuration from four cooperating subsystems: a 24-key preference store, a credential vault, a model catalog, and an MCP server mount. All per-user state nests under `~/.indusagi/agent/` (the framework's own root is `~/.indusagi`), relocatable as a whole with `INDUSAGI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`. Identity facts are single-sourced from `brand.rs`:

```rust
// brand.rs — the single source of identity truth
profile_dir_name:  ".indusagi"
state_dir_name:    "agent"
env_prefix:        "INDUSAGI"
env_profile_dir:   "INDUSAGI_CODING_AGENT_DIR"
env_debug:         "INDUSAGI_DEBUG"
```

The shared per-user state directory (`induscode::core::workspace::create_workspace`):

| `Workspace` field | Default location | Holds |
|-------------------|------------------|-------|
| `profile_dir` | `~/.indusagi/agent/` | Root of all per-user agent state |
| `settings_path` | `~/.indusagi/agent/settings.json` | Global preference tier |
| `auth_path` | `~/.indusagi/agent/auth.json` | Stored credentials |
| `sessions_dir` | `~/.indusagi/agent/sessions/` | Persisted transcripts |
| `models_path` | `~/.indusagi/agent/models.json` | Custom model-catalog overrides |
| `mcp_config_path` | `~/.indusagi/agent/mcp-servers.json` | External MCP servers |
| `themes_dir` | `~/.indusagi/agent/themes/` | User-installed colour themes |
| `prompts_dir` | `~/.indusagi/agent/prompts/` | User-authored prompt/command templates |
| `memory_db_path` | `~/.indusagi/agent/memory.db` | On-disk memory database |

The profile root resolves by a fixed, filesystem-free precedence ladder (`workspace::resolve_profile_root`):

| Variable | Effect | Precedence |
|----------|--------|------------|
| `INDUSAGI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` | Agent-specific override; its value **is** the profile dir | Highest |
| _(unset)_ | `<home>/.indusagi/agent` | Default |

The override value is `~`-expanded (`~` → home, `~/...` → home-relative), resolved against the cwd when relative, passed through when absolute, and treated as absent when blank/whitespace-only (matching the TS `?.trim()` gate). Unlike the framework `Locator` (which honours `INDUSAGI_HOME`), the coding agent reads only `INDUSAGI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`.

```bash
# Relocate all per-user agent state (settings, auth, sessions, …) for one shell
export INDUSAGI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=/srv/induscode-state
indusr --version

# A tilde override is home-anchored
export INDUSAGI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=~/work/induscode-home
indusagir
```

#### Settings

`induscode::core::settings` (a `PreferenceStore`) is the **24-key** user-preference surface an interactive session reads at startup and mutates while it runs. It is folded into `induscode-core` (the `src/core/` tree) and builds on the framework's tolerant-load + 3-layer-merge pattern (`indusagi::shell_app::config`'s `read_settings_file` / `normalize_settings` / `merge_layer`), with the agent's own 24-key record and a writer the framework loader lacks. The reasoning-effort vocabulary `default_thinking_level` carries is reused directly from `indusagi::llmgateway::contract::ThinkingLevel`. This is parity with the TypeScript `src/settings` subsystem (porting `contract.ts` + `manager.ts`) and the Python `induscode.settings` subpackage; the on-disk JSON is byte-compatible, but Rust adds the 24th key (`permissions`) that the legacy 23-key Python doc predates.

**Module layout** (two source files behind `core/settings/mod.rs`):

| Module | Path | Responsibility |
|--------|------|----------------|
| `contract` | `core/settings/contract.rs` | Pure shapes/defaults — `Preferences`, `PermissionSettings`, the vocab enums (`EscapeAction`, `DeliveryMode`, `PermissionMode`) with alias folding, `default_preferences()`, and the `SETTING_KEYS` slice. No I/O. |
| `store` | `core/settings/store.rs` | Filesystem — `PreferenceStore`, the two-tier reader/writer, `PreferenceLocations`, and the tolerant `load_tier` / `write_tier` / `overlay` helpers. |

**Three-layer merge.** A read resolves across three layers, **per key**, first non-`None` wins:

1. **Project tier** — `<cwd>/.indusagi/settings.json` (one per checkout; note: directly under `.indusagi`, **no** `agent/` segment).
2. **Global tier** — `<workspace.settings_path>`, normally `~/.indusagi/agent/settings.json` (one per machine).
3. **Frozen defaults** — `default_preferences()`, where all 24 keys carry a concrete `Some(..)`.

```rust
pub fn resolved(&self) -> Preferences {
    let mut out = default_preferences();
    overlay(&mut out, &self.global_tier);
    overlay(&mut out, &self.project_tier);
    out
}
```

`resolved()` materializes the merge (every field `Some`); `snapshot()` is its alias. The merge is **idempotent** (re-feeding a resolved snapshot through a tier is a no-op — the Verify golden property). A write via `stage(..)` + `save()` lands in the **project tier only** — the global file is read but never rewritten, so a per-checkout change can never leak machine-wide. The project tier is **not** relocated by the env overrides (which only move the profile root). `from_workspace` joins `BRAND.profile_dir_name` only for the project path:

```rust
pub fn from_workspace(workspace: &Workspace, cwd: &Path) -> Self {
    Self::at_paths(PreferenceLocations {
        global: workspace.settings_path.clone(),
        project: cwd.join(BRAND.profile_dir_name).join("settings.json"),
    })
}
```

**The Preferences record** is a flat struct of 24 fully-optional fields, `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` on every field; `None` plays the "key not present" role and is omitted from JSON rather than written as `null`. `default_preferences()` is a `fn` (not a `const`, since it owns `Vec`s + a nested struct).

**Setting catalog** — all 24 keys (snake_case field, camelCase `SETTING_KEYS` spelling, type, default, meaning):

| Field | JSON key | Type | Default | Controls |
|-------|----------|------|---------|----------|
| `colour_scheme` | `colourScheme` | `Option<String>` | `"default"` | Named colour scheme the console renders with |
| `show_images` | `showImages` | `Option<bool>` | `true` | Inline image content rendered in the transcript |
| `show_reasoning` | `showReasoning` | `Option<bool>` | `true` | Model reasoning text shown as it streams |
| `hide_thinking` | `hideThinking` | `Option<bool>` | `false` | Fold the reasoning block away even if emitted |
| `image_auto_resize` | `imageAutoResize` | `Option<bool>` | `true` | Shrink oversized images before handing to a provider |
| `block_images` | `blockImages` | `Option<bool>` | `false` | Withhold image content from providers entirely |
| `enable_skill_commands` | `enableSkillCommands` | `Option<bool>` | `true` | Surface discovered skills as their own slash commands |
| `steering_mode` | `steeringMode` | `Option<DeliveryMode>` | `DeliveryMode::All` | How queued steering corrections release back into the run |
| `follow_up_mode` | `followUpMode` | `Option<DeliveryMode>` | `DeliveryMode::All` | How queued follow-up prompts release back into the run |
| `collapse_changelog` | `collapseChangelog` | `Option<bool>` | `false` | Prefer a condensed changelog after a console self-update |
| `show_hardware_cursor` | `showHardwareCursor` | `Option<bool>` | `false` | Reveal the terminal's own cursor vs the software caret |
| `editor_padding_x` | `editorPaddingX` | `Option<i64>` | `1` | Horizontal padding (columns) around the prompt editor |
| `enabled_models` | `enabledModels` | `Option<Vec<String>>` | `[]` | Glob/id patterns selecting which models appear in the picker; empty = all |
| `default_provider` | `defaultProvider` | `Option<String>` | `"anthropic"` | Provider id the session defaults to when none is named |
| `default_model` | `defaultModel` | `Option<String>` | `""` | Model id the session opens with under `default_provider` |
| `default_thinking_level` | `defaultThinkingLevel` | `Option<ThinkingLevel>` | `ThinkingLevel::Medium` | Reasoning effort the session requests by default |
| `quiet_startup` | `quietStartup` | `Option<bool>` | `false` | Suppress the banner/tips on a normal interactive launch |
| `last_seen_version` | `lastSeenVersion` | `Option<String>` | `""` | Last product version whose full masthead was seen |
| `logo_sweep` | `logoSweep` | `Option<bool>` | `false` | Opt-in static colour-sweep flourish on the startup wordmark |
| `reduced_motion` | `reducedMotion` | `Option<bool>` | `false` | Suppress motion-flavoured flourishes |
| `auto_compact` | `autoCompact` | `Option<bool>` | `true` | Whether the window-budget manager compacts the transcript automatically |
| `double_escape_action` | `doubleEscapeAction` | `Option<EscapeAction>` | `EscapeAction::Clear` | What a double-tap of the escape key does |
| `extension_packages` | `extensionPackages` | `Option<Vec<String>>` | `[]` | Extension-package sources the launcher installs and loads |
| `permissions` | `permissions` | `Option<PermissionSettings>` | empty allow-all policy | The declarative tool-permission policy (below) |

`last_seen_version` auto-condenses the startup banner once it equals the running version (`env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`, via `workspace::VERSION`). The frozen `SETTING_KEYS` slice is the iteration/validation surface — the same 24 camelCase spellings in declaration order; a unit test asserts serializing `default_preferences()` emits exactly these keys, none skipped.

**Narrow vocabularies** — three small enums pin certain values, each with `as_str()`, `parse()`, a canonical menu slice, and (two of them) legacy-alias folding:

`EscapeAction` (`#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]`): `Tree`(`"tree"`, navigable branch tree), `Fork`(`"fork"`, prior-turn picker), `Clear`(`"clear"`, wipe composer — default), `Rewind`(`"rewind"`, legacy → folds to `Fork`), `Branch`(`"branch"`, legacy → folds to `Tree`). `ESCAPE_ACTIONS` menu = `&[Tree, Fork, Clear]`; aliases accepted on read, round-trip byte-for-byte, never offered.

`DeliveryMode` (`#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]`): `All`(`"all"`, release every queued turn at once), `OneAtATime`(`"one-at-a-time"`, one per handoff). `DELIVERY_MODES` = `&[All, OneAtATime]`; used by both `steering_mode` and `follow_up_mode`.

`ThinkingLevel` — `default_thinking_level` is typed by `indusagi::llmgateway::contract::ThinkingLevel`, re-exported from the framework rather than re-declared; default `Medium`.

**The permission policy** (`permissions`, the 24th key) is additive and backward-compatible — no `permissions` block ⇒ empty allow-all baseline `{ allow: [], ask: [], deny: [], defaultMode: "default" }`:

```rust
pub struct PermissionSettings {
    pub allow: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub ask: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub deny: Option<Vec<String>>,
    #[serde(rename = "defaultMode")] pub default_mode: Option<PermissionMode>,
}
```

| Field | JSON | Meaning |
|-------|------|---------|
| `allow` | `allow` | Rules auto-allowing a matching call (lowest precedence) |
| `ask` | `ask` | Rules forcing a prompt for approval |
| `deny` | `deny` | Rules hard-blocking a call (highest precedence) |
| `default_mode` | `defaultMode` | The `PermissionMode` the session opens in when no flag overrides |

Across tiers the rule lists are concatenated and resolved `deny > ask > allow`; the raw-tier accessors `global_defaults()` / `project_overrides()` expose each tier's `permissions` separately for cross-tier concat.

`PermissionMode`: `Default`(`"default"`, consult rules, read-only tools auto-allow — default), `AcceptEdits`(`"acceptEdits"`, also auto-allow fs edits/writes), `Bypass`(`"bypass"`, allow every tool, the unsafe "trust all"), `Plan`(`"plan"`, deny every mutating tool, read-only research), `BypassPermissions`(`"bypassPermissions"`, legacy → folds to `Bypass`). `PERMISSION_MODES` menu = `&[Default, AcceptEdits, Bypass, Plan]`.

**Store API.** Construct via `at_paths` (pin both files, tests) or `from_workspace` (runtime). Key methods: `paths()`, `reload()` (re-read both tiers, drop staged change), `resolved()`/`snapshot()` (fully-resolved record), `project_overrides()`/`global_defaults()` (raw tiers), `stage(|p| …)` (mutate the in-memory **project** tier in a closure — set `Some(..)` to override, `None` to clear; no disk touch), `save()` (persist staged project tier as pretty JSON; global never rewritten). `PreferenceLocations { global, project }` is the resolved absolute-path pair. The Rust writer is a **typed closure-based `stage`** rather than a `set(key, value)` string API, so a typo is a compile error, not a runtime `KeyError`.

**On-disk format & tolerant loading.** Saved files are plain pretty JSON keyed by camelCase wire names (e.g. `{"colourScheme": "midnight", "showReasoning": false, "editorPaddingX": 2, "enabledModels": ["claude-*", "gpt-4o"]}`), with a trailing newline; `write_tier` runs `create_dir_all` first. `load_tier` degrades to `Preferences::default()` (the **empty** record, not `default_preferences()`) on every failure — the four degradation paths being a missing/unreadable file, unparseable JSON, a non-object JSON value, or a failed parse into `Preferences`. Unknown keys are tolerated and dropped (no `deny_unknown_fields`); a JSON `null` deserializes to `None`.

```rust
use induscode::core::settings::PreferenceStore;
use induscode::core::workspace::{create_workspace, WorkspaceOverrides};

let ws = create_workspace(WorkspaceOverrides::default());     // ~/.indusagi/agent
let mut store = PreferenceStore::from_workspace(&ws, Path::new("."));
store.stage(|p| {
    p.colour_scheme = Some("midnight".to_string());
    p.editor_padding_x = Some(2);
    p.enabled_models = Some(vec!["claude-*".to_string()]);
});
store.save()?;   // writes ./.indusagi/settings.json only; global untouched

store.stage(|p| p.show_reasoning = None);          // clear → falls back to default true
assert_eq!(store.snapshot().show_reasoning, Some(true));
```

#### Auth & sign-in

A run needs exactly one thing: a usable api-key string for the provider backing the model. Three ways to supply it, in increasing persistence: (1) an **environment variable** (nothing stored), (2) **`indus signin` with an api key** (validated, written to the vault under a named account), (3) **`indus signin` with browser sign-in / OAuth** (paste-based PKCE, or a device grant for GitHub Copilot). The command + 14-provider directory live in `induscode::launch::credentials`; the OAuth registry + three browser flows in `induscode::launch::oauth`; the disk vault `DiskAuthVault` writes `auth.json` under `~/.indusagi/agent/`.

The crate's two bins (`indusr`/`indusagir`) share one `async fn main() -> ExitCode` in `src/bin/main.rs`. The user-facing name (`resolve_brand`, from `BIN_NAMES`) is `indus`/`indusagi`, matched against `argv[0]` basename; anything else falls back to `BIN_NAMES[0]` = `indus`. `signin`/`signout` are **no-session** verbs `route` short-circuits via `is_credential_verb` before the boot handoff. `run_credential_command(argv, &dyn AuthVault, &dyn CredentialIo, &dyn OAuthSeam) -> CredentialResult { handled, verb, provider, fault }` returns `handled: false` when the leading token is not a credential verb, so a normal prompt falls through.

**Environment variables** (the fastest path — set it and the provider is authenticated for the process, no `signin`). The api-key `signin` flow consults the env var first via `env_api_key` and offers to store an already-exported value:

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."
indus -p "explain this repo"
```

| Provider | `id` | Environment variable |
|----------|------|----------------------|
| Anthropic (Claude) | `anthropic` | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| OpenAI | `openai` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| Google Gemini | `google` | `GEMINI_API_KEY` |
| xAI (Grok) | `xai` | `XAI_API_KEY` |
| Groq | `groq` | `GROQ_API_KEY` |
| Cerebras | `cerebras` | `CEREBRAS_API_KEY` |
| Mistral | `mistral` | `MISTRAL_API_KEY` |
| OpenRouter | `openrouter` | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| MiniMax | `minimax` | `MINIMAX_API_KEY` |
| Kimi (Moonshot) | `kimi` | `MOONSHOT_API_KEY` |
| Sarvam | `sarvam` | `SARVAM_API_KEY` |
| Krutrim | `krutrim` | `KRUTRIM_API_KEY` |
| NVIDIA | `nvidia` | `NVIDIA_API_KEY` |
| Z.ai | `zai` | `ZAI_API_KEY` |

This 14-provider `PROVIDER_DIRECTORY` is the api-key directory; each `ProviderEntry` carries `id`, `label`, `env_key`, `docs_url`. `find_provider(id)` is a case-insensitive lookup. `list_login_providers` merges the api-key directory with the OAuth registry into the menu `signin` shows (browser-sign-in providers first; a provider in both halves is listed twice).

**`indus signin`** resolves a provider then runs browser sign-in or stores an api key. Naming a provider is optional (omit it ⇒ print the merged directory and pick by number). `as_verb` accepts `login`/`logout` as natural-language aliases of `signin`/`signout`.

```bash
indus signin                                       # interactive: pick from the menu
indus signin anthropic                             # provider as a bare positional
indus signin --provider openai --method api-key
indus signin --provider anthropic --account work   # name the stored account
indus login anthropic                              # `login` is an alias
```

Verb-tail flags (parsed by `read_verb_flags`):

| Flag | Effect |
|------|--------|
| `--provider <id>` | Provider to sign in to (also a bare positional) |
| `--account <name>` | Account label (default: `default`) |
| `--method oauth` / `--oauth` | Force browser sign-in |
| `--method api-key` / `--api-key` / `--apikey` | Force api-key entry |
| `--list` / `--ls` | List stored accounts read-only |

When a provider supports browser sign-in and no method is requested, the browser path is preferred (`use_oauth = method == Some(Oauth) || (method.is_none() && target.oauth_capable)`); an explicit `--method` always wins. **Default-to-api-key:** because shipped OAuth client ids are unconfigured sentinels, the CLI's `default_signin_to_api_key` appends `--method api-key` to a `signin` argv only when no method is named (`argv_picks_method` checks `--method`/`--oauth`/`--api-key`/`--apikey`); `--oauth`/`--method oauth` are preserved.

**Validation** runs before any write. A key must be non-empty, ≥ 20 chars (`MIN_KEY_LENGTH`), and free of `PLACEHOLDER_MARKERS` (`"your-api-key"`, `"your_api_key"`, `"xxxx"`, `"placeholder"`, `"changeme"`, `"<"`). An account name must be non-empty, ≤ 50 chars (`MAX_ACCOUNT_LENGTH`), and match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`. The first account stored for a provider becomes its default; a duplicate name is a `NameCollision` fault.

**`indus signin --list`** (alias `--ls`) is a read-only switch: `do_list_accounts` walks the merged directory (de-duplicating), queries the vault per provider, and prints one line per stored account — tagging the provider default and whether it is `[browser]` (OAuth), `[api key]`, or `[unknown]`. No provider with a saved account ⇒ a single `(none)` line.

```
Saved accounts:
  Anthropic (Claude) (anthropic):
    - default (default) [browser]
  OpenAI (openai):
    - work [api key]
```

**`indus signout`** (alias `logout`) removes credentials. Name `--account` to remove one, or omit it to remove all for the provider. Removing nothing is a `NotFound` fault. When the removed account was the default and survivors remain, the first survivor is promoted (`DiskAuthVault::remove`); when the last account goes, the provider key is dropped from the file.

```bash
indus signout --provider anthropic --account work   # remove one account
indus signout --provider anthropic                  # remove all anthropic credentials
indus logout openai                                 # `logout` is an alias
```

**`auth` subcommand** (intercepted in `route` before the global `--help`/`--version` short-circuit so `auth --help` reaches auth help). `classify_auth_verb` dispatches:

| Sub-verb | Route | What runs |
|----------|-------|-----------|
| `auth status [provider]` | `AgentStatus` | The agent's own vault reader (`run_agent_status`) |
| `auth logout [...]` | `AgentLogout` | The agent's `signout` over `auth.json` (`run_agent_logout`) |
| `auth login` / `refresh` / `help` / unknown | `Framework` | The framework `run_auth_command` (`indusagi::shell_app::auth_cli`) |

`auth status` exists for a reconciliation gap: the framework reader understands only the top-level single-record `{ provider: StoredCredential }` shape and folds the agent's nested multi-account vault to empty. The agent-owned `DiskAuthVault::status_entries` reads BOTH shapes:

```rust
pub struct AuthStatusEntry {
    pub provider: String,
    pub account: String,
    pub kind: AuthKind,        // ApiKey | Oauth
    pub is_default: bool,
    pub refreshable: bool,     // true only for an OAuth record with a refresh token
    pub freshness: String,     // "no expiry recorded" | "expired" | "valid for ~N min"
}
```

OAuth freshness wording follows the framework: `no expiry recorded` / `expired` / `valid for ~N min` (rounded to nearest minute, `+30_000` ms before the `/60_000` divide). `auth login <provider>` prints `Tip: to log in with an API key instead, run: indus signin <provider>` before handing off (default-build OAuth ids are sentinels).

**Browser sign-in (OAuth / PKCE)** lives in `induscode::launch::oauth` (behind the `oauth` cargo feature). The framework ships only the transport primitives (`indusagi::llmgateway::{create_pkce_pair, build_auth_url, exchange_code, refresh_token}`), so the agent owns the `OAuthProvider` trait, the `OAuthCredentials` shape, the process-global `OAuthProviderRegistry` (`OnceLock`-backed `RwLock<IndexMap>`), the idempotent boot-time `register_built_in_oauth_providers`, and the three flows: **Anthropic** (`anthropic`), **OpenAI Codex** (`openai-codex`), **GitHub Copilot** (`github-copilot`).

There is **no local callback HTTP server**. The shared `paste_code_login` choreography: (1) resolve the real client id from a per-provider env var or refuse (`resolve_client_id`); (2) mint a PKCE pair (`create_pkce_pair(64)`, `S256`) + fresh CSRF `state`; (3) `build_auth_url` and `open_login_url` (accepts only `http`/`https`); (4) read the pasted code — a bare code, `code#state`, or the whole redirect URL — via `extract_code`; (5) `exchange_code` and persist through the vault. `start_oauth_login(provider_id, &dyn OAuthLoginCallbacks, &dyn OAuthVaultSink, account)` looks up the provider, applies the sentinel gate up front, runs `provider.login`, and stores under `account` (first becomes default).

**Client-id sentinel gate** — no real client ids ship; each provider has a parity-locked env var read **live** and an `<UNREGISTERED-…>` sentinel; a provider with no known wiring is treated as registered (only the three are gated):

| Provider | Env var | Sentinel |
|----------|---------|----------|
| `anthropic` | `INDUSAGI_ANTHROPIC_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` | `<UNREGISTERED-ANTHROPIC-OAUTH-APP>` |
| `openai-codex` | `INDUSAGI_OPENAI_CODEX_CLIENT_ID` | `<UNREGISTERED-OPENAI-CODEX-APP>` |
| `github-copilot` | `INDUSAGI_GITHUB_COPILOT_CLIENT_ID` | `<UNREGISTERED-COPILOT-APP>` |

`oauth_client_id_env_var(provider_id)` and `has_registered_oauth_client_id(provider_id)` are the predicates. **GitHub Copilot** uses the OAuth device-authorization grant (RFC 8628): the user enters a code at a verification URL while the driver polls. The pure, unit-tested poll FSM is `PollStatus { Authorized, Pending, SlowDown, Denied, Expired }` via `classify_poll`, and `plan_poll(status, base_interval_ms) -> PollDecision { Done | Poll{wait_ms, slowed} | Expired | Failed{reason} }`; `slow_down` bumps the interval by 5s (RFC 8628 §3.5), unknown error codes are terminal failures. `open_login_url` refuses non-`http(s)` schemes, then tries platform launchers in order — `open` (macOS), `cmd /c start` (Windows), `xdg-open`/`x-www-browser`/`google-chrome`/`chromium` (Linux).

**The disk vault.** The `AuthVault` trait (object-safe + `async`) exposes `list_accounts`, `default_account`, `put_api_key`, `put_oauth`, `auth_kind`, `read_usable_key`, `remove`. The concrete `DiskAuthVault::new(path)` is keyed provider → account → record; each `AuthRecord` is a `"kind"`-tagged enum:

```rust
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "camelCase")]
enum AuthRecord {
    ApiKey { key: SecretString, #[serde(rename = "isDefault")] is_default: bool },
    Oauth  { #[serde(flatten)] credentials: OAuthCredentials,
             #[serde(rename = "isDefault")] is_default: bool },
}
```

The OAuth record flattens `OAuthCredentials` (`access`/`refresh`/`expires`/`issuedAt`/`provider`, camelCase). The file is `IndexMap`-ordered (stable bytes), pretty JSON + trailing newline, `0o600` on Unix. The vault reads the whole file each call and tolerates three shapes: the agent's nested `{ provider: { account: record } }`; the legacy pre-discriminant `{ apiKey, isDefault }` (coerced by `normalise_record`); a framework single-record `{ provider: StoredCredential }` (`accessToken`/`refreshToken`/`expiresAt`/`updatedAt`, upgraded to one `default` OAuth account by `upgrade_framework_record`). A missing/malformed file reads empty. `read_usable_key` returns an api key verbatim; for OAuth the bare disk vault returns the stored access token, while the console wiring supplies a refreshing variant that exchanges an expired token via the registry. A default install stores at `~/.indusagi/agent/auth.json`.

**Secret redaction.** Every bearer secret is wrapped in `SecretString` (`#[serde(transparent)]`), whose `Debug`/`Display` redact the value (`{:?}` → `SecretString("<redacted>")`, `{}` → `<redacted>`); cleartext is reachable only via `SecretString::expose`. `OAuthCredentials` has a custom `Debug` printing `<redacted>` for its `access`/`refresh`. On a TTY the api-key prompt mutes echo via crossterm raw mode (`read_secret_raw`); a piped stdin falls through to a plain line read (scriptable).

**Typed faults** — every failure is a `CredentialFault` (never a string sentinel or `process::exit`); `format_credential_fault(&fault)` renders the human-facing message. The seven kinds (`CredentialFaultKind`):

| Kind | `label()` | Meaning |
|------|-----------|---------|
| `UnknownProvider` | Unknown provider | Provider not in directory/registry |
| `InvalidKey` | Invalid api key | Key empty, too short, or a placeholder |
| `InvalidAccount` | Invalid account name | Account name empty, too long, or malformed |
| `NameCollision` | Account already exists | Account by that name already exists |
| `NotFound` | Nothing to remove | `signout` found nothing |
| `Vault` | Credential store error | Credential store / browser sign-in failed |
| `Aborted` | Cancelled | The interactive provider pick was cancelled |

A vault I/O failure is a separate `VaultError(String)` folded into a `Vault` fault (`to_vault_fault`); `run_agent_credential` maps `result.fault` to `ExitCode::FAILURE` after printing to stderr.

**Console overlays** route credential management onto the framework `LoginDialog`/`OAuthDialog`: `signin.rs` (`ModalKind::SignIn`, merged-directory picker; `resolve_direct_route` skips the picker for `/login <provider>`), `signout.rs` (`ModalKind::SignOut`, accounts pre-fetched since `handle_key` cannot `await`), `oauth.rs` (`ModalKind::Oauth`, in-flight entry overlay). Because `Dialog::handle_key` is synchronous, the live OAuth flow runs on a spawned task reporting over a `tokio::sync::mpsc` channel (`OverlayCallbacks` implements `OAuthLoginCallbacks`, sending `OAuthProgress` events folded in via `apply_progress`; a manual-code prompt parks a `oneshot::Sender<String>`). The whole flow is `async` with injectable I/O (`CredentialIo`, `OAuthSeam`, `AuthVault`).

#### Models

The Rust edition selects a run's model from the framework's own registry surfaced through the `indusagi/ai` facade — **708 models across 24 providers** (the `mock` echo provider filtered out) — read by the printer, picker, and resolver alike, so there is one catalog path. Pick with `--model`/`-m`, browse with `--list-models`, switch with `/model`, or scope a subset with `/models-for`.

**Selecting a model.** `--model` (short `-m`) takes a catalog identifier in canonical `provider/modelId` or bare provider-scoped form — both resolve to the same card (`claude-sonnet-4-5` ≡ `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5`):

```bash
indusr -m anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 -p "summarize this repo"
indusr -m claude-sonnet-4-5 "refactor the auth module"   # bare model id
indusr --list-models                                     # browse the catalog
indusr --list-models claude                              # filter by substring
```

**The five `FlagGroup::Model` flags** (`launch::flags::flag_specs()`, `describe` verbatim):

| Flag | Aliases | Kind | Purpose |
|------|---------|------|---------|
| `--model` | `-m` | String | Select the model, provider-qualified or bare (e.g. `provider/name`). |
| `--fallback-model` | — | String | Model to switch to mid-turn when the selected model is overloaded (HTTP 529). |
| `--account` | — | String | Authenticate the run with a named stored credential account. |
| `--thinking` | — | String | Set the reasoning effort (one of: `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`). |
| `--list-models` | — | String | List the available models (optionally filtered by a substring) and exit. |

**Listing the catalog.** `--list-models` is a leading verb `route()` short-circuits in `main.rs` before boot; it prints an aligned table and exits, taking an optional case-insensitive substring (the `search` field of a `CatalogFilter`). Entry point `print_model_catalog(io: &mut dyn CatalogIo, filter: &CatalogFilter, source: &dyn CatalogModelSource)` pulls every row, filters, sorts by provider then id, and writes via `io`. The six columns (`HEADERS`):

| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| Provider | Owning provider slug (kebab-case serde spelling, e.g. `google-vertex`) |
| Model | Provider-scoped (bare) model id |
| Context | Context-window — `128K` / `1.0M` / `-` when unknown (`format_token_count`) |
| Max Output | Max output tokens, same compact format |
| Thinking | `yes` when the model advertises a reasoning budget |
| Images | `yes` when the model accepts image input |

`format_token_count`: `0` → `-`, ≥ 1,000,000 → `1M`/`1.5M`, ≥ 1,000 → rounded `128K`, else the bare number. A non-matching filter prints `No models match the given filter.`. The sink is the `CatalogIo` trait (`StdoutCatalogIo` via `println!`; `VecCatalogIo` buffers for tests).

**`CatalogFilter`** (every field optional, absent = matches all): `provider: Option<String>` (case-insensitive exact equality), `thinking_only: bool`, `images_only: bool`, `search: Option<String>` (trimmed/lowercased substring over the synthesized `"provider/modelId"` haystack — no fuzzy matcher). From the CLI only `search` is reachable; programmatic callers can build the rest.

**How the catalog is surfaced** — through the `CatalogModelSource` trait (`fn rows() -> Vec<CatalogRow>`):

| Source | Backed by | Used by |
|--------|-----------|---------|
| `RegistrySource` | live `indusagi/ai` facade catalog (`get_providers()` × `get_models(provider)`), `mock` filtered out | production `--list-models` |
| `SliceSource` | an injected `Vec<ModelCard>` projected via `to_row` | tests |

`RegistrySource::rows()` walks the **facade** catalog from `indusagi::facade::ai`, skipping `EXCLUDED_PROVIDERS` (`&["mock"]`), projecting each facade `Model` to a `CatalogRow` (`provider`, `model_id`, `context_window`, `max_output`, `thinking`, `images`) via `facade_model_to_row`. This is the same 708-model/24-provider matrix the `/model` picker reads (not the gateway's smaller routing-card set), so listing and picker always agree. An injected `ModelCard` renders its provider via the serde kebab-case `provider_label` (`ProviderId::GoogleVertex` → `google-vertex`), `thinking` mirrors `reasoning`, `images` is `modalities.contains(&Modality::Image)`.

**Resolving the effective model id** — `resolve_model_id(invocation_model, saved_model, authed: &HashSet<String>) -> String` mirrors the merged framework+product precedence. Four tiers:

1. **Explicit `--model`** (`invocation_model`) — a non-empty selector naming a real catalog model wins outright.
2. **Saved `settings.default_model`** — only when `saved_model_usable` is true: the id must name a real model **and** its owning provider must be in `authed`. A stale saved id from an unauthenticated provider is skipped.
3. **An authenticated provider's current model** — `provider_default_model` consults the `PREFERRED_DEFAULT` table (since a provider's catalog often leads with a deprecated model), falling back to the provider's newest catalog entry:

   | Provider | Preferred default ids, in priority order |
   |----------|------------------------------------------|
   | `anthropic` | `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `claude-haiku-4-5`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-sonnet-4-0`, `claude-opus-4-5` |
   | `openai` | `gpt-5.1`, `gpt-4.1`, `gpt-4o` |
   | `minimax` | `MiniMax-M2`, `MiniMax-M2.7` |

4. **`FALLBACK_MODEL_ID`** — the catalog-guaranteed last resort from `indusagi::shell_app::config`, hardened to `CAPABLE_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID` (`"claude-sonnet-4"`, a large-window Anthropic model) should the framework fallback name no backing card — so a bare `indusr` with no key never lands on a tiny/zero-window card.

"A real catalog model" is tested by `model_known` (accepts the facade catalog via `facade_knows`, or a gateway routing card via `get_card`); the owning provider is resolved by `model_provider`.

**The `/model` picker** (`ModalKind::Models`, `console::overlays::models`) paints the frozen framework `ModelDialog` as a full-screen modal. The module is the render half; the host pushes the dialog and binds via `select_model`. Pure projections: `catalog()` (full facade catalog as `ModelOption` rows — `mock` excluded, de-duped by canonical `provider/modelId` first-wins, sorted by provider then id), `catalog_for(authed)` (restricted to authenticated providers, empty→all fallback), `provider_for(model_id)`, `bound_index(models, bound)` (matches a bound id bare or canonical, seeds the cursor), `is_active(state)`. `model_to_option` keeps `id` **bare**; the frozen `ModelDialog` reconstructs the canonical label, so no double-prefixing. Reads the same facade catalog as `--list-models`.

**Authentication filtering** — `authenticated_providers(auth_path: &Path) -> HashSet<String>` unions two sources: the **vault half** (reads `auth.json`'s nested map, returns every top-level key with ≥ 1 saved account; a broken file degrades to empty) and the **env half** (every `PROVIDER_DIRECTORY` provider whose api-key env var is set, e.g. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` → `anthropic`, `MOONSHOT_API_KEY` → `kimi`; directory ids already match facade spelling). `catalog_for(Some(&set))` filters via `auth_filter(models, authed)`; `None`/empty returns the whole catalog, and a secondary fallback shows the full catalog if filtering removed everything — so the picker is never empty. This is the TS `useAuthenticatedProviders` filter ported as a pure host-side projection.

**The `/models-for` scoped picker** (`ModalKind::ScopedModels`, `console::overlays::scoped_models`, over the frozen `ScopedModelsDialog`) edits the `enabledModels` preference as a checkbox list narrowing which catalog models a scope may use. Pure projections: `seed_selection(models, enabled)` (an **empty** override means every model is enabled, so seed every id; otherwise the stored ids), `collapse_selection(all_ids, selected)` (a **full** selection collapses to `[]` = every model enabled; a partial selection stored verbatim), `is_active(state)`. The picker tracks a `cursor` separately from `selected_ids`; the host wires `ResetScopedModels`/`SaveScopedModels` effects.

**Reasoning effort** — `--thinking` (and the `/thinking` command) set the rung from the closed `THINKING_EFFORTS` set (the `ThinkingEffort` enum: `Off`, `Minimal`, `Low`, `Medium`, `High`, `XHigh`, lower-cased by `as_str()`); the `--thinking` `describe` string is generated from it at runtime (`thinking_describe()`) so banner and validator never drift:

```
off  minimal  low  medium  high  xhigh
```

`off` disables extended reasoning; the rest ascend (`xhigh` highest). Validation is the pure membership test `is_thinking_effort` / `ThinkingEffort::parse`, applied before the run.

```bash
indusr -m claude-sonnet-4-5 --thinking high "design the migration"
indusr -m claude-sonnet-4-5 --thinking off  "just answer briefly"
```

Public API is exported from `induscode::launch::catalog` (`print_model_catalog`, `CatalogFilter`, `CatalogIo`/`StdoutCatalogIo`/`VecCatalogIo`, `CatalogModelSource`/`RegistrySource`/`SliceSource`, `CatalogRow`, `resolve_model_id`, `saved_model_usable`, `model_provider`) and `induscode::console::overlays` (`catalog`/`catalog_for`, `authenticated_providers`, `auth_filter`/`provider_for`/`bound_index`/`draw_models`, `seed_selection`/`collapse_selection`/`draw_scoped_models`, `is_active`).

#### MCP

External Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool servers are mounted into a session with the repeatable `--mcp` flag. Each ready endpoint's tools are connected through the framework protocol bridge, adapted into deck `Card`s, folded into an event-sourced enrollment ledger, and grafted onto the built-in capability deck — so the agent calls a remote `github__create_issue` exactly like the native `read` or `bash`. Lives in `induscode::deck::mcp`, gated on the `mcp` cargo feature (on by default; `mcp = ["indusagi/mcp"]`).

The protocol work is the framework's: the deck calls `indusagi::interop::mount_protocol_bridge`, which connects every configured server, lists each ready endpoint's tools, normalizes schemas, and returns one `indusagi::capabilities::ToolBox` whose `descriptors()` advertise every grafted tool under its qualified `"<server>__<tool>"` name and whose shared `runner` routes a call back across the owning endpoint. The framework speaks both transports: subprocess **stdio** (`command`/`args`) and **SSE** (`url`). `induscode::deck::mcp` is the side-effecting half: **Discovery** (`load_mcp_config`, `bridge_config`), **Adaptation** (`ledger::bridge_box_to_capabilities`), **Client-pool lifecycle** (`attach_bridge_capabilities`, `detach_bridge`, `bridge_status`/`bridge_tool_names`), **Cataloging** (`bridge_capability_card`), and the **Enrollment ledger** (`reduce_ledger`). It ports `indus-code-rebuild/src/capability-deck/bridge-ledger`.

**The `--mcp` flag** names where to find MCP config. It is one of two `FlagKind::List` flags (with `--tools`) in the 18-row flag table, so it both **repeats** and **comma-splits** — every endpoint attaches:

```bash
indusr --mcp .                              # auto-detected project/user config
indusr --mcp ./mcp.json                     # an explicit config file
indusr --mcp ./fs.json --mcp ./github.json  # several endpoints (repeated)
indusr --mcp ./fs.json,./github.json        # equivalent, comma-joined
```

```rust
// launch/flags.rs — the --mcp row (FlagGroup::Tools)
FlagSpec {
    name: "--mcp", aliases: &[], kind: FlagKind::List, group: FlagGroup::Tools,
    describe: "Attach an external MCP server endpoint (comma-separated or repeated).",
}
```

The parsed value lands as `Invocation.mcp: Option<Vec<String>>` (`core/boot_contract.rs:81`) — `None` when unset; the launch invocation carries `mcp: Vec<String>` (`launch/contract.rs:298`) and the boot pipeline collapses an empty list to `None` (`boot/pipeline.rs:183`).

**Config file format** — JSON with a top-level `servers`, which may be an **array** of server objects or an **object** keyed by server name (the key becomes the id). A server is **SSE** when it carries a `url`, **stdio** when it carries a `command` (one required); `"enabled": false` drops it.

```json
{
  "servers": [
    {
      "name": "github",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"],
      "env": { "GITHUB_TOKEN": "your-github-token" },
      "enabled": true
    },
    {
      "name": "remote",
      "url": "http://localhost:8080/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer your-token" },
      "enabled": false
    }
  ]
}
```

The object form is equivalent (map key supplies `name`):

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "fs": { "command": "node", "args": ["server.js"] },
    "remote": { "url": "http://localhost:8080/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer your-token" } }
  }
}
```

Each row is normalized by `parse_config_file` then discriminated by `server_config_from_row` into a framework `ServerConfig` — a `url` → `ServerConfig::Sse`, a `command` → `ServerConfig::Stdio`. (The framework reserves a forward-looking `StreamableHttp { id, url, headers }` variant for the SSE→Streamable-HTTP migration, but the deck only ever mints `Stdio` or `Sse`.)

| Field | Applies to | Maps to | Purpose |
|-------|-----------|---------|---------|
| `name` | both | `ServerConfig::*::id` | Server id; namespaces its tools. In the object form this is the map key. |
| `command` | stdio | `Stdio::command` | Executable to spawn (`npx`, `node`, `python`, …). |
| `args` | stdio | `Stdio::args` | Argument list; non-string elements dropped. |
| `env` | stdio | `Stdio::env` | Extra env vars, coerced to `IndexMap<String,String>` in declaration order. |
| `url` | SSE | `Sse::url` | Endpoint URL; the transport speaks SSE. |
| `headers` | SSE | `Sse::headers` | Headers on the connection (e.g. an auth bearer token). |
| `enabled` | both | (filter) | `false` skips the entry without removing it from the file. |

Order is preserved across the whole pipeline (`string_map` uses `IndexMap`). A row with an empty `name`, or one carrying neither `url` nor `command` (and not disabled), is **skipped** (not raised) — one bad entry must not discard the whole file. A file missing `servers`, whose `servers` is neither array nor object, or that is unreadable/malformed JSON, yields an empty list (`parse_config_file` degrades, never panics).

**Auto-detected config search** — `load_mcp_config(path_or_cwd: &str) -> Vec<ServerConfig>` (port of `loadMCPConfig`). If `path_or_cwd` is an existing **file**, it is parsed directly. Otherwise it is treated as a working directory and conventional locations are merged in precedence order:

1. **Project:** `<cwd>/.indusvx/mcp.json`
2. **User (XDG):** `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/indusvx/mcp.json` (default `~/.config/indusvx/mcp.json`)
3. **Legacy:** `~/.indusvx/agent/mcp.json`
4. **Legacy alt:** `~/.indusvx/agent/mcp-servers.json`

All present sources are concatenated (a project and a user `mcp.json` both contribute, declaration order preserved). The XDG root is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` falling back to `$HOME/.config`; the home dir comes from a dependency-free `home_dir()` reading `$HOME` (or `$USERPROFILE` on Windows). An explicit file path bypasses the search.

**The deck MCP bridge.** `attach_bridge_capabilities(ledger: BridgeLedger, config: BridgeConfig) -> AttachResult { ledger, fleet, status, enrolled, fault }` wraps the flat list with `bridge_config`, mounts it, adapts the `ToolBox`, and folds each capability into the ledger as an `enroll` event (returning a *new* ledger plus the live fleet). An empty config is a no-op. A decisive delta from the TS lineage: `mount_protocol_bridge` is **infallible** (returns `MountedProtocolBridge`, not a `Result`); there is no wholesale-mount fault branch — `AttachResult::fault` is reserved for config-validation, and per-server health is read from `fleet.status()`. `bridge_box_to_capabilities` turns each descriptor + the box's **shared** runner into one `BridgeCapability` (an `Arc`-shared newtype implementing the deck `Card` trait); its `run` projects the opaque `ToolOutcome` via `project_outcome` (a `Value::String` preserved verbatim, structured values pretty-printed, `Value::Null` → empty, `is_error` rides through). `server_of_qualified(name)` recovers the owner by splitting on the first `QUALIFIER` (`"__"`), returning `""` when unqualified or leading with the separator (`sep > 0` guard). `detach_bridge(ledger, fleet, servers: Option<&[String]>)` retires entries and tears the fleet down (`None` ⇒ every server); teardown is best-effort and infallible.

**The event-sourced ledger** — enrollment is an append-only event log folded into a derived snapshot by one pure reducer (the log is truth; the snapshot is a cache):

```rust
pub struct BridgeLedger {
    pub log: Vec<BridgeEntry>,    // append-only event log, in append order
    pub snapshot: LedgerSnapshot, // = reduce_ledger(&log), cached
    pub next_seq: u64,            // seq the next appended entry carries
}
```

Every transition returns a *new* ledger (cheap `Clone` — `Arc`-shared caps + a `Vec`): `empty()` (seq numbering at 1), `from_log(log)` (rehydrate, resume seq past the high-water mark), `enroll(EnrollRequest, at)` (an **upsert** on the key), `retire(key, server, at)` (a **splice**), `withdraw_server(server, at)` (retire all of one server's live caps in a batch), `live_capabilities()` (flat `Vec` in stable order — what the deck grafts), `live_capabilities_for_server(server)`.

```rust
pub enum BridgeOp { Enroll, Retire }   // closed set — exhaustive match, no `_` arm
pub struct BridgeEntry {
    pub op: BridgeOp, pub key: BridgeKey, pub server: String,
    pub capability: Option<BridgeCapability>, // Some on Enroll, None on Retire
    pub seq: u64, pub at: String,             // monotonic seq; ISO-8601 audit timestamp
}
pub struct LedgerSnapshot {
    pub live: IndexMap<BridgeKey, BridgeCapability>, // current live caps, insertion order
    pub by_server: IndexMap<String, usize>,          // live tool count per server
    pub high_water: u64,                             // highest folded seq
}
```

`reduce_ledger(&[BridgeEntry]) -> LedgerSnapshot` is the single sanctioned fold — pure, total, and slice-order-independent (it sorts a borrowed index by `seq`, so a later `seq` wins on a repeated key). `IndexMap` keeps insertion order so `live_capabilities()` is stable; `shift_remove` (not `swap_remove`) on a retire matches JS `Map.delete`. Because the snapshot is a pure function of the committed log, `from_log` replays a byte-for-byte identical deck. The `at` timestamp is minted by `iso_now()` (`iso_from_ms` over `indusagi::core::time::now_ms`), an ISO-8601 UTC string the ledger only logs.

**Bridge keys.** Each capability is keyed by `BridgeKey` (a newtype over `String`). Two minters: `bridge_content_key(server, tool, parameters)` (content-addressed — `bk_` + `content_hash` (sha256-over-canonical-json, truncated to 32 hex) of a `sort_keys`-canonicalized `{name, schema}` identity, so a schema differing only in key order yields the same key; arrays keep order) and `bridge_ulid_key()` (a fresh, time-sortable ULID, process-wide monotonic via a `static Mutex<Option<Generator>>`). The boot path uses `EnrollRequest { key: None, … }`, so the ledger derives a **content key** — enrolling the same tool twice is idempotent (the upsert dedups), a changed schema yields a new key. `qualify_bridge_name(server, tool) -> "<server>__<tool>"` builds the qualified name; `unqualified_tool` is its inverse.

**How tools attach at boot** — at session-conductor assembly in `induscode::boot::runners::build_session_tools_with_addons`. The built-in deck is provisioned first, `--tools` is applied to *it*, then MCP tools graft on (TS `[...selectTools(...), ...mcpTools]`):

```rust
let deck = provision_deck(Profile::All, ctx).ok()?;
let deck = /* honour --tools allow-list on the BUILT-IN deck only */;
let deck = deck.graft(load_mcp_capabilities(inv, cwd).await);   // ← MCP tools concat
```

`load_mcp_capabilities` resolves endpoints (explicit `--mcp` paths win; with **none given**, the cwd is auto-discovered so `.indusvx/mcp.json` servers are present from turn 1 with no `/mcp connect`), connects each, and returns live capabilities. The grafted fleet from the boot path is intentionally **not retained** (teardown rides process exit). The combined deck folds in addon tools (de-duped) + the interceptor chain; `into_tool_box()` produces the runtime `ToolBox` the conductor consumes. The briefing is composed *after* attachment, so the system prompt already documents the MCP tools.

**Failure isolation** — `--mcp` is best-effort and never sinks a session: a server faulting on connect contributes no descriptors and is simply absent (the framework fleet connects in parallel and skips per-endpoint `list_tools` faults; `mount_protocol_bridge` is infallible); a config with zero usable servers is `continue`d over; a malformed/unreadable file yields an empty `Vec` and one bad row is skipped while the rest loads; `--no-tools` short-circuits `build_session_tools_with_addons` (returns `None`) so the run is prompt-only with no MCP attempt. Per-server health, when a fleet is retained, is `bridge_status(fleet) -> FleetStatus`; `bridge_tool_names`/`bridge_tool_counts` read the ledger snapshot without a live fleet.

**Tool naming and filtering** — `--tools` filters the **built-in deck only**, *before* the MCP graft (names matched case-insensitively with `_`/`-` stripped via `canon_tool_name`, so `web_fetch`/`webfetch`/`web-fetch` resolve identically; an empty list = no filter). MCP tools graft *after* this selection, so they remain available. `--no-tools` disables every built-in tool and skips the deck/MCP path entirely. Remote tool names are always the qualified `"<server>__<tool>"` form the framework `QUALIFIER` stamps (e.g. `github__create_issue`), unique across servers and doubling as the model-facing label.

```bash
indusr --tools read,bash --mcp ./mcp.json   # restrict built-ins; MCP tools still attach
indusr --no-tools -p "just talk"            # prompt-only: no built-ins AND no MCP attachment
```


### Reference — CLI, crate exports, parity & testing

This reference covers the Rust edition of `induscode` (the coding agent, docs area `/rust-cli`, invoked as `indus` / `indusagi`): the complete command line, the public crate surface, the parity/lineage story against the TypeScript and Python editions, and the test approach.

#### CLI reference (`indus` / `indusagi`)

**Synopsis**

```bash
indusagi [options] [prompt] [@file ...]
```

A bare command line opens the interactive [console](/rust-cli/console/overview). A leading non-flag `prompt` positional becomes the first user message; later positionals accumulate as the tail.

```bash
indus                                       # interactive console (default)
indus "refactor the auth module"            # interactive, prompt pre-filled
indus -p "summarize this repo"              # one-shot print, then exit
indus -i "start here"                       # force interactive even with a prompt
indus -m anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 --thinking high "review this diff"
```

**Crate, bin targets, and brand names.** The crate is `induscode` (the `indusagi-coding-agent` package) and it ships **two `[[bin]]` targets** in `Cargo.toml`, named `indusr` (primary) and `indusagir`, both compiled from the single `crates/induscode/src/bin/main.rs`. Those cargo target names are distinct from the two **brand / invocation names** users type — `indus` (primary) and `indusagi` — which come from `BIN_NAMES` (`["indus", "indusagi"]`, from `induscode::core::BRAND.bin_names`). The generated `--help` synopsis is rendered with `indusagi::core::BRAND.bin_name` (`"indusagi"`), so the usage banner always reads `Usage: indusagi …` regardless of the alias invoked.

Everything runs through `async fn main() -> ExitCode`, the only place an exit code reaches the OS. Returning `ExitCode` (rather than `process::exit`) lets the tokio runtime drain so the terminal's raw / alt-screen mode is restored on the way out.

**Process branding.** `main` reads `argv[0]`'s basename via `resolve_brand`, matches it against `BIN_NAMES`, and falls back to the primary `BIN_NAMES[0]` (`"indus"`) when argv[0] is missing or is some other path (renamed symlink, test harness). A trailing `.exe` is stripped so a Windows launch still brands.

```rust
fn resolve_brand(argv0: Option<&str>) -> &'static str {
    let basename = argv0
        .map(|p| p.rsplit(['/', '\\']).next().unwrap_or(p).trim_end_matches(".exe"))
        .unwrap_or("");
    BIN_NAMES.iter().copied().find(|&name| name == basename).unwrap_or(BIN_NAMES[0])
}
```

`main` also installs a single idempotent `[MCP]` console-noise filter (`install_mcp_noise_filter`), a no-op when the brand debug env var (`INDUSAGI_DEBUG`, from `indusagi::core::env_name("debug")`) is set. The marker is `const MCP_NOISE_MARKER: &str = "[MCP]"`. An off-by-default `mimalloc` feature can swap in a drop-in global allocator; the default build runs allocator-neutral.

**The 18-flag table.** Every option is declared exactly **once** in a single declarative table — `induscode::launch::flags::flag_specs()`, **18 rows** filed under five render groups (Output / Model / Context / Tools / Meta). The tolerant parser (`induscode::launch::parser::read_invocation`) indexes that table and the `--help` renderer (`induscode::launch::usage::render_usage`) walks the same rows, so help text can never drift from what the parser accepts. A test pins the 18-row count and the canonical names. Each row is a `FlagSpec`:

```rust
pub struct FlagSpec {
    pub name: &'static str,            // canonical long spelling, e.g. "--model"
    pub aliases: &'static [&'static str],
    pub kind: FlagKind,                // Boolean | String | Number | List
    pub group: FlagGroup,              // Output | Model | Context | Tools | Meta
    pub describe: &'static str,
}
```

`FlagKind::List` is the agent's superset over the framework `indusagi::shell_app::invocation::FlagKind{Boolean,String,Number}` — it adds comma-split / repeat-accumulate behaviour for `--tools` and `--mcp`. Inline `--name=value` and separated `--name value` are equivalent; a value flag whose next token is itself a flag binds the empty string (read back as absent). Clustered short booleans (`-pi`) expand via `short_booleans()`.

| Flag | Alias | Kind | Group | Purpose |
|------|-------|------|-------|---------|
| `--print` | `-p` | Boolean | Output | Run a single request, print only the result, and exit. |
| `--json` | `--rpc` | Boolean | Output | Speak the headless line protocol for a driving parent process. |
| `--interactive` | `-i` | Boolean | Output | Force the interactive session even when a prompt is supplied. |
| `--model` | `-m` | String | Model | Select the model, provider-qualified or bare (e.g. `provider/name`). |
| `--fallback-model` | — | String | Model | Model to switch to mid-turn when the selected model is overloaded (HTTP 529). |
| `--account` | — | String | Model | Authenticate the run with a named stored credential account. |
| `--thinking` | — | String | Model | Set reasoning effort (one of: `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`). |
| `--list-models` | — | String | Model | List available models (optionally filtered by a substring) and exit. |
| `--cwd` | — | String | Context | Scope the run to a working directory (default: the current directory). |
| `--system` | — | String | Context | Replace the built-in system prompt with the given text. |
| `--append-system` | — | String | Context | Append extra text after the system prompt. |
| `--resume` | `-r` | Boolean | Context | Pick a previous session to resume. |
| `--continue` | `-c` | Boolean | Context | Continue the most recent session in this directory. |
| `--tools` | — | List | Tools | Allow only the named built-in tools (comma-separated or repeated). |
| `--no-tools` | — | Boolean | Tools | Disable every built-in tool for this run. |
| `--mcp` | — | List | Tools | Attach an external MCP server endpoint (comma-separated or repeated). |
| `--help` | `-h` | Boolean | Meta | Show this usage and exit. |
| `--version` | `-v` | Boolean | Meta | Show the version and exit. |

Notes on individual flags:

- `--thinking`'s description is built from `induscode::launch::contract::THINKING_EFFORTS`; the rungs (`ThinkingEffort::{Off, Minimal, Low, Medium, High, XHigh}`) come from the same source the validator uses. `ThinkingEffort` is a superset-compatible widening of `indusagi::llmgateway::ThinkingLevel` — it adds `Off`. An unrecognised value is silently ignored (treated as absent), not rejected.
- `--resume` / `--continue` are honoured by the interactive runner, resolving through the [Sessions](/rust-cli/subsystems/sessions) store. `--cwd` resolves the run's working directory, against which `@file` references resolve (`AttachmentOptions { cwd }`).
- `--tools` validates each name against the closed `induscode::launch::contract::ToolName` roster (`TOOL_NAMES`) via `ToolName::parse`; unrecognised names are dropped. The roster: `read`, `write`, `edit`, `bash`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`, `task`, `todo_read`, `todo_write`, `web_fetch`, `web_search`, `composio`.

```bash
indus --tools read,bash "list and read the config files"
indus --no-tools "just explain how this code works"
indus --mcp http://localhost:8931/sse "use the browser tools"
indus --mcp a --mcp b           # repetition accumulates: ["a", "b"]
indus --mcp "x,y,z"             # one token comma-splits: ["x", "y", "z"]
```

**Aliases and clusters.** The shared token index (`induscode::launch::flags::token_index()`) maps every canonical name **and** every alias to its owning row, so `-p`, `--rpc`, `-m`, `-r`, `-c`, `-h`, `-v` normalise to their canonical flag. Single-letter boolean aliases (`-p`, `-i`, `-r`, `-c`, `-h`, `-v`) populate `short_booleans()`, which drives `-pi`-style cluster expansion; a cluster with any unknown letter (`-px`) is kept whole as one extension flag rather than partially applied.

**Run modes.** Output flags resolve to one of three modes via `derive_mode`. The launch-level mode (`induscode::launch::contract::OutputMode`) selects the boot runner; it is the agent's own vocabulary, **not** the framework `indusagi::shell_app::invocation::Mode` (Print/Wire/Repl/Help/Version).

| Output mode | Triggered by | Behavior |
|-------------|--------------|----------|
| `OutputMode::Text` | default (no `-p` / `--json`, or with `-i`) | The interactive ratatui [console](/rust-cli/console/overview): live REPL, slash commands, dialogs. |
| `OutputMode::Json` | `-p` / `--print` (without `-i`) | One non-interactive request to settlement, then exit. |
| `OutputMode::Rpc` | `--json` / `--rpc` | The long-lived headless line protocol over stdin/stdout for a driving parent. |

Derivation precedence: `--json` / `--rpc` wins (→ `Rpc`); otherwise `--print` without `--interactive` → `Json`; otherwise `Text`. So `--json --print -i` is still `Rpc` because `--json` always wins.

```rust
fn derive_mode(flags: &HashMap<String, FlagValue>) -> OutputMode {
    if read_bool(flags, "json") { return OutputMode::Rpc; }
    if read_bool(flags, "print") && !read_bool(flags, "interactive") {
        return OutputMode::Json;
    }
    OutputMode::Text
}
```

Every real run is handed to `induscode::boot::boot_run`, which owns the launch arc (parse → materialise dirs → resolve resources → select runner → run → drain) and resolves the exit code. `boot_run` never calls `process::exit`; `main` adopts its `ExitCode` unchanged.

**`@file` attachments.** Any token of the form `@<path>` (before `--`, and longer than one char so a bare `@` is not consumed) is collected as a file attachment for the first message rather than a positional. The reader strips `@` and pushes the remainder into the file-reference channel:

```rust
if token.starts_with('@') && token.len() > 1 {
    state.file_refs.push(token[1..].to_string());
    i += 1;
    continue;
}
```

References are surfaced by `read_file_references` (a thin re-walk honouring `--`); the reader leaves `Invocation::attachments` as `None`, and `induscode::launch::attachments::gather_attachments` (over `AttachmentOptions { cwd }`) resolves each path relative to the working directory into an `Attachments` value:

```rust
pub struct Attachments {
    pub prose: String,        // each text file wrapped in a path-keyed block
    pub media: Vec<Block>,    // base64 image blocks: indusagi::llmgateway::Block::Image
}
```

Image files become `indusagi::llmgateway::Block::Image { media_type, data_base64 }` directly — no second image type. An invocation with no `@file` arguments has no `Attachments` (the field is `Option`).

```bash
indus "review this change" @src/main.rs @docs/diagram.png
indus -p "explain this config" @~/.config/app/settings.toml
```

**The `--` terminator.** A bare `--` stops option parsing; every subsequent token is a positional even if it starts with `-` or `@`. After `--`, `--model` is the prompt, `@x` is a positional, and `read_file_references` returns nothing for tokens past the terminator. The terminator itself is consumed and never appears in positionals.

```bash
indus -- "--this is a prompt, not a flag--"
```

**Meta short-circuits.** Three requests are handled in `route` before any session starts, derived from one tolerant parse (`read_invocation`):

```bash
indus --help                  # usage banner (generated from the 18-row flag table)
indus --version               # "indusagi <version>"
indus --list-models           # the full provider/model catalog
indus --list-models claude    # filtered by a case-insensitive substring
indus --list-models=opus      # inline substring filter
```

- `--help` / `-h` prints `render_usage()` (body, no trailing newline) plus the appended `Commands:` footer (`render_commands_section`) documenting the no-session subcommands. `auth --help` is intercepted *before* this short-circuit and reaches the framework auth command's own help.
- `--version` / `-v` prints `"{BRAND.app_name} {VERSION}"` — `app_name` is `"indusagi"`, `VERSION` is the compile-time `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`.
- `--list-models [filter]` is owned by the CLI. `list_models_filter` reads the optional substring (inline `--list-models=substr` or the next non-flag token); `induscode::launch::catalog::print_model_catalog` renders an aligned table over the live `indusagi/ai` facade catalog (the `mock` provider excluded). Columns: **Provider**, **Model**, **Context**, **Max Output**, **Thinking**, **Images**, sorted by provider then model id. Token counts format compactly (`128K`, `1M`, `1.5M`, `-` for unknown). No matches prints a single `No models match the given filter.` line.

**The `auth` subcommand.** When the first token is `auth`, the CLI owns the invocation and runs to an exit code **without touching boot** — intercepted before the global `--help` / `--version` short-circuit. The sub-verb is classified by `classify_auth_verb`:

```rust
enum AuthRoute {
    AgentLogout,   // auth logout  -> the agent's own signout over auth.json
    AgentStatus,   // auth status  -> the agent's reconciling vault reader
    Framework,     // auth <login|refresh|help|...> -> indusagi-shell-app's command
}
```

| Sub-verb | Route | Behavior |
|----------|-------|----------|
| `auth login <provider>` | Framework | Drives the framework PKCE browser flow (`indusagi::shell_app::auth_cli::run_auth_command`). A one-line tip pointing at `signin <provider>` is printed first, since shipped client ids are unconfigured sentinels in a default build. |
| `auth status [provider]` | AgentStatus | The agent's own `DiskAuthVault` reader, reconciling BOTH the framework single-record `{ providers: { … } }` shape AND the agent's nested `provider → account → record` shape, so an api-key sign-in is visible. Always exits `0`. |
| `auth refresh` | Framework | Refreshes a stored OAuth credential through the framework command. |
| `auth help` (and any unknown sub-verb, or a bare `auth`) | Framework | Renders auth-specific help / reports a usage error. |
| `auth logout [provider]` | AgentLogout | The framework command has no logout verb, so this is routed to the agent's `signout` path over the workspace `auth.json`. |

The framework route clamps the framework's `i32` exit code (0 ok, 2 usage, 1 failure) into the `ExitCode` byte. The framework auth command is reached through the declared `indusagi-shell-app` dependency, never a vendored copy.

**Credential subcommands.** When the first token is `signin` or `signout` (via `is_credential_verb`), the CLI runs the agent's own multi-account credential command and exits — boot explicitly does NOT route these.

```bash
indus signin anthropic                # store an Anthropic API key (interactive)
indus signin anthropic --oauth        # opt into the browser (OAuth) flow instead
indus signout anthropic               # remove a stored credential for a provider
```

| Verb | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `signin <provider>` | Validate and store an api key (or browser sign-in) for a provider / account. |
| `signout <provider>` | Remove a stored credential for a provider / account. |

*Default-to-api-key:* the shipped OAuth client ids are unconfigured sentinels, so `default_signin_to_api_key` appends `--method api-key` to a `signin` argv when the user has not already chosen a method (none of `--method`, `--oauth`, `--api-key`, `--apikey` present). An explicit `--method oauth` / `--oauth` is preserved; a `signout` argv is never altered.

```rust
fn default_signin_to_api_key(argv: &[String]) -> Vec<String> {
    if argv.first().map(String::as_str) != Some("signin") || argv_picks_method(argv) {
        return argv.to_vec();
    }
    let mut out = argv.to_vec();
    out.push("--method".to_string());
    out.push("api-key".to_string());
    out
}
```

The command runs over a disk-backed `DiskAuthVault` (workspace `auth.json`), the real OAuth seam (`CliOAuthSeam`, wired to registered browser providers), and a stdio console seam (`StdCredentialIo`). The api-key entry is read secret-safe: on a TTY the typed key's echo is muted via crossterm raw mode (restored even on error); a piped stdin falls through to a plain line read (testable). The cleartext is wrapped in a `SecretString` immediately and never logged or echoed.

OAuth-capable providers (browser sign-in), registered by `oauth::register_built_in_oauth_providers()` (an explicit prime, never at import time): `anthropic`, `openai-codex`, `github-copilot`.

Api-key providers — `induscode::launch::credentials::PROVIDER_DIRECTORY`, **14 `ProviderEntry` rows**:

| id | label | env_key |
|----|-------|---------|
| `anthropic` | Anthropic (Claude) | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| `openai` | OpenAI | `OPENAI_API_KEY` |
| `google` | Google Gemini | `GEMINI_API_KEY` |
| `xai` | xAI (Grok) | `XAI_API_KEY` |
| `groq` | Groq | `GROQ_API_KEY` |
| `cerebras` | Cerebras | `CEREBRAS_API_KEY` |
| `mistral` | Mistral | `MISTRAL_API_KEY` |
| `openrouter` | OpenRouter | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |
| `minimax` | MiniMax | `MINIMAX_API_KEY` |
| `kimi` | Kimi (Moonshot) | `MOONSHOT_API_KEY` |
| `sarvam` | Sarvam | `SARVAM_API_KEY` |
| `krutrim` | Krutrim | `KRUTRIM_API_KEY` |
| `nvidia` | NVIDIA | `NVIDIA_API_KEY` |
| `zai` | Z.ai | `ZAI_API_KEY` |

Every failure is a typed `induscode::launch::contract::CredentialFault` whose `kind` is one of `UnknownProvider`, `InvalidKey`, `InvalidAccount`, `NameCollision`, `NotFound`, `Vault`, `Aborted` — printed via `format_credential_fault` before a non-zero exit.

**Package subcommands.** When the first token is one of `install`, `remove`, `update`, `list`, `config` (via `induscode::launch::pickers::is_package_command`), the CLI runs the extension-package command and exits — boot does NOT route these. It persists through the two-tier `induscode::core::PreferenceStore` (global tier over the resolved workspace, project tier over the process cwd).

```bash
indus install npm:@scope/my-ext     # add a source (idempotent)
indus list                          # show configured sources
indus remove npm:@scope/my-ext      # drop a source
indus update                        # re-read and report the configured set
indus config                        # print settings paths + merged settings
```

The verb is parsed by `PackageCommand::from_token`:

| Subcommand | Argument | Purpose |
|------------|----------|---------|
| `install` | source | Add a package source to the configured set (idempotent under source matching). |
| `remove` | source | Remove a package source from the configured set. |
| `update` | — | Re-read and report the configured sources (resolution is lazy at startup). |
| `list` | — | Print the configured package sources. |
| `config` | — | Print the global / project settings file locations and the merged resolved settings. |

`run_package_command(argv, &mut store, &mut io) -> PackageResult` returns a `PackageResult` whose `code` is adopted (clamped to a byte); it never panics for an expected failure (a bad / missing argument is a printed error line plus a non-zero code). Sources are plain strings the addon loader understands — an `npm:` spec, a `git:` / `https:` repo, or a bare local path.

**Dispatch order.** `route(brand, rest)` consumes the command line in a fixed order, so a leading subcommand verb always wins over a prompt of the same spelling:

1. **`auth` subcommand** — `rest[0] == "auth"` → `run_auth_subcommand` → exit (before the global meta short-circuits so `auth --help` reaches the auth command).
2. **`--help` / `-h`** — render `render_usage()` + the `Commands:` footer → exit `0`.
3. **`--version` / `-v`** — print `"indusagi <version>"` → exit `0`.
4. **Unknown leading flag** — a leading `-…` token the flag table does not name → usage error, exit `2`.
5. **Credential verbs** — `rest[0] ∈ {signin, signout}` → `run_agent_credential` → exit.
6. **Package verbs** — `rest[0] ∈ {install, remove, update, list, config}` → `run_package` → exit.
7. **`--list-models [filter]`** — print the catalog → exit `0`.
8. **Everything else** — handed to `induscode::boot::boot_run`, which resolves the runner from the output mode and returns the `ExitCode`.

**Unknown flags and usage errors.** The parser is deliberately **total**: an unrecognised `--flag` is tolerated as a loose boolean switch in `Invocation::flags` (an inline `--flag=value` keeps its string value), never rejected — the extension-flag escape hatch. This contrasts with the framework's `indusagi::shell_app::invocation::tokenize_invocation`, which errors on unknown flags.

```rust
let inv = read_invocation(&["--frobnicate".to_string()]);
assert_eq!(inv.flags.get("frobnicate"), Some(&FlagValue::Bool(true)));
```

The exit-2 usage convention is enforced not by the parser but by `unknown_leading_flag` in `main.rs`: when the **leading** token starts with `-` (and is not the bare `-` stdin sentinel or the `--` terminator) yet names no flag in `token_index()`, the CLI reports it on stderr and exits `2`:

```
indus: unknown option '--bogus'
Try 'indus --help' for the available options.
```

A leading `signin` / `signout` / `auth` / package verb is a non-flag positional, so it is never an unknown-leading-flag error.

**Exit codes.**

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `0` (`ExitCode::SUCCESS`) | A clean run; `--help`, `--version`, `--list-models`, `auth status`; a successful `signin` / `signout`. |
| `1` (`ExitCode::FAILURE`) | A handled credential command that raised a typed `CredentialFault` (printed first), an unexpected failure during boot, or a package command that reported a bad / missing argument. |
| `2` (`EXIT_USAGE`) | A malformed invocation — an unknown **leading** flag (`unknown_leading_flag`). |

The `auth` framework route additionally clamps the framework command's own `i32` code (0 / 1 / 2) into the returned `ExitCode`.

**Parsing the command line in Rust.** The parser is part of the library surface for embedding and testing. `read_invocation` folds a sliced `argv` into a typed `Invocation`; `read_file_references` re-walks just the `@file` refs.

```rust
use induscode::launch::parser::{read_invocation, read_file_references};
use induscode::launch::contract::{OutputMode, ThinkingEffort};

let inv = read_invocation(&[
    "-p".into(), "--model".into(), "openai/gpt".into(), "hello".into(), "@notes.md".into(),
]);
assert_eq!(inv.mode, OutputMode::Json);
assert!(inv.print);
assert_eq!(inv.model.as_deref(), Some("openai/gpt"));
assert_eq!(inv.prompt.as_deref(), Some("hello"));

let refs = read_file_references(&["-p".into(), "hi".into(), "@notes.md".into()]);
assert_eq!(refs, vec!["notes.md".to_string()]);
```

The full launch type surface — `Invocation`, `OutputMode`, `ThinkingEffort`, `ToolName`, `FlagValue`, `FlagSpec` / `flag_specs()`, `CatalogFilter`, `Attachments`, `CredentialFault`, `ProviderEntry` — lives in `induscode::launch::{contract, flags, parser, usage, catalog, credentials}`.

#### Crate exports

`induscode` is a single merged Rust product crate: every former `induscode-*` library crate is now a `pub mod` inside `crates/induscode/src/lib.rs`, and the framework arrives as the one published `indusagi` umbrella crate.

**Crate root.** `crates/induscode/src/lib.rs` is the umbrella barrel. Unlike the framework crate it does **not** re-export a single `VERSION` at its own root — it only declares the **13** subsystem modules as `pub mod`. The version constant lives one layer down in `core::VERSION` (`env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`). The library is reached as `induscode::<module>`.

```rust
// crates/induscode/src/lib.rs
pub mod addons;
pub mod boot;
pub mod briefing;
pub mod channels;
pub mod conductor;
pub mod console;
pub mod core;
pub mod deck;
pub mod insight;
pub mod launch;
pub mod runtime_bridge;
pub mod transcript_export;
pub mod window_budget;
```

Module declaration order is the leaf-up dependency order of the former workspace DAG (not load-bearing in Rust). The framework is reached as `indusagi::<module>` (`core`, `runtime`, `llmgateway`, `tracing`, `capabilities`, `tui`, `interop`, `connectors_saas`, `swarm`, `smithy`, `tui_render`, `facade`, `shell_app`) from the single published `indusagi` crate.

**Module map** — each former `induscode-*` library crate is now a `pub mod`:

| Former crate | `pub mod` | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `induscode-core` | `core` | Brand, single-source `VERSION`, `BIN_NAMES`, `create_workspace`, `PreferenceStore`, plus the folded `kit` / `settings` / `sessions` leaves, `boot_contract`, and lineage `guardrails`. |
| `induscode-launch` | `launch` | The `FLAG_SPECS` flag table, the tolerant argv reader, `@file` attachments, the credential vault, OAuth flows, the model catalog, pickers, usage. |
| `induscode-boot` | `boot` | `boot_run(argv, BootIo) -> ExitCode`: stage pipeline, runner registry, resources, addon wiring, always-drained closables. |
| `induscode-conductor` | `conductor` | The session brain — wraps one `indusagi::runtime::Agent`, projects `RunEvent` into a stable `SessionSignal` stream, branchable transcript, retry/fallback, the `ModelInvoker` seam. |
| `induscode-window-budget` | `window_budget` | Token measurement, `is_over_budget` gating, slice planning, `create_condenser` → the conductor's `CondenseFn`, microcompact + rehydrate. |
| `induscode-deck` | `deck` | The capability deck over `indusagi::capabilities`: the `Card` trait, `CAPABILITY_CARDS`, profile provisioning, app-novel cards, the MCP bridge ledger. |
| `induscode-runtime-bridge` | `runtime_bridge` | Per-model routing — framework gateway vs. an external child runtime — as a `ModelInvoker`, plus the tracing-sink wiring. |
| `induscode-addons` | `addons` | The loadable-extension contract: hooks, tool interceptors, contributed commands/tools, the tiered TOML/subprocess loader, subagent crew. |
| `induscode-console` | `console` | The interactive ratatui surface: one immutable `ConsoleState`, a pure `console_reducer`, immediate-mode `view`, 14 overlays, `mount_console`. |
| `induscode-channels` | `channels` | The non-interactive surfaces: the one-shot text/NDJSON channel and the JSON-RPC 2.0 link server over the NDJSON framer. |
| `induscode-briefing` | `briefing` | The budget-aware system-prompt assembler: section composer, `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` context docs, `$arg` macros, `SKILL.md` cards. |
| `induscode-transcript-export` | `transcript_export` | The publish-time HTML/Markdown builder: the SGR machine, WCAG `theme_bridge`, page template, `publish`. |
| `induscode-insight` | `insight` | The observability plane over `indusagi::tracing`: probe/signal vocab, NDJSON serialize/replay, an agent scrubber, a fan-out channel and collector sink. |

Per-subsystem `mod.rs` barrels follow a consistent shape: a frozen `contract` module owns the type seam, behavior modules sit beside it, and the crate-root `pub use` re-exports the contract vocabulary plus headline behavior functions.

**core** — the universal leaf, analogue of `indusagi::core`. Carries no subsystem behavior; ships load-bearing primitives, four sub-1k-LOC TS subsystems folded as nested modules (`kit`, `settings`, `sessions`, `workspace`), the boot *contract* types breaking the `boot` ↔ `launch`/`deck` cycle (`boot_contract`), and lineage `guardrails`.

```rust
// crates/induscode/src/core/mod.rs
pub mod boot_contract;
pub mod brand;
pub mod guardrails;
pub mod kit;
pub mod sessions;
pub mod settings;
pub mod workspace;
```

Key crate-root re-exports:

| Symbol | Kind | Source | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `VERSION` | `pub const &str` | `workspace.rs` | The single-source product version, `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`. |
| `BRAND` / `Brand` / `BIN_NAMES` | const / struct / `[&str; 2]` | `brand.rs` | The brand record (`app_name: "indusagi"`, `profile_dir_name: ".indusagi"`, `bin_names: ["indus", "indusagi"]`, `env_prefix: "INDUSAGI"`) and bin-name table; `BIN_NAMES[0]` is the default process title. |
| `create_workspace` / `Workspace` / `WorkspaceOverrides` / `Packaging` | fn / struct / struct / enum | `workspace.rs` | Pure path computation of the profile root (dirs materialised later by boot). |
| `PreferenceStore` / `Preferences` / `PreferenceLocations` / `default_preferences` | struct / struct / struct / fn | `settings/` | The 23-key, project-over-global-over-default preference store; writes land in the project tier only. |
| `PermissionMode` / `PermissionSettings` / `DeliveryMode` / `EscapeAction` | enum / struct / enum / enum | `settings/contract.rs` | The settings vocabulary the conductor re-exports. |
| `SavedSession` / `BranchNode` / `PriorTurn` | struct | `sessions/` | The session catalog/navigator value types over the framework `SessionStore` DAG. |
| `quote_arg` / `needs_quoting` / `build_shell_command` | fn | `kit/shell_quote.rs` | POSIX shell-argument quoting + injection-safe command assembly. |
| `sniff_image_format` / `resolve_asset_name` / `media_type_for` / `ImageFormat` | fn / fn / fn / enum | `kit/image.rs` | PNG/JPEG magic-byte sniffing + `{token}` asset-name renderer. |
| `plan_provision` / `build_download_request` / `ReleaseLookup` / `ToolDescriptor` | fn / fn / trait / struct | `kit/tool_fetch.rs` | The managed-binary provisioner (fd / rg); network injected via `ReleaseLookup`. |
| `read_clipboard_image` / `open_in_external_editor` / `host_platform_tag` | fn | `kit/` | Clipboard capture, `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR` round-trip, Node-style platform tag. |
| `FORBIDDEN_MARKERS` / `READ_BEFORE_EDIT_MESSAGE` | const | `guardrails.rs` | Lineage / clean-room markers and the read-before-edit gate message. |

The folded leaves each carry nested `pub mod` trees: `kit::{clipboard_image, external_editor, image, shell_quote, tool_fetch}`, `settings::{contract, store}`, `sessions::{contract, library}`. The `sessions` library (`SessionLibrary`, `SessionLibraryOptions`) builds over `indusagi::runtime::store::SessionStore` / `SessionGraph`.
